One or two sentences on my personal connection. One line noting the supporting case study is included separately. Exclude: sales language, next-steps sequence, pricing, call to action.
16. Writing style
Australian English throughout. Prioritise, organise, recognised, minimise, behaviour.
The voice should be: warm · confident · practical · thoughtful · experienced · direct · strategic · implementation-focused · heart-led · realistic.

It should not sound like: an academic paper · a software proposal · a generic consultant · a motivational speech · a job application · a corporate strategy deck · an AI-generated template.

Use first-person language where appropriate:
I would begin by… · I would prioritise this because… · Before choosing a platform… · My first objective would be… · I would consider this phase complete when… · I would treat this as a preliminary hypothesis… · I would involve the team by… · This would remain human-led because… · This recommendation would depend on… · I would deliberately defer… · The goal is not to add more software… · By the end of six months, the business should have…

Avoid excessive repetition of "I would." Vary the sentence structure naturally.

Other useful constructions: The roadmap would be refined after discovery · The initial priority would be… · Where the current process is stable… · Before introducing automation… · The team would be involved through… · I would consider the workflow adopted when… · This would reduce dependency by… · Another Operations Manager would be able to continue by… · The education initiative would initially be treated as a pilot… · The goal is to build the foundation without overwhelming the clinical practice.
Phrases to avoid
unlock potential · leverage synergies · transformative growth · seamless integration · seamless execution · cutting-edge solutions · revolutionise the business · optimise everything · future-proof the company · drive innovation · drive growth · maximise efficiency
Also avoid streamline operations unless the exact workflow and result are explained · operational excellence unless the surrounding statement explains what it means · scalable solutions unless the specific system and capacity issue are explained.
If a sentence needs one of these, explain the mechanism instead. "Streamline the intake process" becomes "remove the follow-up emails currently needed to complete an intake form."
Other formatting rules
Short paragraphs, two to four sentences.
One table only in the client-facing roadmap, plus one small assumptions table.
No emoji. No decorative dividers.
Every recommendation must tie to a business goal, an operational problem, a risk or a growth opportunity. If it cannot be traced to one of those, cut it.
Do not make Zoe feel criticised. Frame gaps as opportunities to build stronger foundations.
Position me as a strategic implementation partner, not merely an adviser.
Show that recommendations will be adjusted after further discovery and access to the company's data.
17. Checklist before you send it back to me
 4–6 pages. Count it.
 Zoe's four requested areas are all directly and visibly answered
 Clear milestones, timeframes, deliverables, priorities, sequencing, explanations and outcomes
 Australian English throughout
 Zero invented facts — every specific claim traces to this brief
 Every assumption is visibly labelled, with what changes if it is wrong
 No pricing, no rate, no retainer, no investment section
 No named platform recommendation
 AI treated as one tool with boundaries, not the centre of the strategy
 No phrases from the avoid list (search for each one)
 Maximum two tables in the client-facing document
 "I would" does not open more than a handful of sentences
 No guaranteed outcomes
 Nothing claims experience I have not confirmed (re-read Section 13)
 Privacy and professional obligations stated as needing validation, never asserted
 Zoe would not feel criticised reading any part of it
 Personal connection appears once, in the closing, in one or two sentences
 Reference to the separately included case study appears once
 Appendix delivered as a separate file

title: Domain Transfer
description:
Transferring divineorigines.com from Canva to Squarespace


Before You Start — Important Notes
The domain is currently doing two things:
Hosting/registered through Canva (expiring July 10, 2026 — renew first!)
Connected to Google Workspace for email (info@divineorigines.com)
Transferring the domain will NOT break your email automatically — but the DNS records that point to Google Workspace need to be carefully carried over to Squarespace's DNS settings before you finalize the transfer. If this step is missed, email will go down.


Step 1 — Renew the Domain in Canva First
Before doing anything else, renew divineorigines.com in Canva before July 10, 2026.
Log in to Canva → go to Brand Kit or Domain Settings
Find divineorigines.com and confirm the renewal
Make sure payment is up to date
Do not start the transfer until the domain is renewed. Transferring while close to expiry is risky and can cause the domain to lapse mid-transfer.


Step 2 — Get Your Google Workspace DNS Records Ready
Before unlocking the domain, note down your current DNS records from Canva. You'll need to re-enter these in Squarespace after the transfer.
Log in to Canva's domain settings and look for the following records tied to Google Workspace:
MX Records — these route your email (there will be several Google MX records)
TXT Records — includes your Google verification record and SPF record (e.g. v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all)
CNAME Records — if you have any Google Workspace-specific ones (e.g. for Google Meet, Calendar, etc.)
Screenshot or copy all of these before proceeding. You will need to re-add them in Squarespace DNS settings after the transfer completes.


Step 3 — Prepare the Domain for Transfer in Canva
Log in to Canva → go to Domain Settings for divineorigines.com
Disable WHOIS Privacy / Domain Privacy (if enabled) — some registrars block transfers when privacy is on
Unlock the domain — look for a setting called "Domain Lock" or "Transfer Lock" and turn it off
Request the EPP/Authorization Code (also called a transfer code or auth code) — Canva should provide this in your domain settings or via support
Make sure the email address on your Canva account is accessible — you'll receive a transfer confirmation email there


Step 4 — Initiate the Transfer in Squarespace
Log in to Squarespace → go to Domains → Transfer a Domain
Enter divineorigines.com
Enter the EPP/Authorization Code from Step 3
Squarespace will check eligibility — the domain must not have been registered or previously transferred within the last 60 days
Follow the prompts to complete the transfer request
Squarespace will charge the transfer fee (usually includes a 1-year renewal)


Step 5 — Approve the Transfer
Check the email on your Canva account for a transfer approval email
Approve the transfer — if you don't approve it manually, it will auto-approve after 5–7 days
The transfer typically takes 5–7 days to complete


Step 6 — Re-add Google Workspace DNS Records in Squarespace
⚠️ This is the most critical step for keeping email working.
Once the transfer completes and Squarespace becomes your registrar:
Go to Squarespace → Domains → click divineorigines.com → DNS Settings
Re-add all the DNS records you saved in Step 2:
All MX Records (Google's mail servers)
SPF TXT Record
Google verification TXT Record
Any other CNAME Records
Save all records
DNS propagation can take 24–48 hours — email may be temporarily interrupted during this window
Tip: To minimize email downtime, add the DNS records to Squarespace before the transfer fully completes if Squarespace allows you to manage DNS early. Check with Squarespace support on whether this is possible.


Step 7 — Verify Everything is Working
After 24–48 hours:
Send a test email to and from info@divineorigines.com
Check Google Workspace Admin (admin.google.com) → Domains → confirm the domain status shows as verified and active
If Google Workspace shows a DNS issue, go back to Squarespace DNS settings and double-check the MX and TXT records match exactly what Google requires


Summary Timeline

Step Action When
Now Renew domain in Canva Before July 10, 2026
Before transfer Screenshot all DNS records from Canva Before Step 3
When ready Unlock domain + get EPP code from Canva When ready to transfer
Same day Initiate transfer in Squarespace Immediately after Step 3
5–7 days Transfer completes After approval
Immediately after Re-add Google Workspace DNS records in Squarespace Critical — do not skip
24–48 hours later Verify email is working After DNS propagation


Key Things to Remember
✅ Renew in Canva before transferring — never transfer close to expiry
✅ Save all DNS records before unlocking the domain
✅ Re-add Google Workspace MX and TXT records in Squarespace immediately after transfer
⚠️ Expect up to 48 hours of potential email interruption during DNS propagation — plan accordingly and give your team a heads up

KEY METRICS / HEADLINE NUMBERS

ABOUT THE ACCOUNT
• 1-2 sentences on what this business does (we'll anonymize if needed)

CHALLENGES BEFORE GIM
• What was messy, missing, or broken before we started supporting this account?
• Scattered data? No SOPs? No automations? Manual processes?

SOLUTIONS WE IMPLEMENTED
• What systems, SOPs, automations, or workflows have you built or set up?
• Group these into categories if you can (e.g. "Backend System Build", "SOP Framework", "Automation Infrastructure")

RESULTS
• Tie back to the metrics above — what specifically improved and by how much?

CLIENT FEEDBACK
• Any quote, message, or shoutout from the client we can use
• Please also save a SCREENSHOT of the actual message/conversation as proof — not just the text

ALSO PLEASE INCLUDE:
Screenshots — ClickUp setups, SOPs, automations, trackers, dashboards (anything visual that supports the above)

HOW TO SUBMIT:

2. Fill it in for your assigned account and save it in the same Drive folder (include screenshots — client feedback and supporting visuals — either pasted into the doc or saved alongside it in the same folder)
3. Once done, comment the Drive link on this ClickUp task

The more specific the numbers, the stronger the case study — so dig into whatever trackers or reports you have. Thank you all for taking the time on this!

description:
Source: automation audit by Divine, 14 Nov 2026 (live checks of GHL Automation and Payments, WordPress Cohortly, WPCode and WooCommerce). Full register and how to audit: SOP JV-OPS-12. title: JV-OPS-15 SOP: Manual fallback, onboarding guide email
description:
JV-OPS-15 · Manual fallback: onboarding guide email (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Snippet #3718 sends each new student one onboarding guide email with their set-password link. Use this when a student says they never got it.

When: A student can't find the email, or the access check (JV-OPS-07) shows they never set a password.
Owner: Ops Assistant
Approver: None
Tools: WordPress Users, WPCode, Gmail or WhatsApp, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Know what is automatic: cohort students get the cohort guide when they are added to a batch; free sign-ups get the free guide 10 minutes after they register. Each guide is sent once per person. The GHL text message step is not set up.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-15-step01-wpcode-list.jpg (WPCode: #3718 on, old #3658 off)
Ask the student to check spam and promotions, then search their email for "Juvibolt".
Still missing: WordPress > Users, find the student, and send a password reset link. (Password reset emails are not affected by the snippet.) Never send a password in chat.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-15-step03-wp-users-instructor.jpg (WordPress > Users)
Send them the steps by email or WhatsApp: set your password, go to the dashboard, open My batches, click Connect Discord, then open the Discord app with the same login.
If no student is getting the guide, the snippet may be off or broken. Rollback (from the snippet notes): turn #3718 off and #3658 on, then tell the portal person.
Log it on ClickUp and re-run the access check (JV-OPS-07).

Done when

Student has set a password and logged in
ClickUp logged

Escalate

More than one student missing the email: tell the Operations Manager and Radz the same day.

title: JV-OPS-14 SOP: Manual fallback, class notices and reminders
description:
JV-OPS-14 · Manual fallback: class notices and reminders (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Cohortly announces each class, sends reminders and posts replay and material notices through Juvi Bot. When that fails, tell the cohort by hand.

When: 24 hours before every class, and after every replay or file upload.
Owner: Ops Assistant
Approver: Operations Manager approves any text posted by hand
Tools: Discord, Cohortly Settings and Classes, Gmail, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Know what is automatic: Cohortly posts each class in the batch Discord channel and emails reminders; Juvi Bot posts "Recording available" or "New material is up". The GHL reminder workflow has no trigger, so it sends nothing.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-14-step01-ghl-reminders-no-logs.jpg (GHL class reminder workflow: no logs, never ran)
24 hours before class, check the batch Discord channel has the class post with the date and the "Open the class" join link.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-14-step02-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Juvi Bot class post and notices)
Check Cohortly > Settings > Notification queue: Retrying 0 and Dead 0.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-14-step03-cohortly-health.jpg (Notification queue)
Check the class itself in Cohortly > Classes: the class exists, has the right time and shows Announced: Posted.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-14-step04-class-row-status.jpg (Class row: Recording and Announced status)
If the post is missing or a job is dead, post the reminder by hand in the batch channel (JV-OPS-04): class title, date and time (New York), and "join from your student dashboard; the join button opens 15 minutes before class". Never paste the Meet link.
If students also missed the email, email the batch from the Juvibolt Gmail with every address in BCC.
Tell the portal person which job failed so they can read its error, and log it on ClickUp.

Done when

Every student told before class
Failed job reported
ClickUp logged

Escalate

Under 2 hours to class and no notice out: post by hand straight away and tell the Operations Manager.

title: JV-OPS-13 SOP: Manual fallback, new paid student (payment to portal access)
description:
JV-OPS-13 · Manual fallback: new paid student (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

What to do by hand when a payment comes in and the automations don't finish the job. Today the GHL to portal bridge isn't built, so portal access is always done this way.

When: Every morning, and whenever Aaron or GHL reports a new payment.
Owner: Ops Assistant (Radz for now; Ops Manager as backup)
Approver: Operations Manager
Tools: GHL Payments and Contacts, WooCommerce Orders, Cohortly Advisor desk, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Check for new payments: GHL > Payments > Subscriptions and Transactions (enroll page), and WordPress > WooCommerce > Orders (website checkout).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-13-step01-ghl-subscriptions.jpg (GHL Payments > Subscriptions)
For each new payment, open the workflow that should have run and check its Execution logs. Plan payments use "INSTALLMENT PLAN - First Payment"; full payments use "Paid Enrollment - [program]" (there is none for RMF yet).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-13-step02-ghl-installment-builder.jpg (INSTALLMENT PLAN: tag, opportunity, welcome email, alerts)
If the workflow didn't run, do its steps by hand in GHL: add the tag ("Installment Plan" or "Student Enrolled"), create the opportunity, send the welcome or confirmation email, and tell the Operations Manager and Aaron.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-13-step03-ghl-aws-builder.jpg (What a Paid Enrollment workflow does)
Website orders: add the contact in GHL by hand with the tags student-enrolled and the cohort tag (J4 is not sending them).
Give portal access: WordPress > Cohortly > Advisor desk > Add lead (name, email, course). Search first so you don't make a duplicate.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-13-step05-advisor-desk.jpg (Cohortly > Advisor desk)
Open the lead. Under "Enrol without payment" write the reason (for example "Paid in GHL, RMF plan, 9 Nov") and click Enrol now. It creates the account if there is none. Scholarships use the same box, or a quote with price 0 placed in the batch.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-13-step06-advisor-enrol.jpg (Enrol without payment, with the reason recorded)
Check the student is on the right batch (Cohortly > Batches roster count) and that the onboarding guide email went out (JV-OPS-15).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-13-step07-batches.jpg (Roster count on the batch)
Finish with the access check: portal login and Discord (JV-OPS-07). Target: access within 48 hours of payment and before the first class.
Log it on ClickUp: payment, workflow result, what you did by hand, time.

Done when

Payment confirmed
GHL tag, opportunity and email done (by workflow or by hand)
Student enrolled in the right batch
JV-OPS-07 checks passed

Escalate

Payment unclear, refund, or a student who paid but isn't in GHL: tell the Operations Manager and Aaron the same day.

Notes

Never type card or bank details anywhere. Payments are only checked, never taken, in this SOP.
To confirm with Radz: that "Enrol without payment" places the student in the right batch on its own (the quote route has a "Place them in" field).

title: JV-OPS-12 SOP: Audit Juvibolt's automations (register 14 Nov)
description:
JV-OPS-12 · Audit Juvibolt's automations (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Check every automation still works, find the ones that stopped, and switch to the manual fallback the same day. First audit done 14 Nov 2026; the register is below. Fixes are tracked in the "Automation audit (14 Nov): fixes" task.

When: Every Monday, and after any change to GHL, WordPress or Cohortly.
Owner: Operations Manager
Approver: Operations Manager; fixes go to Radz
Tools: GHL (Automation, Payments), WordPress (Cohortly, WPCode, WooCommerce), Discord, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Audit register (14 Nov 2026)

# Automation Status What we found Fix (owner)
1 Class reminders (GHL) Not working Published but has no trigger, so it has never run (no execution logs). The subject is fixed to "Class 1". Impact: No GHL reminder emails. Cohortly's own class notices still go out. Unpublish it, or add a trigger and a subject that changes per class. (Radz)
2 RMF pay-in-full confirmation (GHL) Missing Paid Enrollment workflows exist for AWS, Azure, GCP and SOC only. RMF plan payments are covered by INSTALLMENT PLAN; a full RMF payment has no workflow. Impact: A full RMF payment gets no tag, confirmation email or team alert. Build "Paid Enrollment - RMF" from the AWS one. (Radz)
3 New student alerts (GHL) Needs change Internal notifications go to Muhammad Azam (for example "Ops alert - new installment plan" and "New AWS Paid Student - Muhammad"). Impact: Payment alerts go to someone who is leaving. Switch the recipient to the Operations Manager or Radz in every Paid Enrollment and INSTALLMENT PLAN workflow. (Radz)
4 Paid Enrollment AWS, Azure, GCP, SOC (GHL) Untested Only one run ever: an AWS test on 27 Oct. Azure, GCP and SOC have never run. The AWS trigger is named "Order Submitted - Private RMF" (copied name, AWS filters). Impact: We don't know they work for a real order. One test order per product (T5.10 G6); rename the AWS trigger. (Radz)
5 INSTALLMENT PLAN - First Payment (GHL) Working Ran for the deposit-plan student on 9 Nov; every step executed (tag, opportunity, welcome email, 2 alerts). None (see 3 for the alert recipient).
6 Test subscription (GHL Payments) Check A subscription named "test test" for USD 1,000 has been Active since 7 Nov (Stripe). Impact: A test may charge a card or skew reports. Confirm with Aaron and Radz; cancel it if it is a test. (Aaron / Radz)
7 Website orders to GHL (J4) Missing J4 is closed, but there is no webhook in WooCommerce and no inbound-webhook workflow in GHL. Impact: Website checkout orders don't reach GHL (last website order: 6 Nov, pending). Rebuild J4 or retire the website checkout. (Radz)
8 GHL to portal bridge (T5.10 A1) Missing A GHL payment does not create the portal account or add the student to a batch. Impact: Every paying student needs access set up by hand. Build A1 with Abdul. Until then: JV-OPS-13. (Radz / Abdul)
9 Onboarding guide email (WordPress) Working, part off Active since 14 Nov: one guide email per student when added to a batch (free sign-ups after 10 minutes). Its GHL SMS hook is blank and there is no SMS workflow in GHL. Impact: No "check your email" text message. Paste the GHL inbound webhook URL and build the SMS workflow, or drop the SMS idea. (Radz)
10 Class, replay and material notices (Cohortly) Working Notification queue: 109 sent, 0 retrying, 0 dead. Discord bot and Google Meet connected. Snippet #3715 splits recording and file notices. None.
11 Cold Outreach v1 (GHL) Part working 110 contacts went through the 5 emails (finished 2 Nov). "#2 Update Master Sheet status" was Skipped for each contact. Impact: The outreach master sheet was not updated. Fix or remove the sheet step before the next sequence. (Radz)
Steps

GHL > Automation > Workflows. For each workflow check: Published, Total enrolled and Active enrolled make sense, and Last updated. A workflow with 0 enrolled for weeks is either unused or broken.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step01-ghl-workflows-list.jpg (GHL Workflows list: status and enrolment counts)
Open each workflow. A workflow must have a trigger. "Add new trigger" with nothing beside it means the workflow can never run.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step02-ghl-reminders-no-trigger.jpg (Red flag: Published, but no trigger)
Check the trigger filters match the product, funnel and page it is meant for, and that the name matches what it does.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step03-ghl-aws-trigger.jpg (Trigger filters: product, funnel, page)
Open Execution logs (last 7 days). Every step should say Executed. Look for Failed or Skipped, and for "No logs found" on a workflow that should have run.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step04-ghl-installment-logs.jpg (Healthy run: every step Executed)
Skipped steps mean part of the automation is not doing its job.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step05-ghl-outreach-logs.jpg (Problem: "Update Master Sheet status" Skipped)
Open every Internal notification step and check who receives it. Alerts must go to current team members only.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step06-ghl-alert-recipient.jpg (Alert still going to a person who is leaving)
GHL > Payments > Subscriptions: look for test subscriptions, Incomplete or Past due plans.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step07-ghl-subscriptions.jpg (A test subscription still Active)
WordPress > Cohortly > Settings: Notification queue must show Retrying 0 and Dead 0. A dead job keeps the error that stopped it.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step08-cohortly-health.jpg (Cohortly notification queue)
WordPress > Code Snippets (WPCode): the right snippets are Active (#3718 onboarding guide, #3715 Cohortly notices). Old #3658 stays off.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step09-wpcode-list.jpg (WPCode snippets and their on or off switch)
WordPress > WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Webhooks: any webhook GHL relies on must be listed and Active.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-12-step10-woo-webhooks.jpg (No webhooks: website orders don't reach GHL)
Write the results in the audit register (this task, or a new dated audit task), raise a fix for each problem with an owner, and use the matching manual fallback SOP until it is fixed.

Done when

Every automation in the register checked
Each problem has a fix task and owner
Manual fallback running for anything broken

Escalate

Anything that touches payments or student access and is broken: tell the Operations Manager and Radz the same day, and start the manual fallback.

Notes

Never change or delete a workflow during an audit. Note it, and let the owner fix it.
Not checked on 14 Nov: the Azure, GCP and SOC workflow insides (only the list), Stripe (no access), ManyChat.

title: Radz: end-to-end test of the onboarding email + SMS with test students (free, paid, added by team)
description:
After the GHL workflow and the consent fields are done, test with team email addresses and phones (not real students, and not the real cohort batch: use a test batch so the roster and Discord stay clean):

Free: register through the sign-up form. Expect ONE email ("your free course is ready") about 10 minutes later, then ONE SMS.
Paid: test order (website checkout). Expect the WooCommerce order receipt only, then the cohort guide when the student is added to a batch, then ONE SMS. No WooCommerce "New account" email and no Tutor welcome/enrolled email (switched off 14 Nov).
Added by team: create the user in WordPress, add to a batch. Expect ONE cohort guide and ONE SMS.
Check FluentSMTP's email log for each, and that the set-password link and the video link work.
Password reset: request one and confirm it's a normal reset email (not the old "class is tonight" welcome).
Post the results as a comment here and remove the test users.

title: Radz: phone number + SMS consent at sign-up and checkout, and check the A2P campaign covers onboarding texts
description:
The onboarding SMS can only go to students who gave a phone number and agreed to texts.

Free sign-up form (Tutor registration): add a phone field (saved to user meta phone) and an unticked consent checkbox, for example "I agree to receive text messages from Juvibolt Cybertech about my account and classes. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out." Store the consent so GHL can read it.
Checkout (WooCommerce and the GHL enroll page): confirm the phone field is there and add the same consent checkbox.
A2P: our registered campaign is MARKETING (T8.15). Check whether onboarding and class texts fit it; if not, register an account-notification campaign.
Tell Divine what wording you used before it goes live.

title: Radz: GHL workflow "New student onboarding SMS" (webhook from WordPress, then text "check your email")
description:
WordPress is ready to tell GHL every time a new student's onboarding guide email goes out (WPCode snippet #3718 "Juvibolt: one student onboarding guide email + GHL SMS hook (GIM, 14 Nov)"). It covers paid, added-by-team and free students, so there is one trigger for all three.

What WordPress sends (JSON POST): first_name, last_name, email, phone (WooCommerce billing phone, or user meta "phone"), student_type ("cohort" or "free"), batch_id, event = "onboarding_guide_sent".

Please build in GHL:
Workflow with trigger Inbound Webhook. Copy its URL.
Paste the URL into snippet #3718, in the line define( 'JUVI_GHL_ONBOARDING_WEBHOOK', '' );, and click Update. Nothing is sent to GHL until this is filled.
Create or update the contact by email, map the fields, add tags onboarding-guide-sent and student-cohort or student-free.
If the contact has a phone number and SMS consent: send the SMS (text approved by Divine, 14 Nov):
Hi {{contact.first_name}}, welcome to Juvibolt Cybertech! We've just emailed your onboarding guide with your login and a 1-min setup video. Check your inbox (and spam). Reply STOP to opt out.
No phone or no consent: skip the SMS (no email from GHL, WordPress already sent it).
Make sure this doesn't double up with any existing GHL welcome or onboarding workflow (for example the J4 WooCommerce order workflow). Only one SMS per student.

Related: T8.15 (SMS set-up), J4 (WooCommerce to GHL), J8 (A2P).

title: JV-OPS-11 SOP: Daily log and ClickUp task check
description:
JV-OPS-11 · Daily log and ClickUp task check (v1.1, 14 Nov 2026)

Keep ClickUp a true picture of the work: every message that matters gets logged, every task status matches reality.

When: Every working day, end of day.
Owner: Operations Manager
Approver: Operations Manager
Tools: WhatsApp groups, Discord, email, Fathom, ClickUp, Knowledge Hub

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step. v1.1 adds ClickUp screenshots and replaces the v1.0 PDF.

Steps

Read the day's messages: Aaron's chat, Juvibolt x GIM, the Instructors group, My Team, the Discord channels (#tech-help and batch channels), email and any Fathom calls.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-11-step01-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Check the batch channel and #tech-help)
Log what matters in the Knowledge Hub Slack and WhatsApp log (page 07): date, who, what. Leave out codes, sign-in numbers, phone numbers, logins and contractor payment messages.
Every piece of work gets a ClickUp task, including work already done. Name done work "(done date)" and add "Logged for the record" with a checklist of what was done.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-11-step03-clickup-logged-task.jpg (Example of done work logged for the record)
Go through open tasks. Close a task only with evidence, and add a comment saying what the evidence is (for example "Rana confirmed 'Yes I see it now', 7:34 AM").
List the tasks you could not confirm and ask their owners the next day.
New decisions go in the decision log (page 05); new questions in page 06.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-11-step06-clickup-decision-log.jpg (Knowledge Hub decision log)

Done when

Today's log written
Statuses match the evidence
Unconfirmed tasks listed with owners

Escalate

A student problem or payment issue appears in any chat: act on it the same day (JV-OPS-07) and tell the Operations Manager.

title: JV-OPS-10 SOP: Turn a call into ClickUp tasks and decisions
description:
JV-OPS-10 · Turn a call into ClickUp tasks and decisions (v1.1, 14 Nov 2026)

After any call with Aaron, the team or a contractor, capture what was agreed so nothing lives only in someone's head.

When: Within the same day as the call.
Owner: Operations Manager
Approver: Operations Manager
Tools: Fathom, ClickUp, Knowledge Hub

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step. v1.1 adds Fathom and ClickUp screenshots and replaces the v1.0 PDF.

Steps

Open the call in Fathom. Read the summary, then check key points in the transcript.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-10-step01-fathom-summary.jpg (Fathom: Summary and Transcript tabs)
Create one parent task in ClickUp: "T# Actions from <call name> (date)". In the description add the source (Fathom link) and "What came out of the call" as short bullets.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-10-step02-clickup-call-task.jpg (Example: T8, the 11 Nov call, with its subtasks)
Add one subtask per action, each with an owner and a due date.
Add every decision to the Knowledge Hub decision log (page 05) as a row: Date, Decision, Who, Source.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-10-step04-clickup-decision-log.jpg (Knowledge Hub page 05: Date, Decision, Who, Source)
Add open questions to page 06, and new facts about the client to the client profile.
Never copy login details, codes or passwords from the call or chat.
Send the team a short summary of what was agreed and who owns what.

Done when

Parent task with source link
Every action has an owner and date
Decisions logged

Escalate

Two sources disagree (call vs chat): mark it "to confirm" and ask the person who decided.

Notes

Work in ClickUp under your own account, never under someone else's.

title: JV-OPS-09 SOP: Weekly report to Aaron
description:
JV-OPS-09 · Weekly report to Aaron (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

One weekly page for Aaron: where things stand, what he needs to decide, and what is next. First sent for 2 to 8 Nov.

When: Once a week, before the weekly call with Aaron.
Owner: Operations Manager
Approver: Operations Manager
Tools: ClickUp, WhatsApp groups, Fathom, Knowledge Hub decision log

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Pull the week's facts: ClickUp tasks closed and still open, the WhatsApp groups (Aaron, Juvibolt x GIM, Instructors, My Team), Fathom calls and the decision log.
Write the report in five parts: Ready status (for example "ready for Class 1"), Asks for Aaron (numbered), Done this week, His decisions this week, Next week.
Keep the asks to a short list he can answer with yes or no. Add a default: what happens if there is no answer in 72 hours.
Save the report as a page and as a file (HTML or PDF). Send it to Aaron on WhatsApp with the file attached (JV-OPS-08).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-09-step04-whatsapp-aaron.jpg (Send to Aaron's direct chat with the file)
Prepare a short call script for the weekly call from the same asks.
After the call: turn the outcomes into ClickUp tasks with owners and dates (JV-OPS-10), and log the report as done in ClickUp.

Done when

Report sent with the file
Call held and outcomes in ClickUp

Escalate

A decision is still open after 72 hours: apply the stated default and tell Aaron.

title: JV-OPS-08 SOP: Send an update to Aaron on WhatsApp
description:
JV-OPS-08 · Send an update to Aaron on WhatsApp (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Keep Aaron (CEO) informed with short, factual updates he can read in a minute.

When: After a milestone (first class, a new student set up, a decision needed), and as agreed in the weekly rhythm.
Owner: Operations Manager
Approver: Operations Manager (Divine for now)
Tools: ClickUp, WhatsApp, Knowledge Hub

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Gather the facts from ClickUp and today's work. Only include what is verified; mark anything not confirmed as "to confirm".
Draft it in this order: greeting and headline, ✅ what is done, ⏳ what is next, then one thing you need from him (a question or decision).
Get the draft approved.
Open WhatsApp > Aaron Ofosu (the direct chat, not a group, unless the group should see it). Paste the approved text and send. If you send a page link, also send the HTML or PDF file in case the link does not open.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-08-step04-whatsapp-aaron.jpg (Aaron's direct chat, messages blurred)
Check it shows as sent.
Log the time and summary as a comment on the ClickUp task and in the Knowledge Hub Slack and WhatsApp log.

Message template

Milestone update

Hi Aaron! Quick update on Class 1 ✅
Rana ran the intro this morning. [what happened, 2 lines]
Since then:
✅ [done item]
✅ [done item]
⏳ Next: [next steps]
One thing to check with you: [question]

Done when

Sent to the right chat
Logged in ClickUp

Escalate

Aaron asks for something outside the plan: add it as a ClickUp task and tell the Operations Manager.

Notes

Never put passwords, codes, logins or payment details in updates or logs.

title: JV-OPS-07 SOP: Check a new student's portal and Discord access
description:
JV-OPS-07 · Check a new student's portal and Discord access (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Confirm a new student can get into everything they paid for, then tell Aaron. Built from the check done for a deposit-plan student on 10 Nov.

When: At payment or approved place, again after 24 hours and 48 hours, and always before their first class.
Owner: Student Success (Ops Assistant until named)
Approver: None
Tools: WordPress Users, Cohortly Batches, Discord, WhatsApp, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Confirm the student's place: paid (payment plan or full) or an approved scholarship place on Aaron's list.
WordPress > Users: search by email. The account exists and the student has logged in.
Cohortly > Batches: the student is on the right batch (the roster count goes up).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-07-step03-batches.jpg (Roster count on the batch)
Discord: the student is in the server and can see the batch channel. Students join by: set password, go to the dashboard, My batches, click Connect Discord, then open the Discord app with the same login.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-07-step04-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Batch channel students should see)
If anything is missing, fix it or hand it to the portal person the same day, and message the student with the next step.
Send Aaron a short update (JV-OPS-08).
Log it in ClickUp as a checklist: paid, portal account, logged in, on the batch, in Discord, Aaron updated.

Done when

Access within 48 hours of payment and before the first class
ClickUp checklist complete

Escalate

Not set up 24 hours before class, or payment unclear: tell the Operations Manager and Aaron.

title: JV-OPS-06 SOP: Give an instructor portal access
description:
JV-OPS-06 · Give an instructor portal access (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Set up a new instructor so they can teach, see their batch and students, and add replays. Built from setting up Rana (9 to 10 Nov). Full checklist history: Knowledge Hub page 10.

When: Before an instructor's first class.
Owner: Ops Assistant (portal); Operations Manager (final check)
Approver: Aaron confirms the instructor and course
Tools: WordPress Users, Cohortly Team, Tutor LMS, Google Calendar, Fathom, Discord, WhatsApp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Collect from Aaron or the instructor: full name, login email, course(s), timezone, job title, short bio and photo, their slides or materials, and the named backup instructor.
WordPress > Users: create the user (or find them). Roles: Subscriber + Tutor Instructor. Never Administrator. Send a password reset link; never send a password in chat.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-06-step02-wp-users-instructor.jpg (Users filtered to Tutor Instructor: check the Roles column)
New users are created from Users > Add User. Tick the Tutor Instructor role.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-06-step03-wp-add-user.jpg (Users > Add User: roles at the bottom)
Cohortly > Team > Add a person: Tier Teacher, duties Teach, Manage recordings and See batches (everything else off). Under Courses they teach, add their course.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-06-step04-cohortly-team.jpg (Cohortly > Team: Teacher with three duties)
Check the batch exists with the right dates, capacity and Discord channel (Cohortly > Batches).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-06-step05-batches.jpg (Cohortly > Batches)
Ask the instructor to log out and back in so the instructor dashboard shows, then confirm they see their course and students.
Recording: the instructor installs the Fathom Chrome extension. When Fathom asks to join, whoever is signed in to the Juvibolt account approves it. The instructor picks "Audio and Video". Test on a short Meet first.
Discord: give the Instructor role (not Admin). Check they can see #instructors-only and the batch channel.
Add them to the Juvibolt cybertech Instructors WhatsApp group and tell them who to contact: the portal person for portal issues, the Operations Manager for operations.
Log each step with the date and who did it on the instructor's ClickUp task.

Done when

Logs in and sees the instructor dashboard, course and students
Has the calendar invite for the next class
Fathom tested
In Discord with the Instructor role
In the Instructors WhatsApp group

Escalate

Dashboard shows 0 students after the role change: ask them to refresh, then tell the portal person.

Notes

Do not turn on Tutor's Reports add-on to show students. It mixes free sign-ups with the cohort.

title: JV-OPS-05 SOP: When a class can't go ahead (tell students, keep the record)
description:
JV-OPS-05 · When a class can't go ahead: tell students and keep the record (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

What to do when the instructor cannot teach a scheduled class.

When: As soon as an instructor says they cannot teach.
Owner: Ops Assistant
Approver: Operations Manager; Aaron decides on a cover teacher
Tools: WhatsApp (Instructors group, Aaron), Cohortly, Discord, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Confirm with the instructor and ask Aaron right away whether he or a backup can teach instead. (11 Nov: Aaron said he would teach if the instructor could not.)
If the class is cancelled, find it in Cohortly > Classes. Use Cancel, not Delete: Cohortly says cancelling keeps the record and tells the cohort, while deleting removes the session and its attendance.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-05-step02-class-row-status.jpg (Classes list: Cancel keeps the record)
Check what the cohort received. If they need more (what to do instead, when the next class is), post the approved "Class not going ahead" message in the batch channel (JV-OPS-04).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-05-step03-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Batch channel)
Tell the Instructors WhatsApp group and Aaron what happened and what was sent.
Agree the make-up plan (catch-up session or the next class) and update the class plan.
Log it in ClickUp: reason, who decided, what was sent and when, and the make-up plan.

Done when

Students told before the class time
Class cancelled (not deleted) in Cohortly
Make-up plan agreed and logged

Escalate

No cover and under 2 hours to class: message Aaron directly and post the notice as soon as it is approved.

title: JV-OPS-04 SOP: Post an announcement in the cohort Discord channel
description:
JV-OPS-04 · Post an announcement in the cohort Discord channel (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Send the cohort a short update in their batch channel: new material, a class change, the schedule, a reminder.

When: When something changes for the cohort and Cohortly has not already told them.
Owner: Ops Assistant
Approver: Operations Manager approves the text before it is posted
Tools: Discord (Juvibolt CyberTech server), ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Check first whether Juvi Bot already posted it. Cohortly tells the batch about new classes, replays and lectures by itself, so do not post twice.
Draft the message: a friendly hello, what changed, where to find it, and the next step. Keep it short. Never paste a Google Meet link: students join through the portal link, which opens 15 minutes before class.
Send the draft to the Operations Manager and wait for approval.
Open Discord > Juvibolt CyberTech > Batch Channels > the batch channel (for example #november-2026-rmf). Type the approved text in the message box. To attach a file, click + > Upload a File.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-04-step04-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Batch channel, Juvi Bot notices, and the message box)
Send, then check the post shows correctly (text, attachment, emojis).
Log it on the ClickUp task: channel, time and the text posted.

Message templates

New material

Hi everyone! 👋 Here's the RMF Training Curriculum for this cohort: 8 modules that follow the NIST Risk Management Framework, from Introduction through RMF Steps 0 to 6 (Prepare, Categorize, Select, Implement, Assess, Authorize, Monitor). You'll also find it at the top of the RMF course in your student dashboard. See you in class!

Class not going ahead

Hi everyone! 👋 Quick update: tonight's class won't be going ahead, as our instructor has an emergency. In the meantime, I highly recommend going through the RMF Training Curriculum (posted above, and at the top of the RMF course in your student dashboard) and preparing your questions for the next class. We'll share the next class details here soon. Thank you for understanding!

Done when

Text approved
Posted in the right batch channel
ClickUp logged

Escalate

A student replies with a problem (cannot log in, missing access): follow JV-OPS-07 and tell the Operations Manager.

title: JV-OPS-03 SOP: Make a Juvibolt-branded PDF document
description:
JV-OPS-03 · Make a Juvibolt-branded PDF document (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Turn a document from an instructor or the team into a Juvibolt-branded PDF before it goes to students or Aaron.

When: Any student-facing document, and any document going to Aaron for review.
Owner: Ops Assistant or Marketing
Approver: Operations Manager; Aaron for new course content
Tools: Source file, Juvibolt template, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Get the source file and confirm who owns the content (instructor or Aaron) and who it is for.
Use the Juvibolt look: black pages, white Juvibolt logo top left, a short label top right, a pill tag with a teal dot, a big title with one word in Juvibolt blue, numbered cards, and a soft blue and violet glow. Font: Plus Jakarta Sans. The RMF Student Glossary is the reference.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-03-step02-brand-reference.jpg (Reference: RMF Student Glossary cover)
Keep the content exactly as written. Only formatting changes are allowed. Replace long dashes with words (for example "K to L", "U to Z").
Check the finished PDF against the original: every section and entry is there (the glossary has 141 entries), page breaks are clean, links work.
Name the file "Juvibolt-<Topic>.pdf" and save it in the shared Juvibolt folder.
New course content (for example slides) goes to Aaron for review before students see it.
Log it on the ClickUp task with the file attached, what changed, and what is next (for example "upload to portal").

Done when

Content matches the source
Branded file saved and attached to ClickUp
Reviewer named on the task

Escalate

Content looks wrong or out of date: ask the instructor or Aaron. Do not edit their content yourself.

Brand colours: Black #04060B, Juvibolt blue #038EFA, light blue #42A4FF, teal #0EC9AC, body text #C0D0E0, violet glow. Font: Plus Jakarta Sans.

title: JV-OPS-02 SOP: Add a PDF or resource to a course and notify the cohort
description:
JV-OPS-02 · Add a PDF or resource and notify the cohort (v1.0, 14 Nov 2026)

Put a document (curriculum, slides, glossary, worksheet) in the course as its own lesson, and let the batch know through Cohortly.

When: Whenever an instructor or Aaron approves new material for a cohort.
Owner: Ops Assistant
Approver: Operations Manager (content and placement)
Tools: WordPress Media, Cohortly, Tutor Course Builder, Discord, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step.

Steps

Confirm the file is approved and which batch and course it is for. If it is not yet in the Juvibolt style, brand it first (JV-OPS-03).
Upload the PDF in WordPress: Media > Add Media File > Select Files. Open the file and copy its URL.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step02-media-upload.jpg (WordPress > Media > Add Media File)
Go to Cohortly > Classes > New class > Recorded lecture. Pick the batch and course, add the title (for example "RMF Student Glossary (PDF)") and a one-line description.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step03-lecture-form-top.jpg (New class > Recorded lecture)
Set Where is the recording = External link and paste the PDF's URL. ("Embed code" does not save, tested 14 Nov.) Set Who it is for and Who may join, then click Publish lecture. This creates the lesson and tells the batch by Discord and email.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step04-lecture-form-bottom.jpg (Use External link for a PDF)
Open Tutor LMS > Courses > the course > Curriculum and click the pencil on the new lesson.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step05-course-builder.jpg (Hover a lesson to see edit, duplicate and delete)
In the lesson: remove the video link, write a short description, add an "Open or download" link to the PDF, embed the PDF in the content, and add the file under Exercise Files. Remove "Recording:" from the title if it is there. Save, then drag the lesson into place and click Update.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step06-lesson-editor.jpg (Lesson editor: content, link and Exercise Files)
Open the live lesson page and check the PDF shows and can be downloaded.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step07-lesson-pdf.jpg (The PDF shows on the lesson page)
Check the batch Discord channel for Juvi Bot's post about the new material.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-02-step08-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Juvi Bot posts the new material in the batch channel)
Log it on the ClickUp task: file name, lesson name, position in the module, and that the batch was notified.

Done when

Lesson visible in the right module, PDF opens and downloads
Batch notified by Cohortly
ClickUp task logged

Escalate

Wrong course or batch, or a file that should not be public: unpublish and tell the Operations Manager.

Notes

Keep Tutor's own "New Lesson Published" email OFF. It emails everyone enrolled in the course, including free self-paced sign-ups.
Material added straight in Tutor (not through Cohortly) is not announced. Use the Cohortly route so the batch hears about it.

title: JV-OPS-01 SOP: Publish a class replay to the student portal
description:
JV-OPS-01 · Publish a class replay to the student portal (v1.1, 14 Nov 2026)

Put the recording of a live class on the student portal so the cohort can watch it, and tell them it is up.

When: After every live class. Target: replay live within 24 hours of the class.
Owner: Ops Assistant
Approver: Operations Manager (only for any extra Discord text)
Tools: Fathom, WordPress Media, Cohortly, Tutor Course Builder, Google Drive, Discord, ClickUp

PDF version: attached to this task (Juvibolt-branded). Screenshots are attached too, named by step. v1.1 adds the Fathom screenshot for step 1 and replaces the v1.0 PDF.

Steps

Download the class recording from Fathom, signed in to the account that recorded the class. Rename it the same way each time, for example "Juvibolt RMF_ Day 2 - Nov 11 2026.mp4".
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step01-fathom-summary.jpg (The class recording in Fathom)
In WordPress go to Media > Add Media File > Select Files and upload the MP4. Files up to 1 GB are fine here (Class 2 was 279 MB).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step02-media-upload.jpg (WordPress > Media > Add Media File)
If the class already exists in Cohortly: go to Cohortly > Classes, search for the class and click Edit. In the Recording panel open Manage this recording, set Where is the recording = Media library, pick the MP4, set Where in the course, then click Publish recording.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step03-class-edit.jpg (Cohortly > Classes > Edit: the Recording panel shows Attached once a replay is on the class)
If the class has no Cohortly entry: go to Cohortly > Classes > New class and choose Recorded lecture. Pick the batch and course, and title it "Topic: Class N".
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step04-lecture-form-top.jpg (New class > Recorded lecture)
Set Lecture date (the class date and time), Where is the recording = Media library, choose the file, Where in the course, Who it is for = This batch, Who may join = Paying students only (scholarship students and mentors in the batch keep access). Click Publish lecture.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step05-lecture-form-bottom.jpg (The fields to fill, then Publish lecture)
Check for the confirmation: "Lecture published. It is in the course now and the cohort has been told." If clicking Publish seems to do nothing, reload the page, choose the file again and publish again (this happened once on Class 1).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step06-class-row-status.jpg (In the Classes list the class shows Recording: Published and Announced: Posted)
Cohortly places a new lecture at the top of the course. Open Tutor LMS > Courses > the course > Curriculum and drag the "Recording: ..." lesson to sit after the previous recording. Click Update.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step07-course-builder.jpg (Tutor Course Builder > Curriculum: drag lessons by the handle)
Open the live lesson page as a check: the lesson shows its duration in the side menu and the video plays.
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step08-lesson-video.jpg (Live lesson page: duration shows and the video plays)
Check the batch Discord channel: Juvi Bot posts "Recording available" automatically. No extra post is needed unless the Operations Manager asks for one (then follow JV-OPS-04).
Screenshot: JV-OPS-01-step09-discord-batch-channel.jpg (Juvi Bot's automatic notice in the batch channel)
Save a copy in Google Drive: Bootcamp Master > Class Recordings > [Course] > [Cohort folder], named "Class NN - YYYY-MM-DD - Topic.mp4" (for example "Class 02 - 2026-11-11 - Introduction to RMF.mp4").
Log it in ClickUp as a task named "Class N replay published (done date)": the Fathom link, the Media ID, the lesson name, where it sits in the course and the playback check.

Done when

Lesson shows on the course with its duration and plays
Cohort notified (Cohortly confirmation and Juvi Bot post)
Copy saved in the Drive cohort folder
ClickUp task logged

Escalate

No recording 24 hours after class: Cohortly raises a task for the instructor; tell the Operations Manager. Upload fails or the video will not play: tell the Operations Manager the same day. If notices don't go out, use JV-OPS-14.

Notes

Recordings belong to Juvibolt: the replay lives on the portal and a copy goes in the Juvibolt Drive.
The RMF course is also the free self-paced course, so check Who may join before you publish.

title: New student onboarding: one welcome email with the video, plus an SMS "check your email" (paid and free) | Juvibolt Cybertech
description:
Divine, 14 Nov: when someone pays or is added manually, the onboarding email should include the welcome video, and an SMS should go to every new student (paid or free) telling them to check their email for the onboarding guide.

What happens today (checked 14 Nov):
Paid through website checkout: WooCommerce order emails and "New account", Tutor "Welcome Email After Registration" and "Course Enrolled" (both on), Cohortly's batch email when added to a batch.

Free sign-ups: Tutor's welcome email.
None of these include the welcome video.
The branded email is out of date: it says Cohort 1 starts "Monday, Nov 9", "First Live Class (Tonight)", includes the Meet link, and the same template is used for password reset emails.

SMS:

title: RMF Student Glossary: Juvibolt-branded PDF (done 14 Nov), then share on the portal and Discord | Juvibolt Cybertech
description:
14 Nov 2026: Rana's glossary ("Cybersecurity_RMF_Glossary_for_Students.pdf", 10 pages, in Divine's Downloads) rebuilt in the Juvibolt style, same look as the RMF Training Curriculum PDF (black background, Plus Jakarta Sans, Juvibolt logo and blues).

title: Class 2 replay (11 Nov) published on the portal (done 14 Nov) | Juvibolt Cybertech
description:

Cohortly > Classes > New class > Recorded lecture: batch November 2026 RMF, course RMF, title "Introduction to RMF and the NIST Standards: Class 2", lecture date 11 Nov 2026 7 PM New York, source Media library, paying students only (batch members incl. scholarships and mentors keep access), Publish lecture. Cohortly: "Lecture published. It is in the course now and the cohort has been told." (12 students notified.)

title: Send Proposed Process Improvements
description:
After completing the Client Process Map and the first 1 to 2 weeks of onboarding, the Project Owner prepares and sends a short list of proposed process improvements to the client. This shows GIM's value beyond task execution — we don't just do the work, we actively look for ways to make the business run better.
Required Actions:
Review the Client Process Map (Before GIM) and onboarding notes
Identify the top 3 to 5 areas where the client's current process can be improved — bottlenecks, manual steps, gaps, or inefficiencies
For each improvement, include: what the issue is, what GIM proposes to do about it, and what the expected outcome is
Keep it simple and easy to understand — this is a client-facing document, not a technical spec
Share with Head of Operations for review before sending to the client
Send to the client with a short note explaining that this is part of GIM's standard onboarding process
Deliverables:
Proposed process improvements document prepared and reviewed by Head of Strategy and Automations and Head of Operations
Document sent to the client within the first 2 weeks of onboarding
Completion Standard: Client receives a clear, actionable list of proposed improvements with enough context to understand the value. Head of Operations has reviewed and approved before it is sent.

title: Create Operations Implementation Timeline
description:
Create Operations Implementation Timeline
The Head of Strategy & Automations creates an internal operations implementation timeline that maps out exactly what GIM will build, set up, and deliver in the first 90 days. This is the internal version of the onboarding plan — more detailed and used by the team to stay on track.
Required Actions:
Break down the 30-60-90 Day Plan into weekly milestones and tasks for the first 1–2 months
From Month 3 onwards, milestones can be mapped at a higher level without weekly breakdowns
Assign each task to the relevant team member (Project Owner, Project Assistant, Specialist)
Add all tasks and milestones to ClickUp with due dates
Flag any dependencies or tasks that require client input or access first
Share the timeline with RA Malinao for review before execution begins
Deliverables:
Internal implementation timeline created in ClickUp
Weekly milestones for Months 1–2, high-level milestones for Month 3
All tasks assigned with due dates and owners
Reviewed and approved by RA Malinao
Completion Standard:
 The team has a clear execution plan for the first 90 days — week-by-week for the first two months, and milestone-based for Month 3 — with no gaps in ownership or timeline.

title: Create Client Process Map (Before GIM)
description:
Before building any new systems, the Project Owner documents how the client's business currently operates — what the process looks like before GIM stepped in. This serves as the baseline reference for all future improvements and is part of the case study foundation.
Required Actions:
Interview the client or review the Kickoff Call notes to understand current workflows
Map out the end-to-end process for each active client account — how work moves from intake to delivery
Note where the bottlenecks, gaps, and manual steps are
Document what tools are currently being used and how
Save the process map in the client's Google Drive folder
Deliverables:
Completed process map saved in Google Drive
Key bottlenecks and gaps identified and noted
Completion Standard:
The process map clearly shows how the client's business operated before GIM, with enough detail that the team can reference it when building new systems and tracking improvement over time.

 How to Create a Client's Process Map
 
Our implementation service utilizes the Whiteboard ClickUp feature to create process maps. Make sure that you are familiar with how to create and use this feature by going to this link: 

Create a Whiteboard on the Client's folder and name it using the format "<Name of Client> - Process Map".
Reflect the processes of the client through a process map by utilizing the shapes and arrows on the Whiteboard.

Message 1: to Gelton and Nebs (copy as is)
Hi Gelton and Nebs! Here are the answers to your questions from Friday's SOP briefing, in 3 parts. All times are Houston time.

*Part 1 of 3*

*1. Gelton, your hours*
Thank you for staying late to get cleans assigned. Your shift ends at 5 PM, with every lead answered or handed to Nebs. From then, Nebs covers leads, bookings and the Unstaffed list (SOP 7.0 Steps 1, 3 and 4). If you stay on past 5 PM, tell me.

*2. Daily checklist*
SOP 7.0 Step 3 is Gelton's daily checklist and Step 4 is Nebs's. Start every shift with SOP 5.0 Step 2. A checklist for each of you is planned in ClickUp by Fri Oct 16.

*3. End-of-shift posts*
Gelton posts by 5 PM, Nebs at 8 PM. List what is still open, not the jobs you booked: leads waiting, anything promised, and for Nebs, tomorrow's confirmations still Pending. Job dates only, no names or numbers (SOP 7.0 Steps 3 and 4).

*4. Thumbtack new-lead alerts*
You were right. The alerts are not working yet, and the business email only shows customer replies. We are checking why. Until we say they work, check Thumbtack Messages yourselves at the start of and all through your shift (SOP 5.0 Escalation). From 5 PM, Nebs checks alone.

*5. Weekends*
Gelton, your paid shifts start Sat Oct 3: Saturday 10 AM to 12 PM and Sunday 7 to 9 PM (SOP 5.0 Step 6). Until then, Matthew covers weekends (SOP 3.0 Step 5).
We are asking Matthew about weekends with nothing booked, from Oct 3. I will walk you through the weekend steps before Oct 3.

*Part 2 of 3*

*6. Profit margin and the 35%*
No change. The floor, the lowest margin you may quote, is still 40%, and 50% is the goal (SOP 1.0 Step 2). Offer the normal price first, and never lower a price the customer has accepted.
35% is allowed in two cases only, first visit only (SOP 1.0 Step 3):
a) a customer who would otherwise book another company
b) a customer signing up for a regular plan, which means a recurring plan: every 2 weeks, monthly, or weekly if they ask (SOP 6.0 Step 3)
A customer who picks a standard clean because a deep clean costs too much is not case b. That is a normal quote at 40% or above, unless they would otherwise walk (case a).
Plan visits after the first are at the plan price, nothing lower.
Gelton, fair point: 35% is an exception, and Matthew sees each one on Friday (SOP 1.0 Step 5).

*7. The cap after the $49*
The 35% stop is only for those two cases. For everyone else, the floor stays 40%.
Caps: about $50 off a deep clean or a move in or out, and $35 off a standard, counted from the price you quoted after the $49. Stop at the 35% price or the cap, whichever comes first. SOP 1.0 Step 3 has an example.

*8. Rates and the Profit Margin tab*
Build every quote in Progressive 83, as before. Only its Rate column (Contractors) is out of date, so take the cleaner's standard or deep rate from the cleaner pay sheet (SOP 1.0 Step 2).
Still being set: the pay sheet and the Profit Margin tab. For now, Nebs asks Gelton for a rate, and you log one Profit Margin row per quote (SOP 1.0 Step 5). We will tell you when both are ready.

*9. Condition surcharge*
It is real and new: Matthew turned it on in Progressive 83. Standard cleans only. The booking page asks how the home is kept:
Normally kept: no extra.
Needs extra attention: add 25%.
Hasn't been cleaned in a long time: add 50%.
The price and the booked time both go up by that percentage, so the cleaner gets the extra time. On a regular plan, only the first visit (SOP 1.0 Step 1).
Rule for now on a phone or Thumbtack quote: ask the customer the same question and add that percentage.

*10. Carpets*
Mostly right. 3 or more carpets: charge for half, rounded up, so 3 or 4 are charged as 2, and 5 as 3. Only if the job still clears 40% after shampoo and machine rental (SOP 1.0 Steps 1 and 2). Tell me the same day a carpet job is booked.

*11. The deposit and the 6 PM check*
Card first: Request Payment Info emails the customer the card link. No card: a deposit of 50% of the job price by Zelle or Venmo, part of the price, not on top (SOP 3.0 Step 2). A card OR the deposit must be in by 6 PM the day before.
After the clean, a job with a deposit is charged only the balance: the job price minus the deposit. Example: a $300 job with a $150 deposit is charged $150. The Charge box fills in the full price, so change it to the balance before you press Charge. A deposit Matthew has not confirmed yet: do not charge, tell me. Only the deposit in and no card on file: tell me, as now (SOP 3.0 Step 6).
Nebs, the 6 PM check is yours every weekday, with the confirmations, not only when Gelton is out (SOP 3.0 Step 5). No card and no deposit: call, then tell me that evening. Never cancel alone.
Still being set: a day Nebs is out. For now, tell me early so I can set the cover.

*12. Zelle and Venmo*
Only Matthew can see them. When a customer says they sent a deposit, post the job date and amount in the team group, no names. He confirms there each evening. Mark it paid only once he confirms, or I find it in his list (SOP 3.0 Step 2 item 4, Step 6 and FAQ). Never press Charge on a job the customer says was paid in full by Zelle or Venmo.
Rule for now: not confirmed by your 6 PM check? List it as open in your end-of-shift post and tell me. Do not cancel.
We are asking Matthew about payment alerts to an inbox you can see.

*13. The card hold and the 5 PM charge*
Both are off in Progressive 83: the 48-hour card hold, and the automatic charge at 5 PM ('Charge when the job is done, at 5pm'). So a card is charged only when someone presses Charge. Both stay off until I tell you.
The SOPs say the hold is on in a few places: the Start here tools table, and in SOP 3.0 the Step 2 customer script, Step 4, the Held row in Step 6 and the FAQ. It is off, so skip those lines. Do not mention a hold to customers. Just say 'You pay after the clean.' In the morning check, look for a card on file or a confirmed deposit.
Never change a charge or hold setting. On a row that already shows Charged, the Charge button stays live with the full price filled in. Do not press it again without asking me first, even for overtime or an extra. If a Completed row may already have been charged, or a row shows Held, tell me before you press Charge. A customer charged twice: tell me at once.

*Part 3 of 3*

*14. Backup cleaner*
How the backup is picked and noted is still being set.
The SOPs say every job has a backup, picked before the day: the nearest free cleaner who fits the rate rule, with the distance checked on Google Maps (SOP 3.0 Step 3, SOP 4.0 Step 4).
Our rule for now:
a) Do not press Assign for the backup ahead of time. It books and emails that cleaner. Just know who you would call.
b) If the backup gets their own clean that day, pick another. None found: tell me the same day. Never cancel alone.

*15. Few cleaners*
Thank you for raising this. We are asking Matthew about hiring more. Meanwhile, work the Unstaffed list early (SOP 3.0 Step 3). No cleaner free, or none that fits the rate rule: tell me the same day (SOP 7.0 Step 3, SOP 3.0 Escalation).

*16. Refunds and cleaner pay*
Still being set. Never cut a cleaner's pay yourself, after a refund or on a complaint with no photos. Tell me, and I take it to Matthew (SOP 2.0 Steps 2 and 5). Until the complaint log is set, send complaint details to me the same day.

*17. HAR*
Nebs, you told us Matthew asked you to stop HAR. SOP 7.0 Step 4 item 5 still has one last follow-up to the interested realtors. Rule for now: hold it, and make no realtor calls until he confirms. We are asking him. Social media stays paused.

*Three corrections from the call*
1. Gelton, sign customer texts as Hilton, as you do today, never as Gelton (SOP 5.0 Step 3).
2. The day 10 and day 21 emails stay OFF until Matthew has checked the wording.
3. Gas money is $15, only for a drive of more than about 45 minutes (SOP 4.0 Step 4).

*Reading order for the SOPs*
Use the copy I posted in the team group until Matthew's ClickUp, planned by Fri Oct 16, with a walkthrough then.
Both of you: the intro ('Start here'), then SOP 7.0. Then our suggested order:
Gelton: 5.0, 1.0, 3.0, 4.0 (you back up confirmations and run them in your weekend shifts), 2.0, and the Deep Clean Tracker part of 6.0.
Nebs: 4.0, 5.0, 6.0, then 1.0, 3.0 and 2.0 for after 5 PM.

Hi Matthew, three questions from Gelton and Nebs that only you can answer, from Friday's SOP briefing.

1. More cleaners: Gelton says few active cleaners are left. From his last interview list, only a few were hired, because others did not reply or took full-time jobs. Assigning cleans is slow, and he sometimes stays until about 7 PM Houston time to finish. A backup cleaner for every job needs more cleaners too. Do you want him to start hiring more now?

b) Charging: the 48-hour hold and the 5 PM automatic charge are both off in Progressive 83 today, and the VAs never change a charge or hold setting. The hold question is in the payment rules message. e) Gelton tells me when he stays on past 5 PM.

Why: the plan call (Fri Sept 25) set no place for leads that come by phone, text or voicemail. For now SOPs v2 says: log them in the Lead Tracker, as Gelton does today. The dashboard's leads-by-channel view and the lead-tracker build both wait on this.

Done when: one place is agreed, Jedy tells both VAs, and the "Still being set" line in SOP 5.0 closes in the next SOP revision.

title: Fix each cleaner's standard and deep rate with Gelton
description:
Why: on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Matthew said the cleaner rates in Progressive 83 are not up to date. Only one cleaner's rate is right, some cleaners have a different rate for deep cleans, and he doubts Progressive 83 can hold two rates per cleaner. Quotes use the cleaner pay sheet instead.

Steps
With Gelton, confirm which cleaners are still active.
Write each one's standard rate and deep rate in the cleaner pay sheet.
Fix Progressive 83 where it can hold the rate.

Done when: every active cleaner has a standard and a deep rate in the pay sheet.

title: Get Matthew's answers on cleaner pay after a refund or a complaint with no photos
description:
Why: the plan call (Fri Sept 25) left these cleaner-pay questions open. Until they are answered, SOPs v2 says a VA tells Jedy and never decides them.

Ask Matthew in one message
Does money back cut the cleaner's pay?
Is a cleaner still paid on a complaint with no photos?
Who is paid when a different cleaner does the re-clean?
Re-cleans on regular cleans.
A cleaner asking for more than her rate.
Extras (for example inside the oven), a cancelled job, the carpet machine, booked versus real hours.
The make-good after a cleaner no-show.

Done when: his answers are in SOP 2.0 and the cleaner pay sheet.

title: Set up the complaint log and show Matthew
description:
Why: on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Matthew backed logging every complaint the same day ("having a log will be very important") but no sheet was named. We decide where it lives and show him. Until then, SOPs v2 says: log it the same day and send it to Jedy.

Steps
Pick the place (a new sheet for now, ClickUp later).
Columns: date, job date, problem, photos (yes or no), next step and time, outcome, money back.
Show Matthew, then Jedy shares it with both VAs.

Done when: both VAs log complaints in it.

title: Find a second lead source with Matthew
description:
Why: the 90-day plan Matthew approved on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) adds a second lead source in Days 61 to 90 (for example referrals or Google Local Services), so InVogue relies less on Thumbtack.

Steps: Divine raises it at the Day 30 review (Fri Oct 16) and agrees the options with Matthew.

Done when: Matthew has picked a second lead source to try.

title: Set up the WhatsApp group for Matthew, Divine and Jedy
description:
Why: on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Divine offered a separate WhatsApp group for Matthew, Divine and Jedy, and Matthew said "that'd be perfect". From Mon Sept 28 Jedy is the daytime path, and anything for Matthew goes through Divine.

Done when: the group exists with the three of them, before Mon Sept 28.

title: Fix the gaps and issue SOPs v3 after the first week
description:
Why: a SOP counts as done only after the VA who uses it has followed it once. After the first week on SOPs v2, fix what broke and add what v2 is missing.

Add or fix
Each "Still being set" line that has closed (complaint log, backup cleaner, cover when a VA is out, the cleaner pay sheet, lead logging).
The rule for a job that turns out bigger (SOP 1.0 Step 4), tested on a real job.
An arrival check before the job window opens (SOP 4.0).
Who handles a double booking.
Hiring, and pricing an extra that is not on the booking page (SOP 7.0 Step 2).
A missed weekend shift (from Sat Oct 3).
Whatever the daily checks and the VAs' questions show.

title: Ask Matthew about a daytime operations assistant
description:
Why: on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Divine floated an operations assistant in Matthew's day, trained by us, for emergencies or what Gelton cannot do. Matthew did not answer. He also said he will not promise to answer urgent messages during his day.

Steps: bring it back at the Day 30 review (Fri Oct 16), with the count of urgent escalations to Jedy from the first weeks.

Done when: Matthew has said yes or no.

title: Set cover for the days a VA is out
description:
Why: the plan call (Fri Sept 25) left two cover gaps open. SOPs v2 carries a rule for now ("Still being set"), and Jedy settles the final one.

Settle
Nebs out: who makes the 6 PM check for tomorrow's jobs. Matthew said "That's me probably". For now Nebs tells Jedy early and Jedy sets the cover.
Gelton out: how and by when he tells us, and who sends the 5 PM cleaner pay list that day. For now he tells Jedy as soon as he knows and Jedy arranges the pay list.
A missed weekend shift (from Sat Oct 3): not covered by SOPs v2 yet.

Done when: each case has a named person, and the "Still being set" lines in SOPs 4.0 and 7.0 close in the next SOP revision.

title: Run the VAs' daily checklists (recurring, Jedy checks)
description:
Owner: Jedy · Due: Fri Oct 16

Why: From Mon Sept 28 the VAs run their day from SOP 7.0 Steps 3 and 4. Jedy's check is kept short on purpose: read the posts, spot-check what hurts most if missed, and follow up only on what is off. About 10 minutes a day, not a second job.

The routine (each weekday, after the end-of-shift posts):
Read Gelton's 5 PM post and Nebs's 8 PM post.
Spot-check three things (the nested checks list them per VA):
every lead answered or handed over;
tomorrow's jobs confirmed on both sides;
tomorrow's jobs each have a card on file or a confirmed deposit.
Anything off: ask the VA in the team group the same evening. A miss goes in the Friday report by job date only.

Careful:
The 48-hour card hold is off (86d4bx1z1), though SOPs v2 says on. Look for a card on file or a confirmed deposit.
Thumbtack new-lead alerts do not reach the Quo numbers. The VAs check Thumbtack Messages all shift.
Jedy out: Divine runs the checks.
Add a check only when a real problem shows up twice. Take one out once it has been fine for two weeks.

Done when: the checks have run each weekday since Mon Sept 28 and each weekend shift since Sat Oct 3, and what they caught is in the Day 30 pack. At Day 30, decide whether they move to Matthew's ClickUp with the VAs' daily checklists (set up under 86d4bmr32 by Fri Oct 16).

title: Start Gelton's weekend shifts on Sat Oct 10 (40 hours a week)
description:
Owner: Jedy · Due: Fri Oct 2 · First possible shift: Sat Oct 3

Why
On the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Matthew agreed to two paid weekend shifts for Gelton: Saturday 10 AM to 12 PM and Sunday 7 to 9 PM Houston, from Sat Oct 3. On Mon Sept 28 he narrowed it: on a weekend with nothing booked, Gelton isn't needed. Marketing is usually off at weekends, so no new leads come in.

Decided
Gelton works the weekend shifts only on a weekend with a booking (Matthew, Mon Sept 28, on 14zf25zg4u9).
On a booked weekend his job is the schedule tab (cleaners updating their status), booked customers who call, and cleaner messages.
Monday's jobs get their card or deposit check at Nebs's Friday 6 PM check, the same way as the next day's jobs. No card and no deposit: she calls, then tells Jedy that evening. Never cancel alone (Erwin, Tue Sept 29).
The voicemail greeting, Facebook and Yelp show weekends as closed (86d4bx20r, done Tue Sept 29).

Steps
Every Friday at the end of his shift, Gelton checks the weekend schedule and tells Jedy whether he works Saturday, Sunday or neither. Jedy notes it for the pay.
Jedy makes sure both VAs have the weekend rules before Sat Oct 3. The weekend answer went to the team group on Tue Sept 29. Check that Gelton has step 1 and that Nebs has the Friday check of Monday's jobs.
Jedy settles the pay with Matthew before Sat Oct 3, for booked weekends only (per shift or per hour).
On the first booked weekend, Jedy checks Gelton's shift against his checklist (14zf25zg34t).

Done when
Gelton tells Jedy every Friday whether he works the weekend, Nebs does the Friday check of Monday's jobs, and the weekend pay is agreed.

Careful
No booking, no shift, and no weekend pay that weekend.
The shift times stay as agreed: Saturday 10 AM to 12 PM, Sunday 7 to 9 PM Houston.

title: Review the Lead Winner AI first message and its reply rate
description:
Why: on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Matthew asked us to look at Lead Winner AI, the automatic first reply to new leads, and its reply-rate analytics, and to suggest a better first message if we can. He is open to a change.

Steps
Erwin pulls the current first message and its reply rate from Lead Winner AI.
Divine and our copywriters write a better first message. Check the claims in it too (for example "fully insured" and "$49 off").
Divine sends it to Matthew for his yes, then it goes live and the reply rate is compared after two weeks.

Done when: Matthew has said yes or no to a new first message.

title: Design how the backup cleaner is picked and recorded
description:
Why: on the plan call (Fri Sept 25) Matthew asked for a backup cleaner known in advance for every job, because cleaners cancel last minute all the time. SOPs v2 says "Every job has a backup cleaner, picked before the day. Jedy shares where to note it."

Steps
Decide how the VA picks the backup (nearest good cleaner free that day; the VAs learn who covers which areas; distance checked on Google Maps, because the zip-code dashboard is not always right).
Decide where it is noted (for example the Confirmation tab or the booking notes in Progressive 83).
Jedy tells both VAs, and the "Still being set" lines in SOPs 3.0, 4.0 and 7.0 close in the next SOP revision.

Done when: both VAs pick and note a backup for every job the same way.

title: Days 31 to 90: growth work
description: Work the 90-day plan puts after Day 30 (Fri Oct 16). Nothing here is needed for the SOPs to run from Mon Sept 28, and each item needs Matthew's yes.

description: Everything Matthew sees each week and at Day 30, and how the team reaches him: the Friday report, the weekly call, the WhatsApp group with Divine and Jedy, the dashboard, the cleaner scorecard and the Day 30 review (Fri Oct 16).

title: SOP 7.0 Who does what

description: Everything still needed to finish SOP 5.0 in SOPs v2: lead alerts and lead logging, voicemail and listings on Tue Sept 29, the Quo templates, the Lead Winner AI review Matthew asked for, and weekend cover (Gelton's weekend shifts from Sat Oct 3).

title: SOP 4.0 Confirmations and cancellations
description: Everything still needed to finish SOP 4.0 in SOPs v2. The confirmation rule was agreed on the plan call, Fri Sept 25. The new work from the call is a backup cleaner for every job.

description: Everything still needed to finish SOP 3.0 in SOPs v2: switching on the 48-hour card hold, and the one-off clean-up of jobs showing as not charged. The card-or-deposit rule (a deposit of 50% of the job price) was agreed on the plan call, Fri Sept 25.
