title: SOP 1.0 Pricing and quotes
description: Everything still needed to finish SOP 1.0 in SOPs v2 (the file is on "Roll out SOPs v2 and move them into ClickUp"). The pricing rules themselves were agreed with Matthew on the plan call, Fri Sept 25.

title: Bring the website terms in line with how InVogue works
description:
Owner: Erwin lists the gaps, Divine takes them to Matthew · Start: after refund rule version 2 is agreed ("Write the refund and cleaner-pay rules", 86d4bmr2w)

Why
The terms page is a UK template (a UK late-payment law, UK words like "end of tenancy", no governing law, cut off at the end). It has no refund rule. It says payment is taken from the card given at booking, but the VAs take Zelle and Venmo deposits. Its re-clean rule leaves out regular cleans, but the home page promise has no such limit.

Done when
Matthew has seen the list of gaps and said which ones to fix.

title: Process map v3: Matthew's Sept 21 messages and the Quo audit
description:

title: Fix the Quo templates, sign-offs and deposit wording
description:
Owner: Jedy · Due: Mon Oct 5 (Houston), overdue · Waiting on: Matthew's yes for the Quo changes only (steps 2 to 4). The group-text rule (step 5) does not wait.
Why
A small clean-up from the Quo audit (7 to 20 Sept):
Three different sign-off names were used on the Hilton inbox in one week. A lead asked which company was texting.
"InVouge" is misspelled in the two most-used templates.
The templates do not say clearly that a booking needs a card or a Zelle deposit first.
Full addresses and the cleaner pay rate went out in group texts to up to 17 cleaners.
Steps
Send Matthew one message with the full proposal (draft below). He answers yes or no to each line, so it is one reply, not a back-and-forth.
One name per inbox. Once Matthew picks the names, tell both VAs.
Fix the spelling to "InVogue" in the two templates.
Deposit wording. Update the templates to say a booking is confirmed only once a card is uploaded or a Zelle deposit is sent (Matthew's card rule).
Group-text rule (does not need Matthew, nothing changes in Quo). Post it to both VAs today: in a job offer sent to many cleaners, give the street name and city only. Send the full address once a cleaner is assigned. Never send the pay rate or a door code in a group text.
Done when
Each inbox signs with one name. Both templates are spelled right and use the deposit wording, or Matthew said no. Both VAs have the group-text rule.
Careful
Nothing is changed in Quo without Matthew's yes.
Do not say which VA used which name. Both VAs share one Quo login.
Draft message to Matthew
Hi Matthew, four quick Quo fixes from the audit. Just reply yes or no to each:

One sign-off name per inbox so leads aren't confused about who's texting. I suggest: Hilton inbox = [NAME], 3785 inbox = [NAME].
Spelling: "InVouge" is misspelled in our two most-used templates. OK to fix to "InVogue"?
Deposit wording: add this line to the booking templates: "Your booking is confirmed once a card is on file or the Zelle deposit is received." OK?
FYI, no action needed: I'm telling the VAs that group job offers only include street and city. Full address after a cleaner is assigned, and never the pay rate or door code in a group text.

If you say yes, I'll make the changes in Quo today.

title: Brief Gelton and Nebs on SOPs v2
description:
Brief both VAs today, Fri Sept 25 (Houston), so they start Mon Sept 28 on SOPs v2 (the file is on "Roll out SOPs v2 and move them into ClickUp"). First review the Fathom recording of the plan call and give SOPs v2 a second look against it; send anything that looks off to Erwin before the briefing. Their shifts overlap from 12 to 5 PM Houston, so one session with both fits there; otherwise one each in their own shift. The written post in the team WhatsApp group stays on the send task next to this one.

Agenda
Read order: the intro, then SOP 7.0, then the SOP for each job. From Mon Sept 28, Jedy is the first stop, not Matthew.
Gelton, 8 AM to 5 PM Houston (SOP 7.0 Step 3): the 8 AM morning check (Scheduler on Today and Unstaffed, both Quo inboxes, cards on file, new leads); leads and quotes on the 40% floor, one Profit Margin row per quote; bookings with a card or deposit, and a backup cleaner for every job; complaints; each deep clean in the Deep Clean Tracker; agreed rates in the cleaner pay sheet; by 5 PM every lead answered or handed to Nebs, the cleaner pay list to Matthew on WhatsApp, and the end-of-shift post. Texts signed as Hilton (SOP 5.0 Step 3).
Nebs, 12 to 8 PM Houston (SOP 7.0 Step 4): texts to both sides 3 days ahead (on Friday, Tuesday and Wednesday jobs too) and a follow-up each day; both sides confirmed by 6 PM the day before, with the 6 PM card or deposit check; Unstaffed cleans assigned ahead; every lead alone from 5 PM, with the quotes, bookings and complaints that come with them; a call first to quoted leads that went quiet; rebooking calls and deep-clean follow-ups from Jedy's ready list, none after 7 PM; the 8 PM end-of-shift post.
Both VAs: at the start of every shift, both Quo inboxes, Thumbtack Messages and the business email (SOP 5.0 Step 2); claim each lead in the team group with a first name only; log every lead in the Lead Tracker by the end of the shift; post at the end of the shift by job date only, with no customer names or numbers. Jedy checks in daily against SOP 7.0 Steps 3 and 4.
Decisions from the call they use from Monday:
Price: 40% or above on every quote. 35% only for a customer about to walk or one moving onto a regular plan, first visit only. Caps count from the quoted price after the $49, and move in or out has the same cap as a deep clean. The $49 is for the first deep clean only (SOP 1.0 Steps 2 and 3).
Standard cleans carry the condition surcharge from the booking page (SOP 1.0 Step 1).
3 or more carpets: charge for half, rounded up, only if the job still clears 40%, with shampoo and machine rental counted as costs (SOP 1.0 Steps 1 and 2).
Quote from the cleaner pay sheet, standard or deep rate, not the rates in Progressive 83 (SOP 1.0 Step 2).
Card or deposit in by 6 PM the day before. The deposit is 50% of the job price and part of it, not on top, by Zelle or Venmo; Matthew checks them each evening (SOP 3.0 Step 2). Tell them whether the 48-hour card hold is switched on yet (SOP 3.0 Step 4).
Offering a job to several cleaners: street and city only; the full address only to the cleaner assigned; never a pay rate or door code in a group text (SOP 3.0 Step 3).
Check Unstaffed in the Scheduler and assign ahead. Every job has a backup cleaner; check the distance on Google Maps (SOP 3.0 Step 3).
A cleaner who cancels late: use every option first. A drive of more than about 45 minutes gets $15 for gas (SOP 4.0 Step 4).
Complaints: re-clean first, with photos within 48 hours and the same cleaner within 7 days; the go-back is left off the 5 PM pay list; then money back up to $50 (SOP 2.0 Steps 2 to 5).
Thumbtack stays on with the $1,500 weekly budget: never pause or hide it. New-lead alerts go to the Hilton number ending 3785; check Thumbtack Messages yourselves until Jedy confirms the change has taken (SOP 5.0 Step 1 and Escalation).
A new lead: call at once. No answer: a voicemail, then a text (SOP 5.0 Step 3).
Rebooking (Nebs): check Progressive 83 first, one script, plan prices only (15% off every 2 weeks, 10% monthly, 20% weekly only if asked), and no offer on a call after a problem clean (SOP 6.0 Steps 1 to 4).
Decide alone, or go to Jedy (SOP 7.0 Step 2): you decide the price, a re-clean, money back up to $50 and confirmations alone. Never cancel for no answer: Jedy says yes first, while you are on shift. Money back over $50, cleaner pay after a refund, or anything the SOPs do not cover: tell Jedy, and Divine takes it to Matthew.
Urgent path: Matthew is not available during his day and reads messages in the evening. Anything that cannot wait goes to Jedy, marked URGENT, in the team WhatsApp group.
Still being set (the rule until each is set):
Log one Profit Margin row per quote.
Ask Gelton for a cleaner's standard or deep rate until Jedy shares the pay sheet.
Log every complaint the same day; until the log sheet is set, send it to Jedy.
Whether a refund cuts a cleaner's pay, or a cleaner is paid on a complaint with no photos: tell Jedy.
Note each job's backup cleaner where Jedy says.
Nebs out: she tells Jedy early, and Jedy sets the 6 PM cover. Past-customer calls wait for her next shift.
Gelton out: he tells Jedy as soon as he knows, and Jedy arranges the pay list. Voicemail takes the morning from Tue Sept 29, and Nebs starts at 12 PM with the Gelton-out checklist (SOP 7.0 Step 5).
Log call, text and voicemail leads in the Lead Tracker.
The day 10 and day 21 emails stay off.
This weekend: there is no weekend shift until Sat Oct 3. Until then, Matthew covers the weekend, as today, including Monday's confirmations and card or deposit checks. Voicemail takes the hours nobody is on from Tue Sept 29. From Sat Oct 3, Gelton works Sat 10 AM to 12 PM and Sun 7 to 9 PM Houston, two 2-hour shifts Matthew approved: SOP 5.0 Steps 2, 3 and 5, with the Sunday and Monday confirmations and card or deposit checks (SOP 5.0 Step 6; SOP 4.0 Step 5; SOP 3.0 Step 5). The full walk-through of his weekend steps comes before Sat Oct 3.
Nebs, the HAR note: no new realtor calls. One last follow-up to the realtors who asked for more information, then HAR closes. Social media stays paused (SOP 7.0 Step 4, item 5).
Where the SOPs live: the team WhatsApp group for now. Matthew approved his own ClickUp; it is set up by Day 30 (Fri Oct 16), and Jedy walks them through it then (SOP 7.0 Step 7).

Done when
Both VAs are briefed today (Houston) and have SOPs v2 in the team WhatsApp group (the post itself is on the send task).
Each can say back their Mon Sept 28 day, what they decide alone and the URGENT path.
Both know Matthew covers the weekend until Gelton's shifts start on Sat Oct 3.
Nebs has the HAR note in writing, with no realtor names.
A comment here gives the date, who joined and the open questions, with no customer names. A question that changes a rule goes to the SOPs v3 fixes, and anything for Matthew goes through Divine.

Old description (Nebs's new daily lane, written before her process call) is saved by Erwin. Its Day 30 baselines (Thumbtack 28-day booking rate 15.9%, leads awaiting a response 467, rebook rate within 30 days 35.8%, jobs with both sides confirmed 51%) belong to "Run the Day 30 review".

title: Build the cleaner pay sheet: standard and deep rate per cleaner
description:
Owner: Erwin drafts from Matthew's answers, Jedy shares it with the VAs · Due: Fri Sept 25 · Blocked by: "Present the plan to Matthew and get his decisions" (86d4bx1wx) · Needs: Needs Matthew

Why
Today every cleaner pay question goes to Matthew. In Quo (7 to 20 Sept) there were 9 pay threads in 14 days. All 9 went to Matthew, and 5 were left hanging. From 28 Sept he is at work in the daytime. One page lets the VAs answer these without him.

Steps
Get Matthew's answers on the call, or by message after it, on each of these:
The rate by job type. Matthew says two cleaners are on $30 an hour and a third is paid hourly (21 Sept). Progressive 83 showed one at $30 on 18 Sept. Our default until Matthew decides on Wednesday: a VA never agrees a new rate. If a cleaner asks for more, the VA says Matthew sets rates and puts the ask on the one list for Matthew's evening (14zf25zffrv step 4). The cleaner is told when they will hear back. Why it matters: a $30 cleaner needs $50 per paid hour to clear 40%, against $41.67 for a $25 cleaner.
Extras, like inside the oven or the fridge.
Gas. Our default until Matthew decides on Wednesday: no gas money unless he agreed it for that job. We recommend one flat amount for jobs further than a distance he sets. Gas is not in his tab today, but it cuts the margin just like cleaner pay: $20 on the $281 deep clean with a $25 cleaner takes it from 45.9% to 38.8%, under 40%. Until he sets it, the VA does not promise gas money and puts the ask on the list for Matthew's evening.
A cleaner asks for more than her rate on a job. Gelton asks Matthew each time (22 Sept). Our suggestion: start from the 'most the cleaner may be paid' line in Matthew's tab, and the job must still clear 40% at the new rate. The 35% exception floor is for a customer's price, not a cleaner's rate, unless Matthew says so. His answers on the call replace the rate and gas defaults above.
The carpet machine and the solution.
What happens to cleaner pay after a customer discount or a complaint.
A fixed pay time.
What to do when the check-in app fails.
Write it on one page. One line per question, in plain words a VA can use in a reply.
Anything Matthew has not answered stays on the page as "not decided yet", so the VAs know to still ask.
Jedy shares it with both VAs and saves it in the client docs.

Done when
Both VAs have the page. The next cleaner pay question is answered from it, with no message to Matthew in the daytime.

Careful
Nothing about cutting a cleaner's paid hours goes in until Matthew has answered that on the call.
Pay rates are not sent in group texts.
Keep it in line with the W4 task "Write the refund and cleaner-pay rules" (86d4bmr2w).

title: Refund and discount rule, version 1
description:
Owner: Erwin writes, Jedy posts it to the VAs · Due: Fri Sept 25 · Blocked by: "Present the plan to Matthew and get his decisions" (86d4bx1wx) · Needs: Needs Matthew

Why
On 21 Sept Matthew wrote that refunds and discounts keep him up at night, and what the cleaner is paid after an unhappy customer. From 28 Sept he is at work in the daytime. The VAs need a short rule before then.

This is the short version. The full version stays in W4, "Write the refund and cleaner-pay rules" (86d4bmr2w). Neither version waits for a document. The T&C Jedy posted on 22 Sept is the website terms page, which has a re-clean rule and no refund rule.

Where we start, from Quo (7 to 20 Sept): complaints get a first reply in about 8 minutes. But 6 of 9 left something open, like a money claim, a promised update or a cleaner's pay question.

Steps
Take Matthew's answers from the call: the refund cap in dollars, and what a VA may give alone.
Start from what his website terms already promise, so the VA rule does not say something different. A free re-clean for deep, move-out and one-off cleans. Asked for within 48 hours of the clean, in writing, with photos. The cleaner goes back within 7 days, with up to 3 times offered. Regular cleans, fixed-hour bookings and carpets are not covered. Use Matthew's answer from the call on whether regular cleans get a re-clean too.
Write one page, in this order:
Re-clean first. Today a re-clean costs no extra cleaner pay: the cleaner goes back to finish and is not paid for the second visit, and at interview cleaners are told they must go back and finish anything missed (Gelton, 22 Sept). This goes in as how it works today until Matthew confirms it as the rule on the call.
The refund cap Matthew sets.
Who may give what alone, and who to ask above that. Who replies to the customer: our recommendation is the VA, every time, from this rule. It goes to Matthew only when the ask is above the VA's cap, or when Matthew already holds that case. Then the VA tells the customer when to expect an answer. Matthew decides.
What a customer gets after a cleaner no-show.
A money claim gets an answer within a day.
Close the loop. Every complaint has an owner and an end. Complaints come in by text, in reviews and on Thumbtack, and Gelton named no place where they are written down (22 Sept). Log each one in one place both VAs can open, with a reply time. Today Gelton asks Matthew whether he should reply or Matthew will. The rule names who replies, so no complaint waits for that answer.
The cleaner is told how her pay is affected, once Matthew has decided that.
Check it says the same as "VA decision rules, version 1", so the VAs do not get two answers.
Jedy posts it to both VAs and saves it in the client docs.

Done when
The page is posted to both VAs. The refund cap and the "alone" limit are numbers from Matthew.

Careful
Do not open a complaint reply by questioning the customer, for example by pointing to the good review they gave the cleaner. Say sorry and ask what is left to fix.
The cleaner pay part stays marked "not decided yet" until Matthew decides it. Do not guess.

title: Set up the Quote Log tab: one row per quote
description:
Owner: Erwin copies the tab in. Erwin and Jedy test it. Jedy sends the VA note and Matthew's 7 questions. · Goes live: with the Lead Tracker switch-over (86d4bx21c, about Fri Oct 2 to Tue Oct 6) · Waiting on: Matthew's yes to the Google Sheet. Jedy's Monday message on 86d4bx1zc asks about the Quote Log too.

Why
The price rules are decided and live in SOP 1.0 (Steps 1 to 3). Step 5 asks for one row per quote, so Matthew sees the exceptions on Friday. Today both VAs type into the same input cells of his Profit Margin tab, so each quote wipes the last and nothing is kept. On 26 Sept the cells still held someone's last quote (24.8%, DO NOT ACCEPT).

What changed (Erwin, Mon Sept 28)
The Quote Log goes in as a new tab in the Lead Tracker once it is a Google Sheet (86d4bx21c), not in the Excel Cleaner Tracker. One file and one link for leads and quotes, and GIM can read the quote rows for the Friday report and the dashboard, so nobody counts them by hand.
So there is no separate heads-up to Matthew and no Excel build. His 21 Sept yes to one row per quote stands, and the Monday Sheets message tells him the Quote Log comes with it.
If Matthew stays in Excel or says no to the move, the Fallback below applies.

What we know
The model is GIM's Google mock (no names), in info@divineorigines.com's Drive. Erwin shares it with Jedy. Its Quote Log tab holds the real formulas, checked in Google Sheets on Mon Sept 28, and the 5 example rows in rows 3 to 7 (EXAMPLE in the Note). Its Read me tab has every heading, drop-down, number limit and formula, and the expected results. The attached Quote-Log-mock.xlsx is only for the Excel fallback.
27 columns. Blue headings are typed by the VA. Grey ones are formulas: Quoted, Cleaner pay, Lowest (normal), Lowest (with a case), Margin, Verdict, Cap check. The rules sit in AD3:AD9 (40%, 50%, 35%, $50, $35, $49, $60 a carpet), so a rule changes in one cell.
Margin = (price minus cleaner pay minus carpet costs) divided by price, the same as his calculator. Carpet costs count on any carpet job, as in his tab. SOP 1.0 Step 2 says 3 or more, so that is question 1. Verdict GOAL, OK or EXCEPTION OK: go ahead. STOP: do not agree, ask Jedy.
The quote row does the math itself, so the VAs stop using his Profit Margin calculator at the switch-over (Erwin, Mon Sept 28). It overwrites itself and still has three older rules that differ from the SOP. We never change or delete it: Matthew decides whether to keep it (question 4).
Rates come from the cleaner pay sheet (14zf25zg34h). Until it is shared, the VA asks Gelton.

Steps
This week: Jedy looks through the Google mock (link above) and gets familiar with it. No heads-up to Matthew and no Excel build.
On Matthew's yes, once the test copy is shared (86d4bx21c step 2): Erwin, signed in as info@divineorigines.com, opens GIM's Google mock, right-clicks the Quote Log tab > Copy to > Existing spreadsheet, and picks the test copy. In the test copy, rename "Copy of Quote Log" to Quote Log and drag it right after Thumbtack Leads. Nothing else in the file changes.
Test on the web, during the copy check (Jedy with Erwin): the 5 example rows come with the tab in rows 3 to 7. Check them against the Read me. Row 3 is the SOP 1.0 Step 3 example ($330 list, $49 Y, 6 h 05 m, $25 cleaner): Quoted $281.00, Cleaner pay $152.08, Lowest $254 (normal) and $234 (with a case), Margin 45.9%, "OK: 40% or more". In row 8, type "Deep clean" in Service: it must be refused. Then clear row 8. Leave rows 3 to 7 in so Matthew can see them in step 5.
Test on a phone (Google Sheets app): one test row in row 8, the drop-downs, a wrong entry refused, the Verdict. Then clear it.
Jedy shows Matthew the Quote Log with the checked copy (86d4bx21c step 8).
At the switch-over (86d4bx21c step 9) the tab goes live with the Sheet. First clear the typed cells in rows 3 to 7 (the grey formulas stay), so the VAs start on an empty log. If a fresh copy was converted, Erwin copies the tab in again and checks rows 3 to 7 before clearing them. Then Jedy sends both VAs the note below in the team WhatsApp group.
Jedy sends Matthew the 7 questions (message below) in the ops WhatsApp group and posts his answers here for Erwin. SOPs v3 (14zf25zg34c) renames "Profit Margin tab" to "Quote Log tab" in SOP 1.0 Step 5 (also screenshot 1.2, the tools table and the price row in SOP 7.0 Step 1), points to the Lead Tracker Sheet, and takes out the "Still being set" lines for the tab.
Erwin, separately: list the Quo template lines that invite haggling, like asking for the customer's budget. They come out only with Matthew's yes.

Done when
The Quote Log tab is in the Lead Tracker Sheet and nothing else in the file changed. The 5 example rows matched the Read me and were cleared, a wrong entry is refused on the web and the phone, both VAs have the note, and Matthew's answers are posted here.

Fallback: Matthew stays in Excel, or says no to the move
Erwin decides first (86d4bx1zc steps 7 and 8). Then the Quote Log goes in as a new tab right after Profit Margin in the Excel Cleaner Tracker, from the attached Quote-Log-mock.xlsx, following its Read me's add-it steps 1 to 16:
Check Viewing switches to Editing. Send Matthew the heads-up below the day you build, before 8 PM Houston.
Build only while nobody is quoting: after 8 PM or before 8 AM Houston, never in Gelton's weekend shifts.
Test the 5 example rows on the web and one row on a phone, as in steps 3 and 4. OneDrive version history is the way back.
In the VA note, say "the Quote Log tab of the Cleaner Tracker". In Matthew's 7 questions, say "right after your Profit Margin tab".

Heads-up to Matthew, fallback only (copy as is):

Hi Matthew, quick heads up. Since you said yes to one row per quote on the 21st, I'll add a new tab called Quote Log right after your Profit Margin tab, at night when nobody is quoting. Your calculator and every other tab stay exactly as they are. Just tell me if you'd like me to hold off.

Only if you cannot edit the file, add:

Could you give me edit access to the Cleaner Tracker? It's only so I can add the new tab.

Careful
It is Matthew's file. Only the new tab is added. His Excel Profit Margin tab stays as it is, and from the switch-over the VAs use only the Quote Log.
A grey cell that differs from the Read me: stop and send Erwin a screenshot. File > Version history is the way back.
Lead ref is the Progressive 83 lead number or a first name only. No phone numbers or full names in the tab.
Never take the cleaner rate from the Rate column in Progressive 83. It is not up to date.
Give no margin percent for any past job or for the whole business.

Note to Gelton and Nebs, at the switch-over (copy as is)

Quote Log: from today, every price you give goes in the new Quote Log tab of the Lead Tracker, not the Profit Margin tab (SOP 1.0 Step 5).

1. Every price you give gets one new row in the Quote Log tab. Use the first empty row and never type over another row.
2. Always fill: date, you, lead, source, service, the Progressive 83 list price (with every carpet), hours and minutes, and the cleaner's rate from the pay sheet. Fill plan, condition, $49, booked before and carpets only when they apply. Blank means one time, none or no.
3. Before you negotiate, read the grey Lowest columns. Lowest (normal) is your limit. Lowest (with a case) is only for a customer who would walk or is moving onto a regular plan, first visit only.
4. Type the agreed price (blank if they took the quote) and the case, then read Verdict. GOAL, OK or EXCEPTION OK: go ahead. STOP: do not agree, ask me.
5. Mark Booked Y or N when you know, and add a short Note for every case or on-site change. Matthew reads the exceptions on Friday.

Message to Matthew once the tab is live (copy as is)

Hi Matthew, the Quote Log tab is live in the Lead Tracker sheet. Each quote now gets its own row with the margin, the lowest price allowed and a go or stop, using the price rules in the SOPs. 7 quick points came up while setting it up. A short answer to each is perfect.

1. Carpets: the tab counts rental and shampoo as costs on any carpet job, like your Profit Margin tab does. The SOP only counts them for 3 or more carpets. One carpet brings in $60 but costs about $58 to $64 in rental and shampoo, plus 30 minutes of pay. OK to change the SOP to count them on any carpet job?

2. Closets have no discount cap yet, so any closet discount comes to me first. What cap would you like, if any?

3. A past customer moving onto a regular plan gets no 35% price in the tab, because the 35% is for a first visit. Is that right, or should their first plan visit count?

4. Gelton and Nebs will use only the Quote Log from now on, so they won't need your Profit Margin tab. It also still has three older lines that differ from the SOP: owner approval below 40%, THIN, and lowering the hours. Would you like to keep the tab as it is for yourself, or remove it?

5. The condition extras show as +25% and +50%, as on the booking page today. If you change them, just tell me and I'll update the tab.

6. The tab needs each cleaner's standard and deep rate. Where will the cleaner pay sheet live?

7. If a rule changes later, like the floor or a cap, old rows get checked again with the new rule. Is that fine, or should I freeze each month's rows?

title: W4 | Oct 5-9 - The money work: refunds, the recurring offer, win-backs

Run the win-back sequence for the 37 quiet customers · Erwin · Fri Oct 9
Bring the website terms in line with how InVogue works · Erwin lists the gaps, Divine takes them to Matthew · after item 1 is agreed

The two customer numbers, so nobody mixes them up
189 customers since February. 68 ever booked twice. Of those 68, 37 have gone quiet 60 days or more - that is the win-back list. 31 are still active repeat customers and they carried 61 percent of August revenue. Both are checked against the customer export.

Careful with the number 37. Progressive 83 separately shows 37 active recurring plans. That is a different measure and the matching number is a coincidence. Never quote the two as if they were the same thing, and never to Matthew.

Version 2 of the refund and cleaner-pay rules is written and the VAs have it. The recurring offer goes out at the right moment instead of by chance, and the post-clean ask has moved from about 14 days to within 48 hours. The win-back sequence has run and we can say how many came back.

Rules
Every update goes in the task comments. Not in DMs, not in a call.

title: Rule for evenings and weekends
description:
Owner: Erwin writes it. Divine gets Matthew's answers on the plan call. The PO posts it to the VAs. · Due: Fri Sept 25 · Blocked by: "Present the plan to Matthew and get his decisions" · Needs: Needs Matthew

Why
Nobody is on shift on weekends, and from 5 to 8 PM only Nebs is on. Someone covers the rest today, but nobody is rostered for it. Meanwhile Google and Yelp say open 8 AM to 8 PM every day, Thumbtack says 24 hours, and the booking page sells same-day and weekend slots. This is check 6 of the 8 for Sept 28.

Facts
Quo, 7-20 Sept. 45% of inbound texts arrive outside Gelton's 8-5 shift. 18% arrive when nobody is rostered (weekday nights and weekends). 27% arrive from 5 to 8 PM, when only Nebs is on.
Weekends bring about 19 texts a day, mostly from cleaners. Customers and leads text too, for example a customer whose cleaner had not arrived.
Someone already answers weekend and late texts. Both VAs share one Quo login, so nobody can say who.
Weekend first reply: about 44 minutes (median). 3 of 11 weekend threads got no reply that day. The worst case seen: a lead waited 51 hours over a weekend.
Missed calls: 12 to 14 in 14 days. 7 of the 12 fell outside Gelton's hours. No missed caller in two weeks left a voicemail (0, possibly 1). Matthew confirmed why on 21 Sept: there is no voicemail on Quo, only an AI answer message.
The number on Google, Yelp and Facebook (ending 3610) is not a Quo inbox. Calls to it never reach the VAs.

Steps
Take Matthew's answers from the plan call: who answers after 5 PM and on weekends, which hours we publish, and whether same-day and weekend slots stay open online.
The rule has to decide one of two, in plain words:
Rostered and paid cover: who, which hours, and what they may decide alone.
An auto-reply that tells people when replies come, with a real time.
Write one page: what happens to a call, a text, a new lead and a cleaner problem outside VA hours. What the VAs do first thing next morning.
Set the after-hours message: what Quo says when nobody answers, and what the auto-reply says. Voicemail: Matthew confirmed on 21 Sept there is no voicemail on Quo, only an AI answer message, and he thinks voicemail is a good idea. Next: agree the greeting wording on the call, with "text this number" in it, and switch it on with his yes. Both need Matthew's yes before anything in Quo changes.
Hand the listing hours to the PO for the task "One phone number and real hours on every listing". Flag that the 3610 number is outside Quo.
If Gelton keeps watching his phone on weekend job days, write down what he does and what he does not do. He told us this on his call. Do not read the weekend texts in Quo as his, because the login is shared.
For Day 30 (16 Oct), count again from Quo the same way: texts outside Gelton's shift (45% now), texts with nobody rostered (18% now), weekend first reply (44 minutes now), and missed calls with a voicemail (0 now).

Done when
The rule is posted to both VAs, the after-hours message is set, voicemail is checked with Matthew's yes, and the published hours match what the team really covers.

Careful
Do not say who answers evenings or weekends today. Someone does, and the shared login hides who. Do not name Gelton, Nebs or Matthew for it.
Nothing changes in Quo (greeting, auto-reply, voicemail) or on the listings without Matthew's yes.
Say 12 to 14 missed calls, not 12. Two calls are still in doubt until two days are pulled again.
Every Quo text count is a floor, because Quo shows at most 10 messages per contact per day.

title: Confirmation rule for customers and cleaners
description:
Owner: Erwin writes it. Divine gets Matthew's answers on the plan call. The PO posts it to the VAs. · Due: Fri Sept 25 · Blocked by: "Present the plan to Matthew and get his decisions" · Needs: Needs Matthew

Why
On 21 Sept Matthew asked for this in writing: the customer confirms the booking, and the cleaner confirms it too. This task used to cover only the cleaner, and no task covered the customer side. This is where no-shows and wrong cancellations start. Today there is no time by which a cleaner must say yes, and no written list of who to call next. Matthew catches some of it himself. This is check 5 of the 8 for Sept 28.

Facts
Confirmations go out 2 to 3 days before by Quo text. Matthew's Cleaner Tracker has a CUSTOMER & CLEANER CONFIRMATION tab to log them. The tracker also lists cleaners by area as primary, backup and reserve, but we have not seen anyone use it.
Progressive 83 can send a job offer the cleaner must accept by a deadline. The VAs do not use it today.
Quo, 7-20 Sept. The Nebs inbox sends most of the confirmations: 40 to customers and 30 to cleaners. The cleaner's text goes within 10 minutes of the customer's.
Customers reply 60% of the time. Their replies often carry a question (arrival time, the vacuum, who is coming). At least 3 of those questions got no answer by text.
When a customer is silent, a day-before text says the booking will be cancelled later that day. That rule cancelled two paying customers on two Saturdays in a row (12 and 19 Sept). One was angry. Of 4 day-before chasers sent on Fri 18 for Saturday jobs, 1 got a reply.
Two customers answered a confirmation with "we already cancelled", so the schedule is not always right. Some customers text Matthew's own phone, which Quo cannot see.
Cleaners reply 81% of the time (both inboxes, confirmations and job offers).
The Hilton inbox sends no day-before confirmation to customers or cleaners. Jobs booked there get none.
The day-of arrival check goes out at or after the job window opens (08:13 and 10:10 for 9 AM jobs). So the office hears about a no-show from the customer.
6 cleaner drop-outs in 14 days: 1 job lost, 1 rebooked with no make-good. Cleaners who stay silent in a job blast are not told when the job is taken.

Steps
On the plan call, Divine gets Matthew's answers:
When the customer confirmation goes out, and the deadline to reply.
By what time the day before a cleaner must have said yes (our suggestion: 6 PM), and whether the VAs may move the job to a backup without asking him.
What happens when a customer is silent. Our suggestion: a phone call before any cancellation, and never a cancellation when nobody is on shift. This replaces the "confirm or it auto-cancels" line.
The backup order when a cleaner is silent or drops out.
Write the rule on one page, both sides:
Who: Nebs owns confirmations day to day. The Nebs inbox already sends most of them.
When: the time the texts go out, and the deadline for a reply.
Hilton inbox bookings: they get the same day-before confirmations to the customer and the cleaner. Today they get none.
Customer silent: a call before any cancellation. Never cancel when nobody is on shift. Answer any question the customer sends back.
Cleaner silent or drops out: the cut-off time, who checks, who to call next in that area, when to tell the customer, and what to say. Tell the other cleaners in a blast when the job is taken.
Day of: the arrival check goes out BEFORE the job window opens, not after. If the cleaner has not answered, the backup order starts and the customer hears it from us first.
Log: every confirmation goes in the CUSTOMER & CLEANER CONFIRMATION tab in Matthew's Cleaner Tracker.
Ask Matthew to confirm the backup list in his Cleaner Tracker is current.
With Matthew's yes, try Progressive 83's job offers with a deadline on a few jobs, so a quiet cleaner shows up a day early.
The PO posts it to both VAs.
For Day 30 (16 Oct), count again from Quo the same way: customer reply rate, cleaner reply rate, and bookings cancelled for a silent customer (2 in 14 days now).

Done when
The rule is posted and covers customers and cleaners. The cut-off times are agreed. The first week runs with no job left unconfirmed past the cut-off, and no paying customer cancelled without a call. Baselines for Day 30: customers reply 60%, cleaners 81%.

Careful
A manual booking also needs a card on file or a Zelle deposit to count as confirmed (Matthew, 21 Sept). That sits in "Card on file: 48-hour hold and the card-link rule". This page links to it and does not repeat it.
Do not say which VA sent what. Both VAs share one Quo login. "The Hilton inbox" or "the Nebs inbox" at most.
In a job offer sent to many cleaners, give the street name and city only. Send the full address once a cleaner is assigned. Never send the pay rate or a door code in a group text.
No customer or cleaner names, numbers or addresses in the rule, this task or the comments.
Nothing changes in the Quo templates, Progressive 83 or the Cleaner Tracker without Matthew's yes.

title: Owner and backup for each of Matthew's daytime jobs
description:
Owner: Erwin writes it. Divine gets Matthew's answers on the plan call. The PO posts it to the VAs. · Due: Fri Sept 25 · Blocked by: "Present the plan to Matthew and get his decisions" · Needs: Needs Matthew

Why
From Mon Sept 28 Matthew is not there in the daytime. Six jobs he does himself today have no other owner. The sixth, cleaner pay questions, was added on 21 Sept after the Quo audit. This is check 4 of the 8 for Sept 28.

Facts
His daytime jobs: turning Thumbtack on in the morning and off at night and weekends, plus picking which leads it buys; the morning check of Quo, the email and the schedule; answering the VAs; catching double bookings; the new-lead emails that only reach him. Evening jobs that stay with him for now: cleaner pay and the carpet machine deposit.

Cleaner pay questions are a daytime job too, and they break on Sept 28. Paying the cleaners is an evening job. Their questions about pay come in all day. Quo, 7-20 Sept: 9 pay threads in 14 days, every one routed to Matthew, 5 left with a question hanging. The questions were about extras (inside the oven), pay for a cancelled job, gas money, and whether a customer's discount cuts the cleaner's pay. From Sept 28 each one waits until the evening at best.

"Answering the VAs" also covers four kinds of decision that go to him in the daytime today: price floors and off-list discounts, extras that are not on the list, hiring, and cleaner pay. The limits for those go in "VA decision rules, version 1". This table only says who owns them.

Steps
One short table: the job, who does it from Sept 28, who backs them up, and what happens if neither is there.
Use Matthew's answers from the plan call, mainly question 3 (who holds the Thumbtack switch) and question 5 (a day without Gelton).
Include the morning check: what to open, in what order, and by what time.
Add cleaner pay questions to the table. The owner answers from the pay sheet in the task "Write the cleaner pay sheet". Anything the sheet does not cover goes on one list for Matthew's evening, and the cleaner is told when they will hear back. No pay question is left without a reply.
The PO posts it to the VAs and saves it in the client docs. Divine sends Matthew a copy.

Done when
Every job on the list has a named owner and a named backup, cleaner pay questions included, and both VAs have seen it.

Careful
Do not say which VA handled which pay thread. Both VAs share one Quo login.
No cleaner names in the table, this task or the comments.
Pay rates and pay rules are Matthew's call. Nothing is promised to a cleaner until he says yes.

title: VA decision rules, version 1
description:
Owner: Erwin writes it. Divine gets Matthew's answers on the plan call. The PO posts it to the VAs. · Due: Fri Sept 25 · Blocked by: "Present the plan to Matthew and get his decisions" · Needs: Needs Matthew

Why
Matthew said better SOPs are "the biggest thing". On 21 Sept he wrote that margin is what keeps him up at night. He sees jobs accepted at a lower margin than he wants. His floor is 40% on every job. He said so on the discovery call (14 Sept), on the kickoff (16 Sept) and in writing on 21 Sept. 50% is the goal, new on 21 Sept. What is still open is the floor number under 40% (he answered the rest on 21 Sept, see Facts) and the dollar cap on refunds. From Sept 28 he is at work in the daytime and cannot answer. This is check 2 of the 8 for Sept 28.

Facts
His Profit Margin tab. Matthew built it on 21 Sept in his Cleaner Tracker (OneDrive Excel). Floor 40%, target 50%, high 55%. A quote calculator: charge, cleaner hourly rate, hours, carpet rental and supplies give cleaner pay, profit, margin and a verdict. Negotiation limits: the lowest charge at the floor, the charge for 50% and for 55%, the most the cleaner may be paid, and the most hours allowed. A price guide by hours. Steps for the VAs.
His formula: margin = (charge - cleaner pay - rental - supplies) / charge. Travel and card fees are not taken off.
His step 5: red means do not accept, get owner approval first. From Sept 28 that approval waits until the evening, and by then the customer is usually gone.
His step 7: if the customer will not move on price, lower the hours or use a lower-rate cleaner, instead of dropping the margin.
Lowest charge per paid cleaner hour (cleaner pay only): for 40%, $41.67 with a $25 cleaner and $50.00 with a $30 cleaner. For 50%, $50.00 and $60.00. Matthew confirmed on 21 Sept that the 40% is on cleaner pay only, so these stand. InVogue keeps the $10 supplies fee, so a weekly plan with a $30 cleaner clears 40%.
The deep clean with $49 off, at full booked hours: about 45% with a $25 cleaner, mid 30s with a $30 cleaner. Progressive 83 shows 25 cleaners at $25 and 1 at $30. Nobody is on $35 in the tool. Matthew says (21 Sept) two cleaners are on $30 an hour now, a third is paid hourly, and more top-rated cleaners will likely get $30 for deep cleans, so the tool may not match what he pays. His rule: a discounted deep clean goes to a $25 cleaner, unless the price still clears the floor with a $30 cleaner.
Quo, 7-20 Sept. The $49 was on every deep-clean quote before the customer asked (20 of 20 in text, 7 of 7 lead calls). Whether that is standard or habit is a question for Matthew. The Hilton inbox made 11 more price cuts in 14 days, 9 with no owner check. The Nebs inbox made no improvised cut. Quo does not show hours or the cleaner's rate, so it cannot show the margin on a job.
Four kinds of decision go to Matthew in the daytime today (Quo): price floors and off-list discounts, pricing of extras that are not on the list (for example a laundry room or inside the microwave), hiring, and cleaner pay. From Sept 28 each one waits until the evening. Each needs an answer before Sept 28.
Divine's reply to Matthew about his tab (sent by Divine on 21 Sept) gave him three ways to handle a job under 40%. He answered the same day. He is open to going below 40% when the lead is already paid for, but wants a clear floor number so the team knows exactly how far they can go. He does not want a lower price for a customer who is already happy with it. Flexibility only when a customer is negotiating or agreeing to a recurring plan. The floor number is the one open item. Our recommendation is 35%, with the rules written in "Write the margin rule on Matthew's Profit Margin tab" (14zf25zfhxk): 40% stays the floor for every quote, 35% only for a customer who is negotiating or moving onto a recurring plan, the drop on the first visit only for recurring, never a lower price once accepted, a $30 cleaner only if the job still clears the floor, one row per exception in the tab, and a dollar cap per job.
The same reply asked him three questions. He answered all three on 21 Sept: the 40% is on cleaner pay only; InVogue keeps the $10 supplies fee; two cleaners are on $30 an hour and a third is paid hourly, and discounted jobs go to a $25 cleaner unless the price still clears the floor with a $30 cleaner. He also agreed to one row per quote in the tab.

Steps
Price and discount decisions are written in 'Write the margin rule on Matthew's Profit Margin tab' (14zf25zfhxk). This task covers the rest and points there, so the two do not say different things.

Lead with the margin floor, not a dollar limit. Before a VA agrees any price, they put the job into Matthew's Profit Margin tab and read the verdict. At 40% or above they can agree it. Under 40% they follow the rule from step 2.
On the plan call, Divine gets Matthew's answers:
The floor number under 40%. Our recommendation is 35%, with the rules in 14zf25zfhxk. Flexibility only for a customer who is negotiating or moving onto a recurring plan. Never lower a price a customer has already accepted.
The dollar cap for a refund, and whether a free re-clean needs his OK.

Trigger
A customer asks for money back, or a cleaner asks to be paid for a job that went wrong.

What it must cover
What a customer can get, and worked out from what base. One real case: quoted 25% of $375, given 25% of $345. There is no rule today.
The limit a VA may settle alone, who approves above it, and by what hour of the evening.
Whether a free re-clean can be given without asking.
The cleaner side: who pays when a cleaner goes back to redo a job.
Where complaints get written down. There is no place for that today.
Close the loop. The Quo audit (7-20 Sept) found the first reply to a complaint is fast, but 6 of 9 complaints left something open: a money claim, an invoice, a promised update, a second call, a make-good, a cleaner's pay question. So every complaint gets an owner. A money claim gets an answer within a day. The cleaner is told how her pay is affected.

A refund has been settled once using this page, with no message to Matthew.

The cleaner-pay part waits for Matthew's own answer on booked hours versus real hours. That question is now on the plan call as his own step 7: his Profit Margin tab tells the VAs to lower the hours if a customer will not move on price. Do not write that part before he answers.

What each add-on buys: fridge $30, single oven $50, double $75, range $100, laundry $30, carpet $60, supplies $10.
The supplies rule per service, and whether the customer must own a vacuum and a mop.

title: Write the rule for a job that turns out bigger
description:
Owner: Jedy drafts, Erwin reviews · Due: Wed Sept 30 · Blocked by: nothing to start the draft · Needs: Matthew's answers from the plan call (what the 40% is measured on, the dollar limit and the under-40% choice)

Trigger
The cleaner arrives and the home needs more work than the booking says, or the customer asks for more on the day.

What it must cover
How the VA checks the real scope: photos, room count, condition notes.
The choice: add the condition charge (+25% or +50%) or re-quote as a deep clean. Which one, and when.
How much the VA may add without asking Matthew. The margin floor is set by Matthew: 40% or above on every job, 50% as the goal. He said 40% on the discovery call and the kickoff, and put both numbers in writing on 21 Sept. Write this rule against that floor, using his Profit Margin tab in the Cleaner Tracker. The VA puts the new hours into his quote calculator. If the job would drop under 40%, the price goes up before the work carries on. Quick check without the tab: to stay at 40%, every paid cleaner hour needs at least $41.67 of price with a $25 cleaner, or $50 with a $30 cleaner (for 50%: $50 and $60). That counts cleaner pay only. Supplies and carpet rental come on top. Only three things are still open, and all three go to Matthew on the plan call: the dollar amount the VA may add alone, what the VA does when a job would still land under 40%, and what the 40% is measured on (cleaner pay only, or also fees, lead cost and supplies).
What the customer is told, and when. Before the work carries on, never after.
Where it gets written down: the booking note in Progressive 83 and the Lead Tracker.

Done when
Gelton has followed it once on a real job without asking Matthew, and the note landed in the right place.

Careful
Nothing goes in here about cutting a cleaner's booked hours until Matthew has answered that question himself. His own tab now says, at step 7, to lower the hours if a customer will not move on price. That question is on the plan call. Until he answers it there, keep hours out of this rule.

title: Confirm with Malik whether the full-refund-for-late-delivery promise still stands
description:
Findings (Sep 21):
 
There is a direct contradiction between two pages on noirlab.io:
 
Video Ad Production page FAQ states: "If we fail to deliver within the stated turnaround without prior agreement, you receive a full refund."
Refund Policy page states: "Once production has started, the order becomes non-refundable" (production starts within 30 minutes of ordering).
 
With on-time delivery at ~50%, the product page promise creates significant refund exposure. Malik needs to clarify which version is the real policy so we can align customer-facing language accordingly.


The noirlab.io FAQ promises a full refund for late delivery, and the on-time delivery rate is currently around 50%. Before we can write customer communication SOPs and reply templates, we need Malik's decision on whether that refund promise still holds.

A reply to a customer whose order is late reads completely differently depending on whether that promise stands, so the SOP work is blocked until this is settled.

This was first raised on 24 Aug and is still open.

What needs to happen:
Ask Malik directly: does the full-refund-for-late-delivery policy on the FAQ still apply?
If yes, confirm the process for issuing refunds.
If no, get his revised position so we can draft the right customer-facing language.

title: E9 - Weekly automation health check (live board)
description:
Updated 20 September.

Recurrence: every Monday, before the client catch-up. Time: 45 minutes.

Overview

The daily check catches things that broke. This one catches things that drifted. The automations depend on a few things staying the same: the form's questions, the product names in Shopify, the list names on the board, the editors on the board, and a monthly budget of 2,500 automation runs. None of those changing produces an error. They produce wrong cards, lost briefs, or a silent stop at the end of the month. This check compares last week to this week and says what moved.

The baseline was reset on 20 September. The customer form changed, the card rules changed twice, and the order confirmation email changed. Compare against that week, not against anything earlier.

Steps

Run budget. Do NOT count rows on the n8n executions page, because the history is pruned at 168 hours and the older runs are simply gone. Take the execution id at the start of the month and the newest one, and subtract. That is the real number of runs. Divide by days elapsed, multiply by days in the month, and compare to 2,500. Write the projected number in the weekly line. Above 70%, tell Erwin the same day.
Every paid order has the right number of cards. In Shopify orders, list orders paid in the last 7 days. The right number is the total settled quantity across the order's real line items, so one package bought twice is two cards, and two different packages is two cards. Tips, fees and the VIP membership are not jobs and get no card. An order with fewer cards than that, or more, gets its number in the weekly line. Cards may be named with a suffix, "#1670-1 Video Ads", or without one when the order needs only a single card.
Every form landed somewhere. Check BOTH forms while the old one is still open: the new form's responses, which is what customers have reached since 19 September, and the old form's responses. List the last 7 days on each. Every response must be on a card or on a flag card on our sandbox board. One that is on neither is a lost customer brief. Note it and tell Jane.
The form has not changed. Open the new form in the Typeform editor and check the question list against last week's. The rule is not "has anything been renamed". The workflows read each question by its ref, which does not change when the wording does, so a reworded question is safe. What is not safe is a question that was deleted, a question whose type was changed, or a choice that was edited on the package questions, because the chasers read those choice labels. If any of those happened, say what and stop there until Erwin has seen it. Do not fix the form.
The products have not changed. In Shopify products, check the list against last week's. A new or renamed product now breaks two things, not one. It needs a line in the package map before its orders file correctly, and since 20 September the order confirmation email builds the customer's form link from an exact list of seven product titles, so a renamed product silently drops off that link and the customer arrives at the form with nothing filled in. Note the product name and tell Erwin.
The lists have not changed. On the board, check the list names against last week's. A renamed list splits one editor into two people in the measurement log, and a new editor list needs the editor added to the member map before the due date automation can put them on the card. An archived list still holding open cards gets flagged to Malik through Jane. Renamed CARDS are a different matter and are fine: a card counts as its package as long as the name still starts with it, so "Video Ads 2.0" and "Video Ads missing form" both read as Video Ads.
Chaser sent log. Open the sends sheet. Note any SEND FAILED rows, any order that reached the 96 hour escalation, and whether the escalation was acted on.
Customers who never answered. On the board, any card in "Order needs attention" older than 7 days is a paid customer who has had four reminders and still not sent a form. That needs a decision from a person this week, not another week of sitting. Send the list to Divine.
Log health. In the measurement log, summary tab: E1 carries the run date and the cutover sentence, and E2 carries the coverage line. "missing" must be 0, "truncated" must be no, and the row count must be higher than last week's.
The two by-editor tables. The same summary tab carries two. A51 grades the WHOLE ORDER, form received to fulfilled, which includes the copywriter's time and the delivery gap. H51 grades the EDITOR'S OWN WINDOW, latest assignment to last handover. They will not agree, and they are not meant to. Any conversation about an editor being late uses H51.
Credentials. On the n8n credentials page, look for any warning on Slack, Gmail, Shopify, Typeform, Trello or Google Sheets. A credential about to expire is a week of silent failure waiting to happen.
Post the weekly line as a comment on this task, and paste the same line into #noirlab-trello.

What is expected to move, so it does not read as drift

Response counts on the old form fall to nothing as the last pre-swap orders are delivered. That is the swap working, not a fault.
Cards for one order can now arrive together rather than one at a time, because a customer who says their packages are all for the same product gets every paid unit filled from one form.
Say where the evidence for each line came from, so a number can be checked later without doing the work again.

Definition of done

The weekly line is posted in both places, every "note it" above has a name or a number against it, and anything that needs a decision has been sent to the person who makes it. A projected run budget above 70% has reached Erwin.

Weekly line format

Weekly check <date>: runs projected <n> of 2500 / orders with wrong card count <n> / forms landed nowhere <n> / form changed yes or no / products changed <names or none> / lists changed <names or none> / send failures <n> / escalations <n> / attention cards over 7 days <n> / log missing <n> truncated yes or no / credential warnings <names or none>

Workflow links

Order intake
Form to card, new form
Form to card, old form
Customer chasers
Reconciliation sweep
Measurement log
Fulfilment turnaround log
Error alerts

title: E8 - Daily automation check (live board)
description:
Updated 20 September.

Recurrence: every working day, first thing Manila time. Time: 10 minutes.

Overview

Seven automations run around the clock on NoirLab's live Trello board: order intake, form to card for the old form, form to card for the new form, the customer chasers, the reconciliation sweep, the delivery measurement log and the fulfilment turnaround log. When one fails loudly, a message lands in Slack and an email reaches Divine. This check is for the other kind of failure: an automation that stops without an error, a run that never happened, a flag card nobody has picked up, or an alert nobody has read. Ten minutes a day turns "it went quiet" into "we noticed the same morning".

Three things to hold in your head:

Paid orders appear on the client's board by themselves, so a card waiting on a customer is normal and not a fault.
Flag cards never go to the client's board. They go to ours, and Jane owns every one of them.
Customers have been using the new form since 19 September. The old form stays open only until the last order placed before the swap is delivered, so both form to card workflows still matter.

Steps

Open the n8n executions page and look at the last 24 hours. Anything red: open it, note the workflow name and the error text, and check it is already in #noirlab-trello. If it is not, post it there in one line.
On the same page, count the rows for the workflows that run on a clock. The chasers run once an hour at minute 25, so 24 rows. The sweep runs every 6 hours, so 4 rows. The measurement log runs once, at 21:45 UTC. The turnaround log runs once a day. That is about 30 scheduled rows. The two form to card workflows and the intake have no fixed count, because they run when a customer or an order arrives. A missing row with no error is the thing you are here to catch. A quiet Slack channel and a broken Slack connection look identical, and this step is what tells them apart, so do it even when the channel is quiet.
Open the client board, list "Order needs attention". Cards waiting on a customer are normal, the reminders chase those on their own, so do not message anyone about them. Look for two things instead. First, a card that already has a brief written on it but is still sitting in this list. The reminders cannot read card descriptions, so that customer is being emailed for a form they have already sent. Move the card to "Orders" and put it in the daily line. Second, a brief that describes two products when the order paid for one. Leave a comment on the card saying which product we are doing, and tell Divine.
Open our own sandbox board, list "Order needs attention". This is where flag cards actually are. Most of them hold the only copy of a paying customer's brief and the client cannot see it. Anything older than 24 hours goes to Jane by name. Two flags mean the opposite of the rest, so read the name before you act: REVISION ON WORK IN PROGRESS means the customer's request is already on the card as a comment, so it does not need filing by hand and putting it on again would start a second clock. FORM ON CARD IN PROGRESS means the card was left alone on purpose because someone is working on it.
Open the divine@noirlab.io inbox. Any chaser escalation or failure alert that is unread and older than one day, message Divine.
Open the measurement log, summary tab, cell E1. The date must be today's. The log runs at 21:45 UTC, which is 05:45 the next morning in Manila, so by the time you look the newest run is dated today. If it still shows yesterday, the log did not run.
On the client board, look at the editor lists, the ones ending (VE), (AV) or (IE). Every card moved into one must have a due date and the editor as a member. One without either means the due date automation failed quietly, so note the card. Cards that were already sitting there before 9 September have no due date on purpose. Four clocks have been live since 10 September, so a due date that is not three days away is not a fault: new work is 3 calendar days, a customer revision is 2 calendar days, work sent back by review is 24 hours, and the senior editor's own review is 24 hours. The first two end at 23:59 UTC and count weekends. The last two move off a weekend to the same time on Monday.
Look at the two Creative Strategist lists on the same board. Since 19 September a scripted brief goes to one of them automatically, English to one list and German to the other, with the copywriter added to the card and a 24 hour due date. These are not editor lists, so they are not part of step 7, but a scripted card sitting in one of them with no member and no due date is the same kind of silent failure and goes in the daily line.
Post the daily line as a comment on this task.

Definition of done

The daily line is posted, and anything red, missing, unowned or unread has been sent to the person who owns it the same day. Noticing is not done. Sending is done.

Daily check <date>: red runs <n> / missing scheduled runs <n> / briefed cards not moved <n> / two-product briefs <n> / sandbox flags over 24h <n> / inbox unread <n> / log updated yes or no / editor cards missing due <n> / copywriter cards missing due <n>

The six workflows
W1, order in. Shopify order created. Log it, open a pending record, wait for the form. About 90 a month.
W2, form in and build the card. Typeform response. Match to the pending order, copy the package template, add the order number, paste the brief, strip client contacts, place it in the strategist column. About 90 a month.
W3, exceptions. No match, or an order with no form. Route to an exception list and alert. About 20 a month.
W4, chasers. Scheduled daily. Find orders with no form, send at 24 hours, 72 hours and 7 days, log every send, escalate to Carolina. About 30 plus sends.
W5, stage logging. The Trello board, polled rather than pushed. Write stage timestamps into the measurement log. About 360 polled, 700 or more pushed.
W6, EOD and dashboard. Scheduled daily. Compose the EOD numbers, refresh the dashboard tabs. About 60.
Roughly 650 to 900 executions a month against a 2,500 ceiling.

Three decisions inside that
W1 and W2 stay separate. The order and the form arrive at different times and either can come first. One workflow assuming order-then-form drops every late-form case, which is the exact failure we are fixing.
W5 polls, it does not subscribe. A Trello webhook fires on every move, comment, edit and attachment, which is unpredictable on a board this busy. Polling every two hours gives predictable volume and timestamps accurate to two hours, fine when we measure in days.
W2 suppresses the customer notification when it marks the order fulfilled. The one step that can produce a customer-visible failure. Test it on a single live order before it goes near the real board.

Two parts: the topline strategy, which says what we're actually solving and why in that order, and the execution plan, which says what happens week by week. Divine showed the founders an example of this on the 3 August call and told them they'd receive one once work starts.

Steps
Write the topline strategy: the problem, the sequencing, and the reasoning for that order.
Build the execution plan week by week across the first 30 days.
Hold days 31 to 90 at phase level only, since fixing them now would lock decisions before the baseline data arrives.
Make sure it agrees with the kickoff agenda, so the founders aren't reading two different versions of the priorities.
Hand it to Divine to present.

Suggested owner
Erwin · Divine (presents)

Inputs / prerequisites
30-60-90 plan, sections 4 and 5
Kickoff agenda

Definition of done
One document covering both parts, first 30 days at week level, days 31 to 90 at phase level, and Divine holding it to present.

⚠️ Divine used the words "operating strategy" with the founders and showed them an example. Title the deliverable something they'll recognise, whatever the task is called internally.

Source: Ops discussion 3 August 19:49 · 30-60-90 Plan §4 (Why the Plan Is Sequenced This Way) · §5 (The 30-60-90 Day Plan)

Blockers
Reach out to Erwin first. Escalate to Divine if it's a scope, client, or commercial question.

✅ Delivered, 18 August

Two pages instead of one document, because the client should not read our internal reasoning.

Topline Strategy — client-facing. Eight sections: the approach, what changes, week by week, the work and who does it, what stays the same, measuring, what we need from you, and day 30. Not yet released or sent.
The First 30 Days — internal master. Background, the workstream chart, the seven tasks, and week by week split into the work against what finishes each week.

The seven delivery tasks E1 to E7 came out of this and are live in this list.

Three things that differ from the definition of done above.

Days 31 to 90 are not at phase level. Month 2 is named as two items, automatic assignment and editor payments, both gated on the team sheet. Days 61 to 90 are not covered. Deliberate: the day-30 cutover decision determines them, so writing phases now would commit us before the baseline exists.
The client page is titled "Topline Strategy", not "Operating Strategy". The caveat above asked for the words the founders heard on 3 August. Say if you want it renamed.
Jane presents it, not Divine. Jane took over all client comms on 18 August. The page byline still reads "Prepared by Divine Origines, Fractional COO, with the implementation team", which is correct for the client, since Jane is never named to them.

We can't name most of them yet, which is why this task is about scheduling rather than running.

Steps
Chase the roster: name, role, location, working hours, and whether each person is full-time, part-time or paid per order.
Work out the overlap windows. The editors sit in the Philippines and wider Asia, the strategist and intake sit in Europe, so there's no single hour that suits everyone.
Book a short session with each person, sequenced to follow the order journey rather than by seniority.
Book the senior editor and the creative strategist first, since both stages are named as where time gets lost.
Add a subtask per person once the names exist, so each session can be tracked and its notes attached.

Jane (schedules) · Divine and Jane (run the sessions)

Team roster with names, roles, locations and hours
Kickoff held, so the team knows who Divine is before she books time with them

Every person on the delivery team has a session in the calendar, with a subtask each, sequenced along the order journey.

⚠️ The founders should introduce Divine to the team before she books anything. Booking cold reads as an audit, and one team member has already been named on a call as a performance concern.

A manual process is where second-hand accounts go thin, and the person doing it has workarounds they have stopped noticing.

Watch her process a live order end to end, including one that is mid-flight.
Time each step, so the twice-daily batch delay is measured rather than estimated.
Note every workaround, every place she leaves the board to chase someone, and anything she does that Malik did not mention.
Write up the process end to end and send it back through Malik for her to correct.

Malik has set up the session

Shopify admin, as a staff account with orders, products, customers, discounts and analytics. Needed for order volume, product mix, average order value, repeat rate, refunds, the customer notification setup and the VIP discount rules.

contact@noirlab.io, shared or delegated. Needed for customer enquiries, complaints and delivery correspondence.

THE 13 STEPS
1. Confirm payment in Stripe (plan or PIF). Bank transfer: Joel confirms first.
2. Check the GHL contact and sales notes, and do the partner check (co-owner or spouse on the contract, a different payer, a shared surname or business). Partner: every step for both, one task named for both.

6. Send the Batphone link (+partner).
7. Welcome email: Joel's automation drafts it in Rodney's Gmail. We don't send our own. (Open question: the plan says helper drafts, Jerold sends. Confirm.)
8. Invite to the next Wednesday kick-off (+partner). In the email just say Wednesday 5pm Melbourne time; don't ask for their city. Can't make it: 1:1 kick-off with Rodney (https://calendly.com/rodney-risewise/15min).

13. Milestone Tracker monitoring copy: automatic since 27 Oct.
Owner check: if Joel's post says "RODNEY HAS NO TASK", message Rodney (name, program, time zone).

COMMENT TEMPLATE (one comment per client)
New client: [name] (+ partner) | program | PIF or plan | closer
• Payment confirmed • GHL, notes and partner check • Notes in ClickUp and Slack • AI4B yes/no • Contract on file (start date) • Batphone link sent • Welcome email drafted (checked) • Kick-off invite for [date] • Skool invite • Trackers checked • 1:1 with Joel booked / not included • Tax invoice sent / not needed • Owner: Rodney has a task / told Rodney

title: Check Stripe transactions and handling Failed Payments
description:
Verify each failed Stripe payment and chase it from divine@ until it's paid or escalated.

FREQUENCY: Every weekday.
STATUS (7 Nov 2026): The alert runs by itself; the checks and emails are by hand. Payment watch (helper 3) will draft the emails after Joel answers (it needs a Stripe read-only key).

RUNS BY ITSELF
• Zapier posts each failed payment in GIM #risewise-failed-payments and tags Jerold.
• Stripe retries the card up to 4 times over 3 weeks.

WHAT YOU DO
1. Verify in Stripe (read only) that it failed and is still unpaid. Search by name and by email (the Stripe email can differ from the client's real one). Look for a second or guest payment.
2. Check Gmail (divine@ and Joel's), GHL, Slack and the client's Active task for a pause, extension, split, refund request or dispute. If there is one, stop and take it to Leanna or Joel.
3. Daily check of three kinds: failed (alerts, Stripe), overdue (past-due invoices, agreed pay-later dates) and missing (New Client posts with no payment, bank transfers Joel hasn't confirmed, deposits with a balance). Disputes go to Joel the same day.
4. Sequence (timing confirmed 7 Nov). Before every email, list every email the client uses (Stripe customer and card email, ClickUp, GHL, contract, onboarding post, Skool, the address they reply from; both partners if there are two) and look for a payment under each one and the name. Paid: no reminder (if it was paid on another Stripe record, tell Divine the same day). Not sure: ask first. Send to the email they use with us. Details on 6.5: Email 1 on Day 0 (which payment, amount, due date, Stripe pay link, invoice copy); Email 2 on Day 3 in the same thread, and tell the closer in RW Slack; Email 3 (final) on Day 7 with the 3-day access notice; Day 10 one message to Joel asking OK to pause access. Wording in SOP 6.5. (Default timing set 7 Nov; use Divine's or Joel's if they set another.)
5. Label: Failed Payments, Second Follow-up, Final Reminder, Escalation, or Payment Reconciled.
6. Comment on the client's Active task in RiseWise ClickUp (date, stage, amount, link). The ClickUp Failed Payments list isn't used any more; Stripe is the record.

DONE WHEN
Every alert since the last check is verified and has the right email or is escalated, and the thread is labelled.

RULES
• The final reminder carries the 3-day access notice (old SOP wording). Actually pausing access needs Joel's OK.
• We have agreed to a short delay of a few days when a client asked (6 Nov). Splits, skips, pauses and extensions go to Joel.
• Claude never refunds, cancels or changes a plan, and never uses Charge customer. Disputes: never accept or submit evidence; Joel decides.
• CC joel@risewise.com.au on every chase email (confirmed 7 Nov 2026). Our own CC'd emails don't come back twice through the Google Admin copy (checked 7 Nov).

title: Won Client Onboarding + Send Tax Invoice
description:
Onboard every new client the same day they are won: 13 steps, including the partner and owner checks.

FREQUENCY: Each new client (about 3 to 4 a week), the same day.
STATUS (7 Nov 2026): Partly automatic. Joel's automation makes the milestone tracker, drafts the welcome email in Rodney's Gmail, creates the Notion row and the ClickUp tasks, and sends the contract. The rest is by hand. The new-client autopilot (helper 7) comes after Joel fixes his client-owner automation.

HOW YOU HEAR ABOUT A NEW CLIENT
• The closer's "New Client" post in RW #sales-team25
• Joel's posts in RW #client-onboarding-claude ("New LAUNCH client", "Contracts")
• RW #stripe-payments; bank transfers need Joel's confirmation
(The won-client Slack post misses clients, so don't rely on it.)

THE 13 STEPS
1. Confirm payment in Stripe (plan or PIF). Bank transfer: Joel confirms first.
2. Check the GHL contact and sales notes, and do the partner check (co-owner or spouse on the contract, a different payer, a shared surname or business). Partner: every step for both, one task named for both.
3. Add the sales notes to the Active task and the Slack thread.
4. Check if they bought the AI4B playbook (GHL, Stripe). If yes, the AI4B Skool too.
5. Check the contract post; note any "no Program Start Date".
6. Send the Batphone link (+partner).
7. Welcome email: Joel's automation drafts it in Rodney's Gmail. We don't send our own. (Open question: the plan says helper drafts, Jerold sends. Confirm.)
8. Invite to the next Wednesday kick-off (+partner). In the email just say Wednesday 5pm Melbourne time; don't ask for their city. Can't make it: 1:1 kick-off with Rodney (https://calendly.com/rodney-risewise/15min).
9. Invite to Skool (+partner).
10. Check the ClickUp Active task: program, payment terms, start and end dates, partner. Tick Stripe Subs only for payment plans.
11. 1:1 with Joel if the contract includes it: offer his times (divine@ Google Calendar) and book a Zoom with its own link.
12. Receipt and tax invoice for PIF clients (made by hand; Stripe receipts are off). Attach both files to the draft (SOP 6.6).
13. Milestone Tracker monitoring copy: automatic since 27 Oct.
Owner check: if Joel's post says "RODNEY HAS NO TASK", message Rodney (name, program, time zone).

COMMENT TEMPLATE (one comment per client)
New client: [name] (+ partner) | program | PIF or plan | closer
• Payment confirmed • GHL, notes and partner check • Notes in ClickUp and Slack • AI4B yes/no • Contract on file (start date) • Batphone link sent • Welcome email drafted (checked) • Kick-off invite for [date] • Skool invite • Trackers checked • 1:1 with Joel booked / not included • Tax invoice sent / not needed • Owner: Rodney has a task / told Rodney

DONE WHEN
All 13 steps are done or checked for the client (and partner), Rodney owns the client, and the comment is posted.

WHAT YOU DO

4. Sequence (timing confirmed 7 Nov). Before every email, list every email the client uses (Stripe customer and card email, ClickUp, GHL, contract, onboarding post, Skool, the address they reply from; both partners if there are two) and look for a payment under each one and the name. Paid: no reminder (if it was paid on another Stripe record, tell Divine the same day). Not sure: ask first. Send to the email they use with us. Details on 6.5: Email 1 on Day 0 (which payment, amount, due date, Stripe pay link, invoice copy); Email 2 on Day 3 in the same thread, and tell the closer in RW Slack; Email 3 (final) on Day 7 with the 3-day access notice; Day 10 one message to Joel asking OK to pause access. Wording in SOP 6.5. (Default timing set 7 Nov; use Divine's or Joel's if they set another.)
5. Label: Failed Payments, Second Follow-up, Final Reminder, Escalation, or Payment Reconciled.
6. Comment on the client's Active task in RiseWise ClickUp (date, stage, amount, link). The ClickUp Failed Payments list isn't used any more; Stripe is the record.

New client: [name] (+ partner) | program | PIF or plan | closer
• Payment confirmed • GHL, notes and partner check • Notes in ClickUp and Slack • AI4B yes/no • Contract on file (start date) • Batphone link sent • Welcome email drafted (checked) • Kick-off invite for [date] • Skool invite • Trackers checked • 1:1 with Joel booked / not included • Tax invoice sent / not needed • Owner: Rodney has a task / told Rodney

title: Check Stripe transactions and handling Failed Payments
description:
Verify each failed Stripe payment and chase it from divine@ until it's paid or escalated.

FREQUENCY: Every weekday.
STATUS (7 Nov 2026): The alert runs by itself; the checks and emails are by hand. Payment watch (helper 3) will draft the emails after Joel answers (it needs a Stripe read-only key).

RUNS BY ITSELF
• Zapier posts each failed payment in GIM #risewise-failed-payments and tags Jerold.
• Stripe retries the card up to 4 times over 3 weeks.

WHAT YOU DO
1. Verify in Stripe (read only) that it failed and is still unpaid. Search by name and by email (the Stripe email can differ from the client's real one). Look for a second or guest payment.
2. Check Gmail (divine@ and Joel's), GHL, Slack and the client's Active task for a pause, extension, split, refund request or dispute. If there is one, stop and take it to Leanna or Joel.
3. Daily check of three kinds: failed (alerts, Stripe), overdue (past-due invoices, agreed pay-later dates) and missing (New Client posts with no payment, bank transfers Joel hasn't confirmed, deposits with a balance). Disputes go to Joel the same day.
4. Sequence (timing confirmed 7 Nov). Before every email, list every email the client uses (Stripe customer and card email, ClickUp, GHL, contract, onboarding post, Skool, the address they reply from; both partners if there are two) and look for a payment under each one and the name. Paid: no reminder (if it was paid on another Stripe record, tell Divine the same day). Not sure: ask first. Send to the email they use with us. Details on 6.5: Email 1 on Day 0 (which payment, amount, due date, Stripe pay link, invoice copy); Email 2 on Day 3 in the same thread, and tell the closer in RW Slack; Email 3 (final) on Day 7 with the 3-day access notice; Day 10 one message to Joel asking OK to pause access. Wording in SOP 6.5. (Default timing set 7 Nov; use Divine's or Joel's if they set another.)
5. Label: Failed Payments, Second Follow-up, Final Reminder, Escalation, or Payment Reconciled.
6. Comment on the client's Active task in RiseWise ClickUp (date, stage, amount, link). The ClickUp Failed Payments list isn't used any more; Stripe is the record.

DONE WHEN
Every alert since the last check is verified and has the right email or is escalated, and the thread is labelled.

RULES
• The final reminder carries the 3-day access notice (old SOP wording). Actually pausing access needs Joel's OK.
• We have agreed to a short delay of a few days when a client asked (6 Nov). Splits, skips, pauses and extensions go to Joel.
• Claude never refunds, cancels or changes a plan, and never uses Charge customer. Disputes: never accept or submit evidence; Joel decides.
• CC joel@risewise.com.au on every chase email (confirmed 7 Nov 2026). Our own CC'd emails don't come back twice through the Google Admin copy (checked 7 Nov).

WHAT YOU DO
1. Verify in Stripe (read only) that it failed and is still unpaid. Search by name and by email (the Stripe email can differ from the client's real one). Look for a second or guest payment.

4. Sequence (timing confirmed 7 Nov). Before every email, list every email the client uses (Stripe customer and card email, ClickUp, GHL, contract, onboarding post, Skool, the address they reply from; both partners if there are two) and look for a payment under each one and the name. Paid: no reminder (if it was paid on another Stripe record, tell Divine the same day). Not sure: ask first. Send to the email they use with us. 5. Label: Failed Payments, Second Follow-up, Final Reminder, Escalation, or Payment Reconciled.
