🧩 Call Type ⏱ Duration 👤 Who It's For 📍 When to Use
🧠 30-Min Coaching 30 mins Clients requesting extra support Only when specifically requested and after referral to Alana or Rodney
📈 1:1 Strategy Session 30–45 mins Launch PIF / contract-based clients If included in contract
🚀 1:1 Onboarding 45 mins PIF clients At start of program
🔥 Kickstarter Custom Intensive 45–60 mins Kickstarter clients After Group Kick-Off
📊 Momentum Custom Intensive 45–60 mins Momentum clients After Group Kick-Off
👥 Group Kick-Off Sessions
Weekly Schedule (Melbourne Time):
🗓 Tuesday – 9:30 AM
🗓 Wednesday – 5:00 PM
🔁 Standard Client Flow (Launch)
Group Kick-Off → Group Glo Up

➡️ Schedule 1:1 Kick-Off with Rodney

➡️ Follow up with Rodney to confirm once the 1:1 Kick-Off has been completed

Must be created via Zoom
Generate a unique meeting link

Duplicate existing Google Calendar event
Reuse same Zoom link

1️⃣ Identify client program + entitlement
2️⃣ Confirm correct session type

4️⃣ Offer / confirm schedule

     ➡️ 1:1 → Zoom + Calendar

7️⃣ Log session in ClickUp
8️⃣ Update status after session

➡️ Simply update the task (client name) status in ClickUp

📩 Always use Divine’s email for comms (centralised trail) | CC closers and Elise 
🎯 Double check program before scheduling
⚡ Book sessions ASAP after request
🧼 Clean tracking = smoother ops and reporting

🏷️ Task Name
Check Database: Update Scale & Coaching Tracker
🎯 Overview
Divine is responsible for maintaining and updating the Scale & Coaching Calls Tracker to ensure accurate attendance records for all coaching and scale sessions.
This process helps the team:
 ✅ Monitor client participation
 ✅ Track coaching engagement
 ✅ Maintain organized attendance records
 ✅ Ensure coaching data is updated weekly
✅ Procedure
1️⃣ Open the Tracker
📂 Go to:
 Scale & Coaching Calls Tracker 
2️⃣ Get and Update Attendance Report
📂 Open the attendance records from:
 Attend Onboarding & Coaching Sessions 
Use the meeting screenshots and attendance tracking to verify client participation.
🗓️ Update attendance based on the session date only.
⚠️ Important Notes:
 The tracker does not require specific session names 
 There may be multiple coaching sessions in one day 
 Once a client attends at least one session on that date, mark them as: 
 ✅ Attended 
Only one attendance tag is needed per client per date.
🎯 Coaching Sessions Included
🏆 Win of the Week w/ Rodney
 ❓ Q&A w/ Joel
 📚 Coaching & Scale Sessions w/ Joel
 🎨 Fashion Design w/ Alana
 📖 Brandbook Review w/ Rodney
3️⃣ Add New Weekly Columns if Needed
➕ If no more attendance columns are available:
 Add 4 new columns manually 
 🗓️ Label each column with the correct weekly session dates 
4️⃣ Double Check Entries
🔍 Ensure:
 Correct spelling of client names 
 Attendance is marked under the correct date 
 No attendees are missed 
 Duplicate entries are avoided 
📆 Weekly Tasks
5️⃣ Identify Inactive Coaching Clients
🔍 Review the tracker weekly to identify clients who have:
 Missed coaching calls for 2 or more consecutive weeks 
 Update status to Inactive (formerly Endorsed) 
📧 Trigger email check-ins for inactive clients to:
 Re-engage them 
 Check their progress 
 Encourage them to attend upcoming coaching sessions 
 Book a 1:1 with the coaches

⏳ Update the tracker immediately after each coaching session

title: Set up Elise automated booking confirmation email for WhatsApp calls
description:
Elise asked if we can send an automated confirmation email when someone books a call, because some people worry it hasn’t been confirmed/booked properly.
Goal
Ensure every booking triggers a confirmation email.
Requirements
Send an automatic confirmation email immediately after a call is booked.
Confirmation should clearly state that the meeting is a phone call via WhatsApp (so the client doesn’t expect a Zoom link).
Steps
Identify the booking tool used for Elise’s calls (ex: Calendly, Acuity, etc.) and where confirmation emails are configured.
Confirm whether the tool supports:
Native confirmation email templates, or
An integration/automation (ex: Zapier/Make).
Create/update the confirmation email template:
Subject line and body copy that confirms the booking.
Call type note: “Phone call via WhatsApp”.
Test end-to-end by creating a test booking and verifying the email is received and wording is correct.
Share the final template copy and where it’s configured for future edits.

title: Schedule Joel's Coaching Calls & Kickoffs
description:
📅 SOP: Scheduling Joel’s Coaching Calls & Kick-Off Sessions
🔁 Frequency: Daily
👤 Owner: Divine / Operations
📩 Primary Channel: Divine’s RiseWise email (for clear communication footprint)
🎯 Purpose
Ensure all Joel coaching calls, 1:1 sessions, and kick-off sessions are:
Scheduled correctly
Communicated clearly
Tracked consistently
📌 Call Types

🧩 Call Type ⏱ Duration 👤 Who It's For 📍 When to Use
🧠 30-Min Coaching 30 mins Clients requesting extra support Only when specifically requested and after referral to Alana or Rodney
📈 1:1 Strategy Session 30–45 mins Launch PIF / contract-based clients If included in contract
🚀 1:1 Onboarding 45 mins PIF clients At start of program
🔥 Kickstarter Custom Intensive 45–60 mins Kickstarter clients After Group Kick-Off
📊 Momentum Custom Intensive 45–60 mins Momentum clients After Group Kick-Off
👥 Group Kick-Off Sessions
Weekly Schedule (Melbourne Time):
🗓 Tuesday – 9:30 AM
🗓 Wednesday – 5:00 PM
🔁 Standard Client Flow (Launch)
Group Kick-Off → Group Glo Up
⚠️ If Client Misses Kick-Off
➡️ Schedule 1:1 Kick-Off with Rodney
➡️ Send email template with Rodney’s booking link
➡️ Follow up with Rodney to confirm once the 1:1 Kick-Off has been completed
⚙️ Scheduling Rules
🎥 For ALL 1:1 Sessions with Joel
Must be created via Zoom
Generate a unique meeting link
🔁 For Kick-Off Sessions
Duplicate existing Google Calendar event
Reuse same Zoom link
❌ Exception: 1:1 PIF Onboarding (create new)
🧩 Process Flow
1️⃣ Identify client program + entitlement
2️⃣ Confirm correct session type
3️⃣ Reach out via Divine’s RiseWise email
4️⃣ Offer / confirm schedule
5️⃣ Set up session:
     ➡️ 1:1 → Zoom + Calendar
     ➡️ Kick-Off → Duplicate Calendar event
6️⃣ Send calendar invite
7️⃣ Log session in ClickUp
8️⃣ Update status after session
📊 Tracking Requirement
📍 After each session:
➡️ Simply update the task (client name) status in ClickUp
🧠 Key Reminders
📩 Always use Divine’s email for comms (centralised trail)
🎯 Double check program before scheduling
⚡ Book sessions ASAP after request
🧼 Clean tracking = smoother ops and reporting

title: Investigate duplicate Risewise bookings creating two Google Calendar events
description:
Abbey reported that when a Risewise Gameplan session is booked, it is now creating duplicate bookings in her Google Calendar (two events side by side). This started within the last week and has never happened before.

What Abbey is seeing
Booking a Gameplan session sends an invite to her Google Calendar and creates two calendar events for the same booking.
The invite is being sent to: abbeyrenee coaching @ gmail.com (as shown in the screenshot).
Abbey has not made any changes on her end.
She is hesitant to delete one of the events because it may show as cancelled/declined to the client.

Goal
Identify the cause and stop duplicate events without impacting clients.

Suggested checks
Verify the booking system is not connected to Google Calendar more than once (duplicate integrations, multiple automations, multiple calendars selected).
Check for recent changes or updates in the booking platform or Google Calendar integration settings.
Confirm whether events are being written to multiple calendars (primary plus another calendar).
Attempt to reproduce with a test booking and capture timestamps and settings.
Provide Abbey with a safe mitigation (if any) that will not send cancellation signals to clients.

Evidence
Screenshots attached in this request show the message thread and calendar examples with side-by-side bookings.

title: Set up two-week inactivity trigger for Rise Wise Milestone Tracker
description:
Request
Elise asked when the “two weeks inactive in the Rise Wise Milestone tracker” trigger will be active. It is being mentioned on onboarding and kickoff calls, but it is not actually set up yet.

Background
The existing process/notifications were misunderstood as “2 weeks not attending coaching sessions”; Slack notifications for that were turned off to avoid unnecessary mentions.
We still need a true Milestone Tracker inactivity trigger based on last milestone update or last opened activity being more than 2 weeks ago.

Goal
Create an automated way (likely in the tracker sheet) to flag clients as inactive after 14 days, so the team can confidently reach out.

Tasks
Confirm the definition of “inactive” for the Milestone Tracker (last updated vs last opened, and which fields/events count).
Map the cleanest setup in the tracker sheet (logic + fields needed).
Implement the script/automation to detect >14 days inactivity.
Define the output: where the alert appears (sheet column, list, Slack/EOC notification, etc.).
Test with sample client records and validate the trigger timing.
Share the timeframe and how it works with Elise and Joel.

Reference
See attached screenshot of Elise’s message + context.

title: Fix FC pipeline confirmation page video redirect
description:
Request
Victoria found an issue in the FC pipeline: after booking, the funnel directs to the “thanks for booking a GP” video/page when it should direct to the “thanks for booking a FC” video/page.

What was observed
In GHL, the confirmation page appears to be set to FC.
When booking through the funnel (Victoria tested by booking herself), it plays the wrong video.

Suspected area
Joel noted it may be in calendar reroute settings.

Tasks
Reproduce the issue by booking through the FC funnel.
Check funnel step settings for the post-booking/confirmation redirect.
Check calendar reroute settings (and any workflow/trigger that changes the thank-you page).
Update redirect so FC bookings always land on the FC thank-you video/page.
Re-test end-to-end to confirm the correct page/video displays.

Reference
See attached screenshot from Victoria’s message for context.

title: Set up Slack EOC notification and commission tracking for Elise
description:
Context
From the Slack thread (screenshots attached):
Elise will manage off-boarding as usual.
Elise should be notified in Slack when a client is about 1 month out from finishing Risewise so she can:
check in,
offer coaching calls,
attempt an upsell after the accelerate call a month later.
Elise will collect 5% of cash collected on deals she closed, calculated at end of term.
We need a consistent way to track deals closed by Elise and send her a monthly figure so she can invoice.
Elise is OK aligning to the existing sales-team commission process (Divine’s proposed cutoff structure: 1–15 and 16–30/31); she originally suggested a 27th-of-month cutoff as an option.

What to build
Slack notification automation
Trigger: when a Risewise client is 1 month from their end date / term ending.
Action: send a Slack ping/notification to Elise with enough client context for follow-up.
Confirm where the “term end date” lives (ClickUp field, CRM, spreadsheet, etc.) and use that as the source of truth.
Elise commission tracking + monthly reporting
Track: which deals were closed by Elise.
Calculate: 5% of cash collected for those deals during the reporting period.
Reporting cadence: monthly.
Cutoff: implement the sales-team cutoff structure (1–15 and 16–30/31), unless the team decides to switch to Elise’s 27th cutoff.
Output: a monthly figure (and ideally a simple breakdown by deal/client) that can be sent to Elise for invoicing.
Process alignment (handoffs for accelerate calls)
Keep the current SOP clean:
Divine continues owning follow-ups for people who miss the accelerate call.
Once someone attends and is ready to book with Elise, handoff to Elise.
Ensure the automation does not create duplicate outreach or conflicting ownership.

Acceptance criteria
Slack ping to Elise reliably triggers at the 1-month-to-end point for every applicable Risewise client.
There is a repeatable way to identify Elise-closed deals and compute 5% of cash collected per reporting period.
Monthly number can be produced quickly (ideally automated or templated), with a clear cutoff definition.

Screenshots
See task attachments (from the request) for the exact Slack thread context.

title: Create workflow to exclude Offer Made clients from marketing blasts
description:
Goal
Prevent leads/clients in Closer Pipeline, Offer Made stage from receiving marketing blasts (e.g., when Joel sends marketing emails), then automatically allow marketing again once they leave Offer Made.
Context
From the team discussion (see attached screenshot):
Leads tagged “onboarded” or “scale onboarded” are already excluded from marketing emails.
The request is to also exclude leads while they are in Offer Made, without requiring the sales team to manually apply/remove tags.

Proposed workflow (automation)
Define the exclusion mechanism
Use a single tag such as “Do Not Market” (or a more specific tag like “Do Not Market - Offer Made”) that is used as an exclusion filter in marketing lists/blasts.
Automation when entering Offer Made
Trigger: Opportunity/lead is moved to Closer Pipeline, Offer Made.
Action: Apply the chosen exclusion tag.
Automation when leaving Offer Made (remove exclusion)
Trigger: Opportunity/lead moves out of Offer Made to any other stage.
Action: Remove the exclusion tag.
Guardrails / exceptions
Ensure we do not remove exclusion if they also have tags that should keep them excluded permanently (e.g., onboarded / scale onboarded).
Confirm the “Won/Closed” automation already applies the correct onboarding tag(s) and that those tags are part of the marketing exclusion rules.
Validation checklist
Test lead enters Offer Made: gets exclusion tag and no longer receives marketing.
Test lead moves to Won: exclusion tag removed (if desired) but onboarded tag(s) keep them excluded.
Test lead moves to Not Won / Nurture: exclusion tag removed so they return to the marketing pool.
Confirm list filters used by Joel exclude the correct tags.

Deliverables
Documented workflow steps (where the automation lives and how it’s configured).
Confirmation of which tag name will be used.
Confirmation that removal of the tag on stage change is feasible and working.

title: Conduct the Discovery Call
description:
This step always stays with Divine. Use the call to understand the business, identify pain points, and confirm fit.
Instructions:
Use the Discovery Call Information Checklist below to guide the conversation
Listen more than you talk
Take notes or debrief immediately after
At the end of the call: if fit → tell them proposal is coming in 2–3 days. If not a fit → close warmly
Update CRM status immediately: Proposal Stage or Not a Fit

Discovery Call Information Checklist
Use this checklist to guide every discovery call or chat with a potential client. The goal is to gather enough information to craft a tailored proposal and 30-60-90 Day Business Plan. You do not need to ask every question word for word — let the conversation flow naturally and fill in the gaps.
About the Business
What is the business name and what do they do?
What industry or niche are they in?
How long have they been operating?
What is their current monthly revenue (approximate)?
How big is the team — who does what?
How many clients do they have, what type, and what do they charge?
Where are their leads currently coming from?
About the Founder
What does the founder's day-to-day currently look like?
What are they best at — where should their time be protected?
What are they doing right now that they shouldn't be?
What do they want to focus on in the next 90 days?
Delivery & Operations
How is work currently delivered — who owns what?
What tools and systems are they using (ClickUp, Notion, Slack, GHL, etc.)?
Are there existing SOPs or documented processes — or is everything in someone's head?
What breaks down most often in delivery?
How are clients currently updated and communicated with?
Pain Points
What is the biggest operational challenge right now?
What is slowing the business down the most?
What has already been tried to fix it — and what happened?
If nothing changes in 90 days, what happens to the business?
Growth & Goals
What does the business look like in 12 months if everything goes right?
What is the main growth opportunity they are not yet capitalizing on?
Are there any upcoming launches, campaigns, or big client opportunities in the pipeline?
What would success look like at the end of 90 days?
Team & Hiring
Are there current gaps in the team — roles they need but don't have?
Have they hired VAs or contractors before — how did that go?
What kind of support have they had before and what didn't work?
Budget & Commitment
Have they worked with an agency or fractional COO before?
Do they have a budget range in mind for this kind of support?
Are they ready to start immediately or is there a timeline?
Red Flags to Listen For
Vague answers about revenue or team structure
No clear pain point — just "I want to grow"
Has tried many solutions and nothing worked — without understanding why
Not willing to give access or share information
Looking for someone to do everything for a very low budget
Unclear on what they want to focus on
After the Call
Update CRM status immediately — Proposal Stage or Not a Fit
Debrief or take notes right after the call while it's fresh
Tag RA to begin the proposal and 30-60-90 Day Plan within 24 hours

description:
Goal
Complete and test the technical GHL updates from the Ben x Divine catch-up on October 21, then submit a recorded walkthrough for our review.
GHL updates needed
1. New-lead automation: fix first
Automation > Workflows: Fix and publish the existing new-lead workflow so every form submission receives an instant email + SMS.
Add a follow-up when the lead does not reply. Stop the no-reply sequence when they respond or book. Use the existing approved follow-up timing; flag it if none is defined.
2. Pipeline stages + follow-up sequences
Opportunities > Pipelines: Improve the Leadly Sales pipeline with No Answer, Follow Up, Rescheduled, No Show, and Cancelled stages.
Automation > Workflows: Connect each stage to its own appropriate SMS + email sequence, including booking links where relevant.
Ensure replies, rebookings, and stage changes stop outdated sequences and prevent duplicate messages.
3. Booking links, time zones + sender name
Settings > Domains + Calendars + Automation > Workflows: Replace generic GHL booking links in emails with the correct branded Leadly landing-page/booking link. Test the full booking flow.
Calendars > Calendar Settings + Notifications: Show appointment times in the lead's local time zone while keeping Ben's internal calendar on Eastern time. Test Eastern and California/Pacific time, including daylight-saving handling.
Settings > Email Services + Calendars > Notifications: Use GRACE, not Divine, as the consistent sender name across emails and calendar notifications.
Booking-link reference: Emails currently show the GHL link; they should use the landing page.


4. Appointment status handling
Calendars > Appointments + Automation > Workflows: Check and fix how Confirmed, Unconfirmed, and No Show statuses are updated and used by automations. Do not treat an unconfirmed appointment as cancelled.
Ensure status changes trigger the correct follow-up without duplicate or misleading messages.
Calendars > Notifications: Verify that video-call appointments include the correct existing meeting link and call details in confirmations.
5. Proposal follow-up automation
Automation > Workflows: Build the 48-hour follow-up for unanswered proposals when a lead enters the proposal stage.
Stop the follow-up if the lead responds or the opportunity advances/closes.
Add the approval step after the follow-up using the documented approval routing. If the approver/action is undefined, prepare that branch and flag it before activation.
Build notes
Update existing workflows where possible; avoid duplicate automations.
Keep current alternative-time wording unchanged until Ben confirms his preference. No copy decision is required to complete the technical fixes above.
If domain access, integration access, follow-up timing, or approval routing is missing, report the exact input needed and continue the other updates.
This task covers technical configuration and testing only, not manual lead follow-up, individual contact cleanup, or the broader GHL backlog.
GHL menu names may vary by version.

title: Watch and read Launch Build Agent Updates
description:
Launch Build Agent Updates

Hi team, all core scenarios from Ric's list have been added and successfully tested. We can definitely present this to Ben now.

Here's what the agent can do, based on Ric's Priority 1 list:
- One asset + one copy = one ad. The basic build.
- One asset + multiple copy sets = multiple ads using the same asset.
- Multiple assets + shared or designated copy = one ad per concept, each with its own copy.
- Mixed images and videos in one launch = separate image and video ads.
- Placement sizes = one ad that shows the square version on feed and the vertical version on stories and reels.
- Multiple concepts with multiple sizes = 2 ads, not 6. Each concept gets its own ad set, same as how we build manually.
- Duplicate an existing ad into another ad set without creating new creatives.
- Add new ads to an existing ad set without creating a new campaign.

Before building anything, the agent posts a summary of what it will build, and the buyer has to reply "go" first. It also counts the expected ads and stops if the numbers don't match.

Everything the agent builds arrives PAUSED. It cannot activate ads, change budgets, or delete anything. Publishing stays with the media buyer. After checking the agent's work in Meta, the buyer just toggles the ad on.

Ric recommended we get these core scenarios stable first before moving to the common variations, and that's done. Some of the variations actually work already as a side effect of how we built it, like different landing pages per creative. The rest will be included in the next version once Ben approves:
- Create a new campaign from an approved reference ad set
- Schedule a future start date while keeping the build paused
- Instant Form ads
- Duplicate several ads as a group

Can you check these ad sets in StarD? All paused, all built by the agent:
Ad Set 1 - Copy variation + duplication
Ad Set 2 - Image + video
Ad Set 3 - Placement sizes, feed and stories/reels

One thing to decide during your review: the agent currently builds with all Advantage+ enhancements turned off, while your live ads run with about ten turned on. Let me know if you want the agent to match your settings or keep builds clean.

I know it's the weekend, but would it be okay to set up a quick call so I can walk you through everything? Or let me know when works for you. Fine on Monday too so you can rest this weekend.

Thank you!!

title: Review ClickUp restructure proposal
description:
Hi team, I’d like to recommend a small restructure for the Studio Nets ClickUp setup, especially for media buyers handling multiple ad accounts.

Right now, the structure is essentially:
1 Ad Account = 1 Folder
Then inside each folder:
Launches
Campaign Ops
Reports
Docs

This works when someone only handles a few accounts, but once a media buyer manages several accounts, it creates a lot of folder switching and makes it harder for them to see their overall priorities in one place.

This came up clearly during the call with Cheily. One of her main concerns was that she already has several tasks across multiple accounts, and it becomes difficult to quickly see:
what she needs to do today,
what is highest priority,
what is for later in the week, and
which tasks belong to which account.
Recommended Structure
Instead of: 1 Folder = 1 Ad Account
I recommend: 1 Folder = 1 Media Buyer
Example:
📁 Cheily
🚀 Launches
⚙️ Campaign Ops
📊 Reports
📄 Docs / Knowledge Hub

Then, we use a required Custom Field: Ad Account.
Example values:
FL MOR
PROPER V2
Gold
Green Dev
Green Green
ADB V2
ADB Energy
ADB SJ
Unlimited
GT V3
GS

This allows us to keep all of Cheily’s work in one operational area while still being able to filter and group tasks by ad account whenever needed. This would also make our work easier and centralized as we monitor their progress.
Suggested Task Fields
For operational tasks, I recommend requiring:
Ad Account — dropdown custom field
Priority
Due Date
Owner
Why I think this will work better
The main benefit is that the media buyer can work from one master queue instead of constantly switching between multiple ad account folders.
We can then create saved views such as:
My Work — This Week
Today / Urgent
By Ad Account
FL MOR
PROPER V2
GT V3
etc.

So for the media buyer, the workspace is organized around what type of work needs to be done, while for GIM we can still filter by Ad Account whenever we need account-level visibility or when reviewing an account with Ben.

For Docs, I suggest one Knowledge Hub under the media buyer folder, with subpages per ad account, as needed, instead of having a separate Docs list under every account.

Example:
📄 Knowledge Hub | Cheily
General Media Buyer SOPs
FL MOR
PROPER V2
Gold
ADB V2
GT V3
etc.

This is just a proposal for now. And one thing I’d like us to check before implementing this is whether any of the current automations, especially the AI Launch Workflow, depend on the existing Folder/List IDs. If yes, we should plan the migration carefully so we don’t break anything.

But operationally, I think this structure will be much more scalable and easier for media buyers who are handling many accounts.

title: T0.4 — Read and acknowledge the privacy rules in writing
description:
The single rule on this account that cannot be broken. Everything else is recoverable.

Ben told us media buyers must not be able to see one another, and he framed it as personal rather than operational. One message with two buyers on it and the trust is gone, with no way to earn it back.

The rules

One-to-one threads only. Every message to a buyer goes in their own thread. No group chats, no cc with two buyers, no "quick note to everyone." This applies to Ben as much as to us, so if he starts a group thread, we move it.
One ad account, one buyer. Never share an account across two people.
Buyers never see the roll-up. In the reporting template (T7) and both dashboards (T2, T9), each buyer sees only their own tab. The consolidated and comparison views stay with Ben and us. This is where the comparison data lives and it is the easiest place to leak by accident.
Winning creatives are distributed, never traded. They go into each buyer's own folder with the source stripped out, one way, curated by us (R3).
When in doubt, do not send it. Ask strategy first. A delayed message costs nothing. A wrong one costs the account.

Step by Step Process

Read the five rules above.
Read the working agreement once T3.7 is written.
Reply on this task confirming you have read and understood them. Written acknowledgement, not a thumbs up.

Done When

Written acknowledgement is posted on this task.

Executing this without the context means making sensible-looking choices that quietly break the thing the client cares most about. So orientation comes before execution, and it happens this week.

We are on day 2 of 30 and the client grades us weekly, so this is a two-day task, not a two-week one.

Step by Step Process

See subtasks T0.1 through T0.5. Do them in order. The recordings first, because everything else reads differently once you have heard him.

Done When

title: T2.2 — Walkthrough with Ben and capture the baseline
description:
Use a call Divine already has with him. Do not create a new meeting he has to find time for. If Friday does not work, early the following week is fine. The sheet does not wait for this.

Purpose

Two things happen here that cannot happen over email.

He is not a reader. On both calls he asked to be shown things rather than sent them, and a screen share is what moved him. A link sent Friday afternoon may sit unopened, and then the reason we pulled the dashboard forward to week 1 is lost.

More importantly, the baseline only exists in his head. It is not in Trello and not in Cheyli's reports. T11 on Aug 25 is built entirely on having it.

Step by Step Process

Screen share the v0 sheet. Do not talk over it, let him read it. Note which columns he reacts to and which he ignores, since that shapes what v1 prioritises in T9.
Point at the gaps openly. Where data is missing, that is information about the business, not a failure of the sheet.
Capture the baseline in his own words. Ask directly: from the day a client signs, how long until their campaign is live? And: how many clients have you lost in their first 60 days?
Take his number as stated. Do not correct it or refine it in the session. His own claim, in his words, is far harder for him to argue with at day 30 than a figure we calculated. T5 does the rigorous timing separately.
Write both numbers down where they can be found again, with the date and the fact that they came from him.
Ask what he wants to see in the sheet that is not there yet. That goes into T9.

Done When

Ben has been walked through the sheet, and the time-to-launch and 60-day churn numbers are recorded in his own words with the date attached.

title: T2.1 — Build and deliver the v0 sheet
description:

Step by Step Process

Pull source data: Cheyli's recent weekly reports and the Trello client database. If Trello access is blocked, use whatever Ben forwards under the T1 fallback.
Build one Google Sheet, a row per client, with these columns: client, budget, location, assigned buyer, landing page template type, latest CPL, latest spend, date of last report received.
Fill every cell you can. Where data is missing, mark it visibly rather than leaving it blank. The gaps are a finding worth showing him, not something to hide.
Label the file v0 in the title. Managing the expectation is part of the deliverable, not an apology.
Sanity check the numbers against two different sources where possible. A wrong CPL in front of him in week 1 costs more than a missing one.
Send it Friday with the weekly update (R1), with a one-line note that we will walk him through it live.

Done When

The v0 sheet exists, is populated from source data, is labeled v0, and has gone to Ben with Friday's update.

Get Ben's explicit sign-off on the SLA line specifically. It is the part he is most likely to quietly ignore.

title: T4 — SOP 2: Creative Request and Handoff Flow | Studio Nets
description:

Purpose

Every request task is assigned to a creative on creation. A limited member cannot build a view across lists and there are 13 Creative lists, so an unassigned request is invisible until someone opens the right list. Zeeshan produces 10 to 12 videos a day.
Naming convention. Blocked, see below.
Privacy rules acknowledged in writing by every buyer and every creative:
One to one only. No thread, task or list with two buyers on it.
Creatives never reference or name another buyer. Direct contact makes the creatives the only people who see across buyers. They are the bridge, so the rule sits with them.
Buyers never see the roll-up or any comparison view.
Set the review path for R1 so no client update goes out unreviewed.

Date order. DDMM or MMDD. 707V1 reads as 7 July to the team and 7 August to Ben and Cheily.
Leading zero. 707 and 0707 both appear today, so sorting breaks in Drive.

Request template built, the Creative list mechanism verified, the naming convention documented once the two gaps are settled, privacy rules acknowledged in writing by everyone, and the R1 review path agreed.

title: T3 — ClickUp Workspace and Guest Architecture | Studio Nets
description:
Owner: Jerold · Window: Jul 28 to Mon Aug 10 · Note: Cheily migrates on a date she agrees, not one she is given

Updated Aug 5. The access model changed twice since this was written. People come in as limited members on studionets.com addresses, not as guests on personal email. The folder unit is the ad account, not the buyer. Both are reflected below.

Purpose / Context

Ben named the same problem on both calls: work and conversation live in his head and across six platforms, with no project management tool he controls.

He also set an explicit constraint on July 27: media buyers must not be able to see one another. He raised it unprompted and framed it as personal, not operational. Slack fails this because every workspace member can see the member directory. The constraint is not negotiable.

We are building in Ben's own ClickUp account, not inside ours. Two reasons. His subcontractors are never inside our workspace, so the privacy rule cannot fail through a permissions mistake on our side. And the system stays his, which makes the day-90 handover clean.

Step by Step Process

Ben creates the ClickUp account and approves the seat cost. Done, T3.1.
Divine and the implementation team get access to his workspace. Done.
Test first. Verify what a test account can see before inviting a single real person. T3.2 covered guests, T23.5 covers limited members.
One folder per ad account, named as it appears in Business Manager. Thirteen folders, four lists each: Launches, Campaign Ops, Reports, Creative. Reassigning an account becomes a permission change rather than a rebuild, and no folder carries a person's name.
Invite as limited members, list level only. Never a folder, never a space. A limited member sees only what is shared with it.
Two people are never on the same list. Two people on one shared list see each other and no setting prevents it. The single written exception is the Creative list, which carries that folder's buyer and both creatives by design, because creatives are the one group already meant to see across buyers.
Statuses and custom fields come from [Template] New Ad Account. Apply the template, never hand-build them. Hand-built statuses land list-level instead of space-level and Founder views silently exclude that folder. That is what broke ADB SJ.
Custom fields taken from Cheily's client database: budget, location, radius, landing page, template type, assigned buyer, assigned creative.
No Channel on any location two people could both reach. Anyone on a location carrying a Channel can see and message everyone else on it.
Retire the two creative Slack channels as the route in. T3.6, rescoped Aug 5 to the Slack half only.
Migrate in this order: Tristan, then Bernardo, then Katy and Zeeshan. Cheily on a date she agrees. Muddasir is on hold by Ben's instruction and does not migrate.
The invite and the welcome message come from us, to each person individually. Buyers on Upwork, creatives on Slack. Never a broadcast.
Screenshot what a limited member sees and pass it to Divine. This is a deliverable to Ben, not an internal check. T3.8.
Write and pin the working agreement, per role. T3.7.

Done When

Access verified with zero cross-visibility, Tristan and Bernardo operating in ClickUp, account lists carrying budget, location and template type, the working agreement pinned, and the privacy screenshots sent to Ben.

It is manual on purpose. No integrations, no automation. Speed beats polish here.

Separating them means his calendar can never delay our week-1 win, but the baseline still gets captured rather than quietly skipped.

title: Social Media Outreach
description:
SOP: Social Media & UGC Outreach for Luminize
Overview
This SOP explains how to manage Luminize’s social media and UGC outreach using Meta Business Suite, Instagram, TikTok, Hyred.nl, and Getbarter.com.
The goal is to build a structured UGC outreach system where the team can source creators, contact them, review replies, approve barter deals, manage paid UGC, and track everything properly without needing Glenn to be involved in every small decision.
Main Goal
Build a repeatable outreach system for:
Barter collaborations
Paid UGC collaborations
Instagram creator outreach
TikTok creator outreach
Hyred.nl assignments
Getbarter.com barter campaigns
Partner Ads / Spark Ads content opportunities
Tools Required 
ClickUp
Luminize Outreach Tracker
Meta Business Suite
Instagram Inbox
TikTok
Luminize Custom GPT
Hyred.nl
Getbarter.com
Google Drive / Contract Folder
Email: contact@luminize.eu


Luminize Preferred Qualification for Influencer/Creator:
Influencer like this are perfect for UGC: 

This is exactly what we look for, her age, look, high quality video and voice are perfect for luminize.
Important Instructions from Glenn
1. Barter Deals
The team can decide on barter deals without asking Glenn every time, as long as the creator is reasonable and fits the Luminize target audience.
Check if the creator:
Looks mature enough and not too young
Has a suitable home, garden, stairway, or interior setup
Creates clean and usable videos
Has a profile that feels natural and trustworthy
Matches Luminize’s home, lighting, garden, or interior audience
The creator’s voice does not matter too much because the voice can be taken from other videos if needed.
2. Product Matching for Barter Deals
Use the creator’s profile and home setup to decide which product to recommend.
Recommended product matching:
 
Creator Profile / Home Setup Recommended Product
Nice house or interior Rechargeable cube with remote
Nice stairway Rechargeable cube with motion sensor
Nice garden Solar light
Modern new-build house 220v or rechargeable outdoor wall light
Outdoor lifestyle / exterior home setup Outdoor wall light or solar light 
3. Paid UGC
Luminize has around €1,200 monthly budget for high-quality paid UGC videos.
For paid UGC:
Product focus should be discussed monthly with Glenn
Paid creators should send their invoice to contact@luminize.eu
Luminize pays after the content has been received
Paid UGC should be reserved for stronger creators and better-quality videos
4. Content Delivery Requirements
For barter and paid UGC, make sure the creator delivers:
Complete edited video
Individual video fragments
Separate voice/audio files, if available
This is important because Luminize editors need the raw fragments and voice clips for post-processing.
5. Partner Ads / Spark Ads
Ask if the creator agrees to use the content for Partner Ads or Spark Ads.
If they agree, the content can be used for Partner Ads / Spark Ads.
If they do not agree, that is okay. Luminize can still use the standard video as advertising material based on the agreed usage rights.
Part 1: Meta Business Suite / Instagram Outreach Process
Step 1: Track Your Time in ClickUp
Before starting the outreach task, track your time in ClickUp.
Recommended time allocation:
Spend at least 1 hour on this task
Use the time to find new creators, check replies, update statuses, and send outreach messages
Step 2: Open the Required Tools

Open the following:
Outreach Tracker
Meta Business Suite
Luminize Custom GPT
Tiktok
Hyred.nl

Login Details Here:

Step 3: Go to Creator Marketplace
In Meta Business Suite, go to Creator Marketplace.
If you are on the Meta Business Suite home page, look for Creator Marketplace from the side menu or folder area.

Step 4: Apply Filters
Use filters to find creators that match Luminize’s basic criteria.
Recommended filters:
Location: Netherlands
Language: Dutch
Hide creators already messaged
If the creator has a highlighted message bubble, it usually means they have already been messaged.
If the creator is saved, it usually means they were already checked before and may already have a conversation in the inbox.

Step 5: Review Creator Profile
Open the creator profile and review:
Follower count
Content quality
Video style
Home/interior/garden setup
Whether they speak or only use visuals
Whether they match Glenn’s preferred creator quality
Whether their profile is suitable for Luminize products
If the creator does not fully match the ideal style but still fits Luminize’s basic criteria, they can still be added to the tracker for outreach.
Step 6: Check if There Is an Existing Conversation
Before sending a new outreach message, check if Luminize already had a conversation with the creator.
Process:
Copy the creator’s username or profile name
Go to the normal Instagram Inbox
Search for the creator
Check if there is an old conversation
Review the previous messages before sending a new message
Important note:
Messages from Creator Marketplace usually go to partnership messages, while normal creator replies from Instagram may appear in the regular Instagram Inbox.
Step 7: Translate Old Conversations if Needed
If the old conversation is in Dutch, copy the conversation and paste it into the Luminize Custom GPT.
Prompt to use:
Translate this conversation to English so I can understand the previous context.
After translating, check:
Did they reject before?
Did they say maybe in the future?
Did they already collaborate before?
Did they ghost or stop replying?
Is it okay to follow up again?
If the last conversation was a long time ago, it is usually okay to reach out again.
Step 8: Take Screenshots for New Creator Leads
If the creator is not yet in the tracker, take screenshots before adding them.
Required screenshots:
Creator overview from Meta Business Suite
Instagram bio/profile section showing creator details, username, follower count, and bio
Make sure the screenshot clearly shows the creator’s important profile details.


Step 9: Use the Luminize Custom GPT
Go to the Luminize Custom GPT and upload/paste the creator screenshots or details.
Use this prompt:
Create an easy-to-copy tracker entry for this creator. Don’t forget the profile link. Also create an outreach message.

Creator name
Creator username
Platform
Profile link
Follower count
Niche/category
Recommended product
Suggested deal type
Tracker-ready row
Outreach message

Make sure the following details are included:
Status
Date contacted
Platform
Creator name
Creator username
Profile link
Follower count
Recommended product
Deal type
Notes
If the creator was already contacted before, update the notes instead of duplicating the entry.
Example note:
Reached out before in 2024. Reaching out again in 2026.
Step 11: Send Outreach Message
Review the GPT-generated outreach message before sending.
Before sending, make sure:
The message sounds natural
The product recommendation makes sense
The tone is warm, practical, and friendly
The message does not sound too formal
The message is in Dutch when needed
Then send the message through Creator Marketplace, Instagram Inbox, or the relevant message thread.
Step 12: Update Tracker Status
After sending the message, update the tracker.
Recommended statuses:

Ready to Reach Out
Contacted
Followed Up
Interested
Needs Review
Approved
Contract Sent
Waiting for Content

Part 2: Replying to Creator Responses
Step 1: Check Replies
Check replies in:

Instagram Inbox
Step 2: Copy the Creator Tracker Row
When a creator replies, go to the Outreach Tracker and copy the full row for that creator.

Step 4: Use the Luminize Custom GPT
Paste both the tracker row and the creator’s reply into the Luminize Custom GPT.
Use this prompt:
Create a reply for this creator based on their tracker row and message.
The GPT should create:
Suggested Dutch reply
English translation
Recommended next step
Tracker note, if needed
Step 5: Adjust the Reply Before Sending
Review and adjust the GPT reply before sending.
Make sure:
The reply sounds natural
The message fits the conversation history
You are not repeating unnecessary intro messages
The product or collaboration type is correct
The reply keeps the conversation moving
If the creator seems interested, do not immediately ask for rates unless needed.
For barter-first conversations, ask for a photo or video of the space first.
Example prompt to adjust the GPT reply:
Please adjust this for barter only and just ask for a picture or video of the spot where they would place the product.
Step 6: Send Reply and Update Tracker
After sending the reply, update the tracker status and notes.
Example notes:
Confirmed wanting to do gifted collaboration, wants outdoor products
Interested in barter deal, asked for suitable product
Asked for photo/video of placement area
Waiting for creator to confirm preferred product

Needs Glenn review before approval

The TikTok process is almost the same as Instagram.

Whether they make product-style videos

Phase 2 Task - New prompt trial with Brittney
description:
Overview / context
We have written a short addition to how Zulema and Brittney generate their daily end-of-day reports. It asks for three things we currently chase by hand: deadlines, rough hours, and work that came in unplanned. Plus a short look at the week ahead on Fridays.
Before sending it to both of them, we want one person to actually live with it for two days.
Brittney first, for three reasons. Her changes are the smaller set. She described her own setup in the most detail, so we know best what we are adding to. And she already reviews and corrects what her tool generates, so she will notice if something looks wrong.
She is doing us a favor here. This is a trial, not a rollout. If it gets in her way, we pull it and rework it. Say that plainly when you ask her.
Thursday and Friday, on purpose. Two days covers the daily changes, and Friday is the only day the week-ahead section appears, so a Thursday start tests everything in one short window.
Instructions
Before you contact her
Check whether the text will even fit. Her tool is a custom GPT she built, and custom GPT instructions have a hard limit of 8,000 characters. Our addition is about 4,250 characters. If her existing instructions are longer than roughly 3,750 characters, it will not fit, and she would have to delete her own instructions to make room. We do not want that.
Ask her to paste her current instructions to you, or just to tell you the character count. Two minutes, and it either clears the concern or changes the plan. Do not send her the file until this is answered.
If it does not fit, stop and flag it. We shorten the addition rather than asking her to cut hers.
When you send it
Tell her to save a copy of her current instructions first. This is the most important line in the whole message. If she keeps a copy, the trial is reversible in one step. If she does not and something goes wrong on Thursday, her tool is damaged and she built it herself.
Send only her file, and be clear it gets added, not pasted over. Her existing instructions all stay. Nothing gets removed.
Offer to do it with her. A few minutes on a call is easier than a written back-and-forth, and it means we see any confusion live rather than hearing about it Friday.
During the trial
Ask her to watch for four things, and tell her these are the things we expect might go wrong:
Does it ask its questions at the right moment, or does it start asking during the day when she is just logging updates?
Does it ask about the right items, or about things she did not mean to include?
Did anything she normally gets in the report stop appearing?
Is answering the questions annoying at the end of a long day? An honest yes here is the most useful thing she can tell us.
Check in once, Thursday evening or Friday morning. One short message. Not a survey.
After Friday
Get her Friday report and read it properly. Confirm three things: the deadlines came through, the hours are there, and the week-ahead section actually appeared and made sense.
Ask her the one question that matters: would she keep it? If the answer is anything softer than yes, we change it before Zulema sees it.
Write up what broke and bring it back before the cascade task runs. If nothing broke, say that too, and the cascade task can go ahead.
Draft message to Brittney
Hi Brittney,
Quick favor to ask, and an easy no if the timing is bad.
We have written a short addition to the EOD reporting setup, aimed at capturing a few things that currently get chased by hand: due dates, a rough sense of hours, and work that lands unplanned. Before sending it to everyone, we would rather one person try it for a couple of days and tell us what does not work.
Given how well you described your setup, you are the obvious person to ask.
Two quick things first. Could you send over your current Brittany Program Ops Tracker instructions, or just tell me roughly how long they are? There is a length limit on custom GPT instructions and I want to be sure ours fits before you touch anything. And whatever happens, please save a copy of your current instructions somewhere before adding ours, so you can put it back exactly as it was.
Nothing gets removed. It is added on top, and the rest of your report stays as it is.
If you are up for it, Thursday and Friday would be ideal. Happy to jump on a quick call and set it up with you rather than leaving you to it.
And genuinely, if it gets in your way, tell us and we will pull it. That is the point of trying it with one person first.
Done when
Brittney has run it Thursday and Friday, we have read her Friday report, and we know whether it goes out to Zulema as written or gets changed first.

title: Phase 2 Task - Cascade new prompts to Zulema/Brittney
description:
Overview / context
Zulema and Brittney each write a daily end-of-day report with AI help. They built their own setups and they work differently. Those reports are where Dr. Yasmin's view of the week comes from. If something is not in a report, she cannot see it.

Three things are missing right now, and we chase them by hand every time:
Deadlines. Plenty of work has no due date attached, so nothing can be sorted by what is due soon.
Hours. Nobody knows what any task actually costs.
Unplanned work. When something urgent lands and pushes other work back, that gets lost.

Everything else we need already comes through fine from both of them.

There is also a Friday piece. Once a week we want a short look at the week ahead. Right now both setups only ask about tomorrow, so nobody has ever been asked to think a week out. It is not a demand for a fully planned week. Whatever they can say is what we want.

The fix is small on purpose. Neither of them has to change how she reports, rebuild anything, or work differently. Each gets a short block added to the setup she already uses.

There are two versions because they work differently. Zulema already tracks time on each item. Brittney already produces a structured section at the end of her report with a due date field in it. One shared block would have made each of them do something twice. The wording each gets is shaped around what she already does, and it is checked line by line against how each of them described her own process in September.

This is temporary. It holds us over until the ClickUp migration, where the plans, the daily updates, the conversations and the time all live in one place and these separate files go away. Say that to both of them, so it does not land as a permanent new process.
Instructions
Send the two .txt files attached to this task. One is Zulema's, one is Brittney's. Each person gets only her own file. Do not combine them and do not reword them. They look different on purpose, and the exact labels inside them are what let us pull the information out quickly at our end.
Zulema is a simple paste. Her setup is a ChatGPT project with standing instructions. Her block gets added to those. A short note with the file is enough.
Brittney is a conversation, not a file drop. Hers lives inside a custom GPT she built and named herself. Asking her to edit it is a bigger ask than asking Zulema to paste something. 
Hours: the point is the habit, not the number. Explain it like this. Right now neither of them can say how long anything actually takes. They will not be able to until they start putting a number on it. The first guesses will be rough. That is expected and it is fine. What matters is that guessing becomes normal, because someone who estimates their work every day gets good at it within a few weeks, and someone who never does stays unable to answer. Once the numbers get closer to real, we can finally answer the useful questions: how long this work really takes, where the week goes, and whether something new can be added without breaking something else.
Be clear about what it is not. Nobody is being timed. Nothing is being billed. It is a guess from memory at the end of the day, rounded off. If either of them hears "time tracking", they will push back, and they would be pushing back on something we are not asking for.
Unplanned work: this is what explains everything else. Today, when a deadline moves, Dr. Yasmin sees that it moved and nothing about why. A week full of interruptions and a slow week look exactly the same to her.
So the block asks for two things whenever something unexpected takes real time. What it was, and what planned work it pushed back. That second part is the one that matters. One line, in their own words, or just "nothing" if it ate time but knocked nothing over.
With that in place, a moved deadline stops looking like a miss and starts looking like what it usually is: a reprioritization, with a reason attached. It also protects them. Right now the work that blows up their day is invisible, so they get judged on the work that slipped instead.
The Friday block: a few lines, once a week. On Fridays only, each file adds a short "week ahead" section. One line per thing she plans to work on next week: which day, what it is, what comes out of it, and a rough estimate. Then whatever is still open and carrying over.
Say clearly that a half-planned week is a fine answer. The block does not ask for all five days. If she only knows Monday and Tuesday, that is what she writes. If she knows the work but not the day, there is a "not sure yet" to use instead. It asks once for anything missing and then moves on, and it never holds the report back. This is the part most likely to be misread as a big new weekly planning exercise, so head that off when you send it.
Zulema keeps her existing "tomorrow's priorities" list and this goes after it, so she is not losing anything she already does.
We check in after the first week. The block holds the report back if work is missing a deadline, and asks up to two rounds of questions before writing it. That is friction at the exact moment they are tired and want to be done. If either of them starts answering "skip everything" every day, it has stopped working and we need to rethink it. Two rounds is a starting point, not a rule.
Done when
Both are running the updated setup, and a real end-of-day report from each has come through with deadlines, hours and unplanned work included. The Friday part gets checked separately, on the first Friday after it goes out.

title: Phase 2 Task - Checking with Zulema/Brittney + Prompt Suggestions
description:
Overview

The CEO dashboard updates daily and its primary input is Zulema's and Brittney's EOD reports. Several parts of it are still blank, and the cause is the report instructions, not anything either of them is doing: the instructions ask for a due date but accept "not specified" as an answer, and they never ask about time at all.

We need their reports to capture what Dr. Yasmin called non-negotiable:

A real deadline per deliverable, or a question back to us if one has not been set yet
Actual time spent per task, captured during the day, in the AI tool they already use
Whether the work was planned, or came up and pushed something else aside
Status in the tracker's five words: Not started / In progress / Waiting on others / Blocked / Done
Owner from the fixed list, so per-person roll-ups do not silently drop rows
Completed date, entered on the day it finishes
Fridays: a plan for the week ahead — each task, the expected deliverable, and an estimated time against it
Both 6:00 PM deadlines are firm — the daily report Mon–Fri, and the Friday plan. "Non-negotiable" is her word.

Steps

1. Check in with Zulema and Brittney separately.
No formal structure, just a conversation. Ask how they use ChatGPT day to day and what their prompt looks like for generating the EOD report. Read a few of their recent reports first so the conversation is specific rather than general. Listening only — do not commit to any change during the call.

2. Write up what each of them said, then go through it with BJ.
Their setups are genuinely different. Brittney's reports already end in a "Spreadsheet-Ready Updates" section carrying most of the fields we need; Zulema's have no equivalent. The same ask lands differently for each, so the write-up should keep them separate.

3. Add the prompt additives.
A draft already exists — check with BJ before writing anything new. This is adapting it to what you find, not starting over.

Two things about it that are deliberate and should not be changed without BJ:
It is additive. It bolts onto whatever each of them already has in their ChatGPT Project. Nothing they use today gets replaced.
Routing is Divine directly to Zulema and Brittney, not via Dr. Yasmin.

title: Phase 2 Task - Daily CEO Dashboard Monitoring & Refresh
Phase 2 Task - Study Tovuti LMS
description:
Owner: Lorie. Preparation for the Phase 2 task takeover. Onboarding and course creation in Tovuti move to GIM, so the goal is to be able to run both unaided.

There is a date behind this. SYWLP is the first live run: Brittney's materials and participant list land Monday 21 September, and onboarding needs to be live with all participants loaded by Wednesday 23 September. Study now so that window is build time, not discovery time.

Access



Instance: https://mwelp-dryasmininstitute.tovuti.io/
Master account: administrator@dryasmininstitute.com

The password is not written here. It is in Dr. Yasmin's email of 15 September on the "SYWLP Tovuti Program Build" thread. Ask BJ if you cannot find it.

Start from what we already have

Do not start from scratch. We did a full study of the Tovuti material in Phase 1: Tovuti LMS analysis. It covers the course structure, the recurring task load, and the user creation steps. DYDLI also has three SOPs, the most useful being SW | Tovuti Course Setup & User Enrollment.docx and SOP Tovuti – User Profiles.docx. Ask BJ for both.

The two jobs to get fluent in

Course creation. Duplicate the prior cohort course, update title, dates, deadlines and resource links, upload the welcome video, forms and pre-program assignments, then test it as a test user.

Onboarding and enrollment. People → User Manager → New, fill the profile, assign user groups including Registered, save. Saving sends the login email automatically. Also learn the CSV bulk import, since a full cohort one at a time is not realistic.

Three things to actually verify in the instance

These are unverified and the SYWLP build leans on them.

Does duplicating a course carry its lessons and course events? Tovuti's own documentation suggests a duplicate keeps settings and custom fields but not lessons or events. Our SOP assumes duplication carries everything. If that is wrong, the 48-hour window is a very different job. Check this first.
Can homework completion be exported? The SOP hedges with "export completion list if possible or manually track", which means nobody knew.
How the homework gating is configured, so course open dates and calendar open dates stay in sync. The SOP is explicit that this is deliberate, to stop fellows jumping ahead.

Two shortcuts

There is a Tovuti tutorial inside Tovuti, under Resources → Tutorials. Cheapest starting point and nobody has used it.

The live documentation is the Help Center at help.tovutilms.com. Tovuti University was discontinued in June 2025, so ignore anything that points you there.

Please be careful

This is the live production instance with real cohorts in it. Look, do not change. If you need to try something, use a test user or a draft course, and check with BJ first.

Output

Keep notes as you go, especially anything that contradicts the SOPs, and send them to BJ. Answers to the three questions above are the priority.

title: Phase 2 Task - Get Access & Create New Email under dryasmininstitute.com
description:
Owner: Lorie. Three things, in order: get into the admin account, create the mailbox, set up the rule that copies us on Zulema's external email.

1. Line up a window with Zulema first

The login for administrator@dryasmininstitute.com sends a verification code to Zulema's email, so you cannot get in without her. Message her and agree a time when she is at her desk and can read the code out to you. 

Dr. Yasmin has already told Zulema this is happening, so you are not breaking news. You can keep it simple: you need a code to finish an admin setup.

Credentials are not written down here. They are in Dr. Yasmin's email of 15 September on the "Temporary Client Email Response Oversight" thread. Ask BJ if you cannot find it.

2. Sign in and confirm the account is actually an admin

Go to admin.google.com and sign in as administrator@dryasmininstitute.com.

If the Admin console opens, you have what we need. Carry on.
If it redirects you to Gmail or Drive instead, the account is not a Workspace admin. Stop there and tell BJ. Nothing below will work and we will need to go back to Dr. Yasmin.

3. Create operations@dryasmininstitute.com

Directory → Users → Add new user. Check the user list first in case the address already exists.

4. Set up the copy rule

Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → Routing. You are adding two rules, one for each direction. Both point at the same place.

Rule 1, incoming:

Name it something like Copy MD inbound to operations
Messages to affect: tick Inbound only
Envelope filter: Only affect specific envelope recipients → single recipient → zulema@dryasmininstitute.com
Also deliver to: Add more recipients → operations@dryasmininstitute.com

Rule 2, outgoing: identical, except tick Outbound only, and use Only affect specific envelope senders → zulema@dryasmininstitute.com.

Leave "Internal - sending" and "Internal - receiving" unticked in both rules. That is what keeps internal DYDLI email out of it, which is what we promised Dr. Yasmin. Only email going to or coming from outside the organization gets copied.

Google shifts these menu labels around from time to time. If the wording on screen does not match exactly, go with the closest equivalent rather than guessing at a different setting.

Send an email from an outside address to Zulema, and ask her to send one out to an outside address. Both should land in operations@. Give it up to an hour, since routing changes take a while to propagate.

title: M-S.7 — Roll out the reporting prompt changes with Zulema and Brittney
description:

title: M-S.5 — Design the Daily Operations Reporting System
description:
⚑ Client dependency — originated with Dr. Yasmin and comes back to her for review.

New scope, raised by the client on 17 August and accepted the same day. Full email exchange in the repo at 05-client-feedback/daily-operations-reporting-email.md. Read it before starting; the wording matters.

Overview
Dr. Yasmin asked for a centralized Daily Operations Reporting System to replace the separate end-of-day reports she currently receives from the Managing Director and Program Manager. She was explicit that the outcome matters, not the mechanism — "I would actually welcome you approaching this as an operational design problem" — so this is a design engagement, not a build-to-spec.

Scope boundary — read this before committing to anything. She asked us to "design and implement". Divine's reply commits to design, then review before building. Design sits inside Phase 1 stabilization. Building and operating a daily reporting function does not, against a fixed $5,250 and the seven deliverables in Proposal §4. The build decision belongs at the Day 15 gate, which is already a stop/go conversation.

Steps
Map the current reporting flow (MD → PM → CEO) and locate where accountability actually breaks. This overlaps M3.9 — do it there rather than duplicating.
Design the standardized template around her fields: Deliverable | Owner | Deadline | Current Status | At Risk? | Blocker | Next Action.
Corrected 20 August. The consolidation step is removed, not designed. The report generates from the tracker instead, one row per deliverable rather than one per day, because the two source reports share no structure and consolidating them would be a rewrite rather than a task. Decided 19 August.
Corrected 20 August. Ownership at launch is Zulema, not the EA — the system goes live regardless of the EA hire, and the EA inherits ownership at onboarding. Ownership covers collection, completeness, escalation, delivery and archive, without making the owner responsible for anyone else's performance. Decided 19 August.
Design the WhatsApp audio-briefing format. She wants an executive briefing, not a reading of the report.
Bring the design back to her for review before anything is built.

Suggested owner
Divine · Support BJ

Inputs / prerequisites
M-S.2 tracker running, so the design arrives with real data behind it rather than as paper
M3.9 decision and escalation mapping

Definition of done
A recommended system design delivered to Dr. Yasmin for review, covering template, workflow, tooling options, ownership model and audio-briefing format, with the design/build boundary stated explicitly.

Handle with care
Her email states that the Managing Director is not consistently holding the Program Manager accountable. The evidence gathered so far points at capacity and system rather than management failure — four programs plus oversight at 80% inception load, and a Program Manager four weeks in who inherited AI-generated deadlines built for the previous cohort. She herself asks us to distinguish a system/process issue from a management/accountability issue from an individual performance issue, so she has pre-committed to that distinction. It still has to be evidenced rather than asserted, and it does not belong in a daily update.

Resources

title: M6.5 — Log the stop/go decision and agreed next steps in writing
description:

It also carries a §14 tail — a marginal hire is likelier to fail inside the 45-day replacement window, which triggers a replacement search at our cost against an unchanged fee. Getting this answer before posting is worth more than getting it thoroughly.

Establish where $55,000 sits: competitive, at market, or below.
Assess what the evening and weekend requirement does to the realistic pool.

title: M3.5 — Document duplication in the Drive, and the Drive/Dropbox split
description:
Rescoped 20 August 2026. The original task covered duplication across the document repository, the Dropbox archive and email. A decision on 13 August dropped Dropbox and email access — the archive was judged irrelevant and email access unnecessary — and this task was never updated to match. It has been unstartable since.

⚠ This narrowing is narrower than Proposal §3, which commits to duplication across "the document repository, the archive, and email." It has to be disclosed in the Operational Diagnostic Report (M5.1), not quietly delivered. Flag to Divine before the Day 11 pack.

Overview

Duplication with no canonical copy is a large part of why documents get lost. Write it up as a finding, not a cleanup plan — remediation is Phase 2–4 work.

Steps

Duplicate names in the Drive, counted. Extend the 20 August folder audit with a file-level pass. Same name in more than one place, and same name plus same size, which is near-certain duplication. Method and limits in 01-phase1/drive-structure-audit.md.
Wholesale duplication from the recovery effort. The personal-drive extractions are the largest single case and are already visible: Dr. Yasmin Davidds G Drive Content, Zulema Google Drive , Brittney's Files, Jackie Davis Persona Google Drive Aug 13, JACKIE PHONE, Videos and Photos from Jackie Laptop , and Crystal Google Drive Aug 12 plus Crystal Davis Google Drive Aug 13 — the same person's drive extracted twice on consecutive days. Nobody can say which copy is authoritative or complete.
The Drive/Dropbox split, evidenced without Dropbox access. The blueprints record where each SOP is supposed to live. Count Dropbox-linked against Drive-linked against filename-only across the six workbooks. GELP links to Dropbox, the April YWLP file to Drive, SYWLP to neither. That gives a real cross-cloud finding from documents already in hand.
What drives it: habit, permissions, or no agreed home. Answerable from the artifacts above without asking anyone.
Write up as a finding, with the exclusions stated plainly.

Explicitly out of scope, and why

Inside Dropbox — no access. Dropped 13 August. See the reopening question below.
Email — no access, dropped 13 August, and nothing since has justified reopening it for duplication specifically.
Which copy is authoritative. Metadata cannot answer this and we are not opening files. It is a question for people, and it is really the question the register in 01-phase1/drive-structure-proposal.md exists to answer. Route it to M3.6 rather than attempting it here.
Version divergence between copies. Requires opening and comparing documents. Out on the same grounds.

Reopening question for Divine — the 13 August basis for excluding Dropbox is now false
Dropbox was dropped as "archive, judged irrelevant." The Drive audit and the blueprint analysis both show it holds live material: GELP's SOP library links into Dropbox, and the chapter discussion questions Dr. Yasmin and Zulema hunted for thirty minutes turned out to be there. It is not an archive. Whether to request access is a decision, not a task step.

Suggested owner
Erwin

Inputs / prerequisites
M3.4 tools audit — in progress, and its Drive pass is the direct input
The six blueprint workbooks, for step 3

Definition of done
A written account covering: duplicate names in the Drive with counts; the recovery-extraction duplication named file by file; the Drive/Dropbox SOP split quantified from the blueprints; what drives the duplication; and an explicit statement of what was not examined and why.

title: [FINANCE] Invoicing for Clients and Subcons - Monthly
description:
🎯 TASK: Subcontractor Invoice Review & Validation
Assignee:  
Support: Jade 
Frequency: First week of every month (or per subcontractor's agreed billing cycle — check task due dates)

📌 PURPOSE
To ensure all subcontractor invoices submitted each month are accurate, complete, and aligned with their agreed rate and hours before payment is processed. This protects ANGL from overpayments, errors, and discrepancies while maintaining a clean financial record for every subcontractor.

⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTES BEFORE YOU START
Each subcontractor is represented as an individual task in the ClickUp Finance V2 Space
Subcontractors will submit their invoice and change the task status to FOR REVIEW — this is your trigger to begin the validation process
Some subcontractors may be on a bi-monthly or different billing cycle — always check the task due date to confirm the correct review period before starting
Jade is the only person responsible for updating the status to PROCESSED — do not process payment or change to that status yourself
For any questions or discrepancies, communicate directly in the ClickUp task comments — do not reach out via email or Slack unless necessary

🔄 STEP-BY-STEP PROCESS
Step 1 — Check for Invoices Ready for Review
Open the ClickUp Finance V2 Space at the start of each week during the first week of the month
Filter tasks by status FOR REVIEW — these are the invoices submitted by subcontractors and ready for your validation
Check each task's due date to confirm the invoice covers the correct billing period before proceeding
Step 2 — Open the Invoice
Inside the task, locate the attached PDF invoice
Open and review the invoice for the following basic details: 
Subcontractor's full name
Payment details (bank account, PayPal, Wise, etc.)
Billing period covered
Breakdown of services or tasks
Hourly rate applied (if hourly)
Total hours worked (if hourly)
Total amount due
Step 3 — Validate the Invoice
For hourly subcontractors:
Open the ClickUp Timesheet Dashboard and filter by the subcontractor's name and the billing period
Compare the total hours on the invoice against the total hours recorded in the Timesheet Dashboard
Confirm the hourly rate matches the rate agreed upon in their contract
Confirm the total amount is correct (total hours × hourly rate)
If the totals match, the invoice is valid — proceed to Step 5
If there is a discrepancy in the total hours, dive deeper into the Timesheet Dashboard and cross-check on a per-task basis to identify where the difference lies — proceed to Step 4 if action is needed
For retainer subcontractors:
Confirm the invoice amount matches the agreed monthly retainer rate in their contract
No timesheet cross-check is required unless the amount differs from the agreed rate
If the amount is correct, proceed to Step 5
If the amount differs, proceed to Step 4
Step 4 — Flag for Changes (if needed)
If there is any discrepancy, incorrect rate, incorrect hours, or missing information on the invoice: 
Change the task status to NEEDS CHANGES
Leave a comment in the ClickUp task clearly explaining what needs to be corrected or what additional information is required
Wait for the subcontractor to resubmit or respond before proceeding
Step 5 — Save the Invoice to Google Drive
Once the invoice is validated and confirmed correct: 
Download the PDF invoice attached to the ClickUp task
Open Google Drive using the Divine ANGL Chrome Profile
Navigate to: Google Drive → Employees & Tax Forms → [Subcontractor Name]
Save the invoice inside the subcontractor's designated folder
Step 6 — Update the Task Status
Once the invoice is validated and saved to Google Drive, update the task status to FOR PROCESSING
Jade will review and update the status to PROCESSED once payment has been completed
Do not change the status to PROCESSED yourself

📋 STATUS FLOW REFERENCE

Status Meaning Who Updates
TO SUBMIT INVOICE Default status — awaiting subcontractor submission System default
FOR REVIEW Invoice submitted and ready for Divine's review Subcontractor
NEEDS CHANGES Discrepancy found — subcontractor needs to correct or clarify Divine
FOR PROCESSING Invoice validated and saved — ready for payment Divine
PROCESSED Payment completed Jade📎 RESOURCES
All subcontractor task details, rate references, and invoice attachments are in the ClickUp Finance V2 Space. Timesheet data is accessible via the ClickUp Timesheet Dashboard (Dashboards > Timesheet Dashboard). Validated invoices are saved in Google Drive → Employees & Tax Forms → [Subcontractor Name] via the Divine ANGL Chrome Profile.

✅ CHECKLIST
[ ] Task status confirmed as FOR REVIEW before starting
[ ] Task due date checked to confirm correct billing period
[ ] Invoice opened and basic details reviewed (name, payment details, billing period, breakdown)
[ ] Hours validated against ClickUp Timesheet Dashboard (hourly subcontractors)
[ ] Hourly rate or retainer amount confirmed against contract
[ ] Total amount confirmed as correct
[ ] Any discrepancies flagged via NEEDS CHANGES status and ClickUp task comment
[ ] Validated invoice downloaded and saved to correct Google Drive folder
[ ] Task status updated to FOR PROCESSING
