title: [HR] Job Posting, Reviewing, & Monitoring - As Needed
description:
🎯 TASK: Job Posting and Candidate Monitoring
Assignee:  
Support: Jade 
Frequency: As needed

📌 PURPOSE
To consistently attract, filter, and manage qualified candidates across multiple job platforms in a structured and organized way. This SOP covers posting job ads, monitoring applications, filtering candidates into ClickUp, and coordinating the interview process through to the point of onboarding (covered in a separate SOP).

⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTES BEFORE YOU START
Always use the approved job post descriptions found in HR V2 Space → Hiring Knowledge Base → Approved Job Post Descriptions — do not create or modify job descriptions without Jade's approval
If unsure about hourly rates to include in the job post, confirm with Jade before posting
Log-in credentials for LinkedIn and Upwork are in the Operations Knowledge Base in ClickUp
The same approved job description is used across all platforms — no platform-specific edits unless instructed
Candidate tasks in ClickUp are confidential — statuses like REJECTED (INTERNAL) are for internal use only and should not be communicated to the candidate unless a conversation has already been established

🔄 STEP-BY-STEP PROCESS
Step 1 — Access the Approved Job Post
Open HR V2 Space → Hiring Knowledge Base → Approved Job Post Descriptions in ClickUp
Locate the correct job post for the role being hired
Review the post in full before publishing — if anything is unclear or if hourly rates need to be confirmed, check with Jade before proceeding
Step 2 — Post the Job Ad
Post the approved job description across the relevant platforms. Use the credentials and access methods below:

Platform Access
Indeed Divine's ANGL email
LinkedIn Jade's LinkedIn — credentials in Operations Knowledge Base
Upwork Credentials in Operations Knowledge Base
Reddit Jade's Reddit account
Facebook Divine's or Jade's Facebook access
Other platforms Create an account as necessary and log credentials in the Operations Knowledge BaseUse the same approved job description across all platforms
Once posted, note the platform, posting date, and any job post link or reference number in the relevant ClickUp task or a comment for tracking purposes
Step 3 — Monitor Applications Daily
Check each platform daily or as needed for new applicants
Review each application for the following minimum criteria before creating a ClickUp task: 
Portfolio — must be included or linked. No portfolio = do not proceed
Experience — relevant social media or content experience required
Niche alignment — experience should align with ANGL's client industries (wellness, lifestyle, e-commerce, food & beverage, beauty, apparel, etc.)
Judgment call — even if the above are met, use discretion on overall fit based on the quality of their application and communication
If the candidate does not meet the above, no further action is needed unless they follow up directly
Step 4 — Create a Candidate Task in ClickUp
For each qualified candidate, create a new task in HR V2 Space → Candidates
One task = one candidate
Task title: Candidate's full name only (e.g. Christian Salinas)
Role field: Add the role they are applying for (e.g. Social Media Manager, Paid Ads Specialist)
Platform field: Add the platform where they were found (e.g. Upwork, LinkedIn, Indeed)
Include the following in the task: 
Link to their application or profile
Portfolio link or attached file
Resume or CV (attach or link)
Social media accounts they currently manage or have recently managed
Any other relevant notes from their application
Set the default status to SHORTLISTED
Step 5 — Review and Forward to Jade
Review the candidate's portfolio, experience, and overall profile thoroughly
If confident the candidate is a strong fit, update the task status to FOR JADE'S REVIEW
Jade will review and update the status to one of the following: 
REJECTED (INTERNAL) — candidate is not moving forward
FOR INTERVIEW — candidate is approved for an interview
Step 6 — Handle Rejected Candidates
If a candidate is marked REJECTED (INTERNAL), no outreach is required by default
If the candidate follows up via the platform or email and a prior conversation exists, respond professionally and courteously — handle on a case-to-case basis
Step 7 — Schedule the Interview
Once a candidate is marked FOR INTERVIEW, coordinate scheduling based on Divine's availability
Reach out to the candidate via the platform where they applied, or via email if provided, to schedule the interview
Confirm the interview date, time, and time zone with the candidate
Send a calendar invite with a Google Meet link
Ensure Fathom is connected to the calendar invite so the interview is automatically recorded
Divine conducts the interview independently
Step 8 — Prepare the Interview Brief
Before the interview, prepare an interview brief for the role using Claude
Use the following prompt and paste the candidate's information alongside it:

"You are preparing an interview brief for ANGL Creative, a boutique social media agency. The candidate is applying for the role of [ROLE TITLE]. Using the candidate information below, generate a structured interview brief that includes:
1. A candidate overview summarizing their background, experience, and portfolio highlights2. A portfolio highlights section with key stats or notable work3. Industries/niches they have worked in4. Core skills listed5. A fit assessment table with two columns: Why They Might Be a Good Fit, and Things to Probe6. A structured interview section with: Part 1 — Agency Introduction, Part 2 — Candidate Introduction, Part 3 — Interview Questions (minimum 7, tailored to the role and candidate), Part 4 — Candidate Questions
Keep the tone professional and practical. Flag any gaps or red flags in the candidate's background under Things to Probe. Here is the candidate's information: [PASTE OR ATTACH CANDIDATE INFORMATION HERE]"

Role-Specific Interview Question Banks
Use these as a reference when reviewing or supplementing the Claude-generated brief. These are the standard questions used at ANGL Creative per role:

Social Media Manager
Walk me through your experience managing social media accounts — what platforms, what industries, and what results did you drive?
How do you approach building a content calendar from scratch for a new client?
Tell me about a piece of content that performed really well. What made it work?
How do you handle a situation where content you created doesn't perform well?
How do you stay on top of platform updates, algorithm changes, and trends?
Describe your design experience — what tools do you use and how comfortable are you creating graphics independently?
How do you manage multiple client accounts at the same time? Walk me through your workflow.
How many hours per week are you available, and do you have other commitments?

Paid Ads Specialist
Give me a specific campaign — what was the objective, the budget, and the ROAS or CPA? How did it compare to the client's target?
Tell me about a campaign that didn't perform. How did you diagnose whether it was a creative, audience, or targeting issue — and what did you change?
How do you decide when to scale spend and when to cut it? What's the minimum monthly budget you'd recommend for a client to get meaningful data?
Most of your portfolio is in [X vertical] — how would you approach a paid campaign for a lifestyle or wellness brand where the goal is brand awareness and DTC sales rather than lead generation?
A client comes to you after 30 days with no results and wants to pull the budget. How do you handle that conversation?
What's working right now on Meta and TikTok in terms of ad formats and creative — and what's changed in the last 6 months?
Have you managed multiple client accounts at the same time? How do you stay organized and prioritize when several clients need attention simultaneously?
How many hours per week are you available? Can you commit to regular check-ins and client-facing meetings during PST business hours?


Review the generated brief and refine as needed before the interview
Share the brief with Divine via Slack ahead of the interview

Step 9 — Conduct the Interview
Confirm Fathom is active and recording at the start of the call
Divine conducts the interview independently using the prepared brief
After the interview, retrieve the Fathom recording link
Share the recording link with Jade by adding it as a comment in the candidate's ClickUp task

Step 10 — Post-Interview Communications
Coordinate with Jade on her feedback of the interview
Handle any follow-up negotiations or communications with the candidate as directed by Jade
If the candidate is moving forward, proceed to the onboarding process (covered in a separate SOP)

📋 STATUS FLOW REFERENCE

Status Meaning Who Updates
SHORTLISTED Candidate task created, pending internal review Divine
FOR JADE'S REVIEW Divine has reviewed and recommends the candidate Divine
REJECTED (INTERNAL) Candidate is not moving forward Jade/Divine
FOR INTERVIEW Candidate approved for an interview Jade
📎 RESOURCES

Platform credentials: Operations Knowledge Base in ClickUp

title: [Sales] Proposal Generation via Nusii - As Needed
description:
🗂️ SOP: Client Proposal Generation Using Claude
Role: Operations Manager / Anyone generating proposals at ANGL Creative 
Trigger: A discovery call has been completed and a transcript is available (Fathom link shared by Jade)
Output: A complete proposal ready to be built in Nusii and sent to the client

📋 Overview
This SOP outlines the step-by-step process for generating a client-facing social media proposal using Claude, from the moment a discovery call transcript is available to the moment the proposal is sent. Follow each step in order. Do not skip steps or send a proposal without completing the full review checklist at the end.

✅ Step 1: Confirm the Discovery Call Transcript is Available
After a discovery call is completed, Jade will notify the team that a transcript is ready. The transcript will be available via Fathom (the call recording platform). Confirm the following before proceeding:
The Fathom recording link has been shared in Slack or via email
The transcript is complete and includes both sides of the conversation
You have the client's name, brand name, and any intake form or job post they submitted prior to the call
If the transcript is incomplete or the recording was not captured, flag this to Jade immediately. Do not proceed without a full transcript.

💻 Step 2: Open the Proposal Generation Project in Claude
Navigate to Claude and open the dedicated Proposal Generation project. This project contains the proposal instructions, writing rules, ANGL Creative agency context, and four sample proposals as reference.
Do not start a proposal in a general Claude conversation. Always use the ANGL Creative project so the instructions are automatically applied. Use the 'Lead Generation - Client Proposals (Nusii)' conversation.

📋 Step 3: Paste the Transcript
Copy the full transcript text from Fathom and paste it directly into a new conversation inside the Proposal Generation project. You do not need to add any instructions — the project will handle that automatically.
Claude will:
Read the transcript
Extract the key client details
Summarize them back to you for confirmation
Review the summary carefully. Check for accuracy across the following:
Client and brand name (spelled correctly)
Industry and what the brand does
Stage of the business
Platforms to be managed
Goals and KPIs
Content availability and any noted challenges
Any important context from the call (budget, previous agency experience, launch timelines, etc.)
If anything is missing or incorrect, correct it in your reply before moving forward. Do not approve the summary if details are wrong.

🏷️ Step 4: Confirm the Brand Name
Claude will ask for the brand name if it was not clearly stated in the transcript. Always confirm the exact spelling and capitalization of the brand name before the proposal is written. When in doubt, check the intake form, the client's website, or their social media handles.

🔍 Step 5: Review the Generated Proposal
Claude will generate the proposal with three sections: Introduction, Objectives, and Execution Plan. Read through the full output carefully before making any requests. Check for the following:
The introduction accurately reflects the brand and frames ANGL's role correctly
The objectives are specific to this client — not generic
The execution plan phases are realistic, properly sequenced, and named appropriately
No details were fabricated or assumed that were not in the transcript
The tone is clean, confident, and professional
Phase names in the execution plan match the client's situation
If anything needs to be adjusted, give Claude a brief and specific correction instruction. You do not need to rewrite anything yourself — just tell Claude what to change and it will revise.

🔄 Step 6: Iterate Until Satisfactory
Repeat Step 5 as needed until the proposal reads exactly as it should. Common adjustments include:
Shortening the execution plan if it feels too long
Updating the introduction to be more generic or more specific
Renaming a phase to better match the client's situation
Correcting a brand name, platform, or detail that was pulled incorrectly
Do not proceed to the next step until the proposal is fully approved. Flag BJ if you are unsure whether the content is accurate.

📝 Step 8: Copy the Approved Proposal into Nusii
Once the proposal copy is approved, open Nusii and create a new proposal for the client. Copy the three sections — Introduction, Objectives, and Execution Plan — into the appropriate fields. Apply the correct ANGL branding, package options, and pricing as instructed by Jade. 

👀 Step 9: Send for Jade's Review Before Sending to Client
Before sending the proposal to the client, share the Nusii draft link with Jade for final review. Tag Jade in Slack with the client name and the Nusii link. Jade will approve or flag any final changes. Jade will be responsible for the final proposal and triggering sending it to the client (via Nusii)

⏰ Step 10: Set a Follow-Up Reminder
After sending, set a follow-up reminder for three business days (using the lead task in ClickUp). If the client has not responded by then, send a brief follow-up email checking in on the proposal. Follow ANGL's standard three-week follow-up cadence from that point forward.

☑️ Checklist Before Sending
[ ] Transcript was complete and reviewed
[ ] Client details were confirmed before writing
[ ] Brand name is spelled correctly throughout
[ ] All three proposal sections are present: Introduction, Objectives, Execution Plan
[ ] No fabricated details in the proposal
[ ] Proposal has been pasted into Nusii correctly
[ ] Jade has reviewed and approved
[ ] Correct client email confirmed
[ ] Follow-up reminder set for three business days

📋 SOP: Upwork Lead Follow-Ups
Support: BJ
Tools needed: Jade's Upwork account, Divine's ANGL email, Delegated access to Jade's Gmail

📌 Overview
After Upwork proposals are submitted, leads may respond with questions or requests for more information. The goal of this SOP is to ensure no lead goes cold — follow up consistently to prompt a response, direct them to the ANGL Creative lead questionnaire, and ultimately move them toward a discovery call with Jade.
Jade reviews completed questionnaire responses and decides whether to schedule a discovery call.

📐 Follow-Up Rules
Send a maximum of 3 follow-ups per lead
Each follow-up is sent one week apart
Do not follow up on any message that is unopened, that is for Jade to reply to

✅ Step-by-Step Process

Step 1 — Identify Leads to Follow Up
Go to Upwork Messages and browse older conversations
Look for conversations where the last message was sent at least one week ago
Do not open or read any messages marked as unread — these are for Jade to respond to
If you accidentally open an unread message, tap the three dots next to the most recent message and mark it as unread immediately

Step 2 — Review the Conversation
Scroll through the full conversation history before sending anything
Check whether the ANGL Creative questionnaire link (anglcreative.co/contact) has already been shared
If it hasn't been sent, or was sent several messages back, include it in the follow-up message

Step 3 — Send the Follow-Up Message
Send a short, friendly follow-up message
Add variety — do not repeat the same message in consecutive follow-ups
Example for follow-ups 1 and 2: "Hi! Just wanted to follow up on my previous message, let me know if you have any questions for me!"
Example for follow-up 3 (final): "Feel free to reach out anytime if you'd like to revisit this — happy to connect whenever you're ready!"
The tone should always be warm, low-pressure, and conversational.

Step 4 — Check for Existing Email Contact
If Jade has previously shared her email with the lead in the Upwork conversation, verify by accessing Jade's Gmail via delegated access through Divine's ANGL email
Search for any prior email exchanges with the lead
If an email thread exists, flag to BJ — BJ handles all email follow-ups at this stage
Do not send any email follow-ups yourself

🚩 Flags & Escalations
Lead has messaged but Jade hasn't responded → mark the message as unread and do not reply
Conversation is unclear or next steps are vague → reach out to BJ before taking any action
Any situation outside of these steps → default to BJ

[ ] Identified conversations where last message was sent at least one week ago
[ ] Confirmed no unread messages were opened
[ ] Scrolled full conversation history to check for prior questionnaire link

title: [Sales] Lead Generation via Upwork - Daily
description:
🎯 TASK: Daily Upwork Proposal Submission
Support: BJ 
Frequency: Monday to Friday, maximum 1 hour per day (can include weekends if there is catching up to do)

📌 PURPOSE
To consistently submit high-quality proposals on Upwork on behalf of ANGL Creative (Jade's profile) to generate new client leads. This task covers browsing eligible job posts, generating proposals using AI, editing for tone and accuracy, and submitting through Upwork — keeping ANGL's pipeline active on a daily basis.

⚠️ IMPORTANT NOTES BEFORE YOU START
Always work from Jade's Upwork profile — never apply as a freelancer from any other profile
Proposals should never over-commit or make specific promises — keep the language safe, balanced, and generic. Instead of committing to specific numbers or deliverables, frame it as "helping with" or "supporting" the client's goals
The goal is 5–7 proposals per day maximum — if there are no qualifying jobs, that's okay. Do not apply to jobs that don't meet the criteria
This task is Monday to Friday only — weekends are as needed, if there's a need to catch up on submitting proposals

🔄 STEP-BY-STEP PROCESS

Step 1 — Check Upwork Connects Balance
Log into Jade's Upwork profile
Check the current Connects balance before starting
If the balance is running low (below 20), notify BJ immediately so Connects can be purchased using Jade's saved card before submitting proposals

Step 2 — Browse and Filter Job Posts
Utilize the following pages for job searching: 
On Jade's Upwork profile, filter job posts using the following criteria: 
Location: US/United States, UK/United Kingdom, and CAN/Canada only, do not apply to jobs outside of these
Job type: Hourly only, or Fixed Rate at $2000 minimum
Hourly rate: Set the rate to match the maximum hourly rate listed in the job post — for example, if the job post says up to $40/hour, enter $40 as the bid rate. Never go above the maximum rate listed as this will disqualify the application
Minimum rate: $35/hour minimum — do not apply to jobs with a maximum rate below $35/hour
Duration: Apply only to projects lasting 6+ months. If the title or description indicates a duration of under 6 months, skip it.
For Fixed Rate projects, set the duration to '3-6 Months'
Set rate increase to Never

Step 3 — Qualify the Job Post 
Before generating a proposal, verify the job is a good fit by checking:
Services match — the job must require at least one of the following:
Social media strategy
Content creation and calendars
Post scheduling and copywriting
Traffic and growth via social media
Campaigns and influencer collaborations
Community management
Industry match — the client should be in one of the following industries:
Beauty, health, and wellness
Food and beverage
Non-profit
Apparel and accessories
Home and lifestyle
Service providers (salons, clinics, aesthetic businesses)
If the job does not clearly match the above, skip it and move to the next one.
Also, refrain from applying to jobs where the scope of work:
requires purely paid ads (it should be organic + paid ads); and
pre-launch type apps, if they're looking for full service.

Step 4 — Generate the Proposal
Copy the full job post text
Paste it into Claude or ChatGPT using the prompt instructions provided by BJ
The AI will generate 2 proposal drafts — choose the best one and review it before using it 
Edit the proposal as needed, keeping the following in mind: 
Remove any language that over-commits or promises specific results (e.g., "we will grow your followers to 10,000" → change to "we will help drive consistent follower growth")
Keep the intro to 1–2 short paragraphs
Keep "Here's how I can help" to a maximum of 5 bullet points
Remove any irrelevant points that don't match the job post
Make sure that the portfolio is at the beginning part of the proposal, and it's introduced coherently in the proposal

Proposal structure, Version A (Draft A)
Greeting (Hi there / Hi [name])
Short intro about Jade and ANGL, 1-2 paragraphs
Portfolio and website links (static, placed immediately after the intro)
"Here's how I'd approach it" — maximum 5 bullets based on the job post
Call to action, tailored to the client's stated goal
Closing: Best, Jade

Proposal structure, Version B (Sharper)
Greeting (Hi there / Hi [name])
Opening observation, one specific detail from the job post, reacted to directly. No self-introduction.
Portfolio and website links (static, woven into the opening thought)
One substantive argument or point of view relevant to their situation, 1-2 short paragraphs
Three to five uneven bullets, varied in length, at least one short and blunt
Any honest scope or experience gap, stated plainly
Closing question whose answer would genuinely change the work
Closing: Best, Jade

Step 5 — Add Upwork Job Highlights
In the highlights section of the application, click Add an Upwork Job
Sort by Highest Rated
Select 3 jobs with strong reviews — look for Social Media Manager roles with positive client feedback
Do not add more than 3

Step 6 — Send for Review (Temporary — First 1–2 Weeks Only)
Create a Google Word Document:
For each proposal, add a new entry with the following: 
Link to the job post
Full proposal body (paste the complete text)
Notify BJ via Slack or message that entries are ready for review
Wait for BJ's approval comment on the Google Doc before proceeding to Step 7

Step 7 — Submit the Proposal
Before submitting, thoroughly review the final proposal one more time for: 
Typos, grammatical errors, or awkward phrasing
Any language that sounds obviously AI-generated (e.g. overly formal phrases, repetitive structure, filler words like "certainly," "absolutely," "I hope this finds you well")
Any placeholder text or brackets that were not replaced (e.g. [client name], [insert here])
Any specific commitments or promises that should not be included
Correct formatting (nothing looks off, no weird spaces)
Only proceed to submit once the proposal reads naturally and all issues are resolved
Paste the final approved proposal into the Cover Letter field in Upwork
Do not attach any files
Click Submit Proposal
After submission, Upwork will show a confirmation screen with the submitted proposal — copy the link from that screen

Step 8 — Log in the Tracker
Open the Upwork Proposal Tracker
Log the following for each submitted proposal: 
Date submitted
Job post name
Link to the submitted proposal

📎 RESOURCES
Proposal Tracker: 
ANGL's Website: 
ANGL's Portfolio: 

✅ CHECKLIST
[ ] Upwork Connects balance checked — BJ notified if running low
[ ] Job post reviewed and confirmed to meet all criteria before generating a proposal
[ ] Proposal generated using Claude or ChatGPT and edited for tone — no over-commitments or specific promises
[ ] Proposal follows the correct structure — greeting, intro, 5 bullets max, portfolio links, dynamic CTA, closing
[ ] 3 Upwork job highlights added (highest rated)
[ ] Proposal reviewed for typos, AI-sounding language, and placeholder text before submitting
[ ] Proposal added to the shared Google Doc and BJ approval received (training period only)
[ ] Proposal submitted on Upwork
[ ] Submission logged in the Upwork Proposal Tracker

description:
TIMESHEEET OVERVIEW
This SOP outlines the weekly process of validating individual chatter timesheets, cross-referencing them with Slack reports, and consolidating verified work hours into the master YUM Hours sheet. This ensures accurate and timely payroll tracking for Emily’s OnlyFans team.
TASK
Verify and update each chatter’s weekly working hours and meeting attendance by cross-checking individual logs with Slack activity and compiling results in the YUM Hours sheet. Final submission is due every Thursday by 7:00 AM PST.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Individual Chatter Timesheets 
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Chatters - Yum Hours - Google Sheets
YUM Hours Master Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Yum Hours - Google Sheets
YUM Slack – For verifying login/logout times
Fathom / Meeting Notes – For verifying meeting attendance
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Access Chatter Timesheets
Open each chatter’s individual Google Sheet
Review login/out times, shift durations, and coverage notes (if any)
 
STEP 2: Cross-Reference with Slack Logs (Reports Channel) 
Use Slack reports (via Dali’s view or direct access)
Match timesheet entries with actual timestamps
Adjust for:
Early outs
Missed shifts
No logout reports
 
STEP 3: Check for Shift Coverage
If a chatter covered another shift, ensure it’s reflected both in their sheet and in Slack
Log any missing notes accordingly
 
STEP 4: Follow the Weekly Cut-Off
Work week is Thursday to Wednesday (PHT)
Complete validation by Wednesday night PHT
 
STEP 5: Update the YUM Hours Sheet
Open the YUM Hours master sheet
For each chatter:
Copy validated total hours
Add +1 hour for Monday night meeting attendance if:
They attended and were not on shift during the meeting
Skip the +1 if:
They were absent
They were already on shift
 
STEP 6: Double Check Everything
Ensure hours match verified Slack logs
Confirm all formulas and summaries are calculating properly
 
STEP 7: Submit by Deadline
Finalize the YUM Hours sheet by Thursday, 7:00 AM PHT
 
IMPORTANT NOTES
Slack is the main source of truth — always verify against it
Some sheets may show default entries (e.g., 84 hrs); don’t rely on these
Only add the meeting +1 hour if confirmed via Fathom or meeting log
Double check chatters with perfect sheets (e.g., Jay, Ian) for consistency
Keep coverage shifts updated in the shared schedule
Do not share access to the YUM Hours sheet with chatters
Check attendance for Monday meetings 
 Verify via recording or Slack updates 
Pay Computation
 Adjust hours first 
 Multiply hours × rate = base pay 
Incentives
Top Chatter:
 Top 1 → $75 
 Top 2 → $50 
Resub & Transfer Bonus:
 $10–$19 → $40 
 $20+ → $100 
Top Chatter Computation
 Based on audit report (Monday–Sunday data) 
Adjustment:
 6-day worker (Xaviera) → divide earnings by 6 
 Others → divide by 5

TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)
FansMetric (FM) – For verifying chatter conversations and fan movement
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Open the Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).
The fan's name was updated and matched in VIP. 
The fan has been "Already in PAID/VIP"
If any of the above criteria is missed, mark as Invalid. 

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

Resub Cases
 Fan explicitly resubscribed 
 Previous VIP → stopped → re-engaged via message/MM 
 Check Billing info to verify if the fan actually resubscribed 
MM Checking
 Use MM Tracker to identify sender 
 Since MM has no chatter name, always cross-check 
Interaction Rule
 Any chatter can interact 
 Credit goes to: 
 Last MM sender 
 Source of resub/transfer 
Invalid Cases
 Username not found / inactive 
 No interaction (buried or no reply) 
 No clear MM or chat basis 
STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 5: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

title: Vault Maintenance
description:
Vault Maintenance SOP
Recurring Frequency
 Weekly or as needed when new content is uploaded
Deadline
 No fixed deadline unless assigned as part of a time-sensitive content update
🎯 Overview
This task ensures the OF vault is properly maintained so all content is organized, searchable, correctly priced, and placed in the right folders. Vault maintenance includes sorting new content, updating old content, checking price folders, applying descriptive categories, and cleaning up unnecessary or duplicate folders. New content uploaded into OF first lands in All Media and must then be sorted into the correct folder system. 
When there is no new content, vault maintenance still continues as a review and cleanup process by checking whether all existing content has the correct pricing, descriptive categories, and quarterly folder placement. 
✅ Task
Maintain Emily’s OF vault by:
 sorting newly uploaded content into the proper folders 
 assigning the correct price folder 
 applying descriptive category tags 
 moving content based on age 
 checking old content for missing or incorrect folder placement 
 cleaning up unnecessary or duplicate folders to keep the vault organized   
🛠 Tools Required
 OnlyFans Vault 
 All Media section in OF 
 Model Info Sheet 
 ClickUp 
 Slack vault maintenance thread 
 Google Drive, if new content is first stored there before being uploaded to OF  
📋 Step-by-Step Process
1️⃣ Open the Vault and Check All Media
Go to Emily’s OF Vault and open All Media.
All newly uploaded or newly dropped content appears in All Media first. This is the starting point for vault maintenance. Any new content found here must be sorted into the proper folders. 
2️⃣ Sort New Content Into the Correct Folder Set
If the content is newly uploaded for the week, it must be added to all applicable folders:
New Content
 the correct Quarterly Folder
 the correct descriptive category folder
Use the circle selector on the media item, then click the folder icon to assign the content to the proper categories. New weekly content should always be placed in all required folders, not left only in All Media. 
3️⃣ Create the Correct Quarterly Folder if Missing
Check whether the correct quarterly folder already exists.
If a new quarter has started and the folder does not yet exist, create a new quarterly folder using the proper naming structure. Example: if the current quarter is April to June 2026, create the corresponding quarterly folder before sorting content into it. 
4️⃣ Apply the Correct Price Folder
After sorting the content into New Content and the correct Quarterly Folder, assign the proper price folder.
Current process requires that even newly uploaded content must already be assigned to a price folder. Pricing must not be guessed. Always cross-check against the Model Info Sheet first before applying the correct vault price. 
5️⃣ Check the Model Info Sheet for Original Pricing
Open the Model Info Sheet and identify:
 content type 
 content duration, if video 
 applicable base/original price 
Use the Model Info Sheet as the source of truth for original pricing. Vault pricing is then applied based on the current pricing rule, content type, and age of the content. 
6️⃣ Price Videos Based on Type, Duration, and Age
For videos, determine:
 the content type 
 the content duration 
 the original price from the Model Info Sheet 
Vault pricing is based on the generic lowest applicable tier. If the content is already 6 months old, apply the 6–6 rule and reduce the original price by 50%. Example: if the original low-tier price is $50, the updated vault price becomes $25 once the content is 6 months old. 
For older video content, the price shown in the vault should reflect the updated discounted folder, not the original full price. 
7️⃣ Price Photos Using the Standard Folder Guide
For older photo content, use the following standard folder guide:
 boob only or butt only = $5
 boob and butt visible = $10
 pussy visible only = $10
 full nude with pussy visible = $15
Also assess image quality:
 If the content is very old or pixelated, lower the price when appropriate. 
 If the content quality is especially strong, the folder price may be justified at a higher tier within the existing rule set.  
8️⃣ Apply Descriptive Category Tags
Add the content to the proper descriptive category folders based on what appears in the content.
A single piece of content may have multiple descriptive tags if applicable. For example, if a video includes more than one content element, it may be tagged in more than one descriptive category. However, it must only have one final price folder and remain properly sorted by date. 
9️⃣ Move Content Based on Age
Content must be moved through the temporary folders based on age:
Week 1: place in New Content
After 1 week: move to Last Week New Content
After 2 weeks: remove from Last Week New Content
 after that, keep it in its proper Quarterly Folder only  
This keeps the “new” folders accurate and prevents old content from staying in short-term folders too long.
🔟 Maintain the Vault Even When There Is No New Content
If there is no new content uploaded, continue vault maintenance by auditing older content.
Check that all existing content has:
 a price folder 
 descriptive category tags 
 correct quarterly placement  
This applies especially to older videos, since videos usually require closer review to confirm category and pricing. 
1️⃣1️⃣ Clean Up Unnecessary or Incorrect Categories
Part of vault maintenance is cleanup.
If a category is unnecessary, one-off, duplicated, or no longer useful:
 rename it if needed 
 move content into the proper permanent folder 
 delete the extra category if no longer needed 
This prevents the vault from becoming too cluttered and makes it easier for chatters to find content. 
1️⃣2️⃣ Update Internal Notes or Task Records if Needed
If there are major changes made during vault maintenance, update the relevant SOP, ClickUp task, or internal tracking notes as needed so the folder logic and pricing rules remain clear for the team. 
⚠️ Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
1. Never guess pricing
Always use the Model Info Sheet first, especially for videos. Pricing must be based on the documented pricing structure, then adjusted according to current vault rules. 
2. Use the generic lowest pricing tier for vault pricing
Vault pricing should be based on the lowest applicable tier for the generic vault system. Do not apply different vault prices based on individual fan spender tiers. 
3. Multiple descriptive tags are allowed, but only one price folder
A content item can belong to multiple descriptive folders, but it must not be assigned to multiple price folders. 
4. Videos require more review than photos
Videos may need to be watched or reviewed more carefully to determine correct duration, category, and pricing. 
5. Quality affects photo pricing
For photos, use the standard folder rules, but consider whether the content is old, pixelated, or especially high quality before finalizing the folder price. 
6. Vault maintenance still applies even without new content
If no new content has been uploaded, the task becomes a maintenance audit of existing content rather than a new-content sorting task. 
7. Keep the vault clean and easy to use
Too many unnecessary folders make content harder to manage and sell. Regular cleanup is part of the task.

STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).
The fan's name was updated and matched in VIP. 
The fan has been "Already in PAID/VIP"
If any of the above criteria is missed, mark as Invalid. 

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

Resub Cases
 Fan explicitly resubscribed 
 Previous VIP → stopped → re-engaged via message/MM 
 Check Billing info to verify if the fan actually resubscribed 
MM Checking
 Use MM Tracker to identify sender 
 Since MM has no chatter name, always cross-check 
Interaction Rule
 Any chatter can interact 
 Credit goes to: 
 Last MM sender 
 Source of resub/transfer 
Invalid Cases
 Username not found / inactive 
 No interaction (buried or no reply) 
 No clear MM or chat basis 
STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 5: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

title: Payroll Computation
description:
✅ Overview
This SOP explains the step-by-step process for computing payroll for YUM chatters. The goal is to make sure each chatter’s pay is calculated accurately based on verified hours, approved hourly rate, and qualified bonuses.
Payroll must always be based on checked and confirmed data from the official trackers. Do not guess or manually estimate any hours, rates, or bonuses.

✅ Task
Compute each chatter’s payroll by checking their verified working hours, calculating base pay, adding approved bonuses, and confirming the final total pay before submission or review.

✅ Tools Required
☐ ClickUp
☐ Chatters - Yum Hours Google Sheet
☐ VIP Top Chatters / Bonus Tracker
☐ Model’s Info Sheet
☐ Resub / Transfer Tracker
☐ KPI / Bonus Structure Tracker
☐ Calculator, if needed
☐ Slack, for confirmation or reporting

✅ Payroll Computation Checklist
1. Confirm the payroll period
Before starting the computation, make sure you are working on the correct payroll date or pay period.
☐ Check the payroll coverage date
☐ Confirm the correct week or cutoff period
☐ Make sure the ClickUp payroll table matches the same payroll period
☐ Do not start computation if the date or week is unclear

2. Open the payroll table in ClickUp
Go to ClickUp and open the correct payroll task, page, or table.
Check that the table includes the following columns:
☐ Name
☐ Rate
☐ Hours
☐ Base Pay
☐ Top Chatter Bonus
☐ Resub / Transfer Bonus
☐ KPI Bonus
☐ Total Pay
Make sure all active chatters for the payroll period are included in the table.

3. Check each chatter’s hourly rate
Review the Rate column for each chatter.
☐ Confirm that the hourly rate is already listed
☐ Do not change the rate unless there is an approved update
☐ If the rate is missing, ask for confirmation before computing
☐ If the rate looks incorrect, flag it before proceeding
Important: Never update a chatter’s rate based on memory. Always wait for confirmation from the manager or approved tracker.

4. Get verified working hours
Open the Chatters - Yum Hours Google Sheet.
Go to the correct weekly hours tab or checked hours section.
For each chatter:
☐ Locate the chatter’s name
☐ Check the correct payroll week
☐ Use the checked or verified total hours only
☐ Include approved overtime only if clearly noted
☐ Do not include unapproved or unclear hours
Copy the verified total hours into the Hours column in ClickUp.
Important: Use verified hours only. Do not use scheduled hours if they are not confirmed.

5. Calculate base pay
Compute each chatter’s base pay using this formula:
Base Pay = Hourly Rate x Verified Hours
Example:
Rate: $5.00
Verified Hours: 41
Base Pay: $205.00
Enter the result in the Base Pay column.
Checklist:
☐ Rate is correct
☐ Hours are verified
☐ Base pay calculation is accurate
☐ Amount is entered in the correct row

6. Check Top Chatter Bonus
Open the VIP Top Chatters or Bonus Tracker.
Go to the correct payweek or bonus section.
Check if the chatter qualified for a top chatter bonus.
Current bonus structure:
☐ Top 1 = $75
☐ Top 2 = $50
Enter the correct amount in the Top Chatter Bonus column.
If the chatter did not qualify, enter a dash or leave it blank based on the current payroll format.
Important: Only add this bonus if the chatter is clearly listed as qualified in the tracker.

7. Check Resub / Transfer Bonus
Open the Model’s Info Sheet or Resub / Transfer Tracker.
Review the entries within the payroll period.
For each chatter:
☐ Check if they have valid resub or transfer entries
☐ Confirm that the entries are within the correct date range
☐ Include only approved or validated entries
☐ Exclude pending, duplicate, unclear, or unapproved entries
Enter the approved amount in the Resub / Transfer Bonus column.
If there is no qualified bonus, enter a dash.

8. Check KPI Bonus
Open the KPI or Bonus Structure Tracker.
Check if each chatter qualified for a KPI bonus during the payroll period.
☐ Confirm the chatter’s KPI result
☐ Check if the bonus is approved
☐ Enter the correct KPI bonus amount
☐ Enter a dash if they did not qualify
Important: Do not add a KPI bonus unless it is confirmed in the tracker or approved by management.

9. Calculate total pay
Compute the final total pay using this formula:
Total Pay = Base Pay + Top Chatter Bonus + Resub / Transfer Bonus + KPI Bonus
Treat blank cells or dashes as zero.
Example:
Base Pay: $205.00
Top Chatter Bonus: $75.00
Resub / Transfer Bonus: $40.00
KPI Bonus: $0.00
Total Pay: $320.00
Enter the final amount in the Total Pay column.
Checklist:
☐ Base pay is added
☐ Top chatter bonus is added, if applicable
☐ Resub / transfer bonus is added, if applicable
☐ KPI bonus is added, if applicable
☐ Final total is correct

10. Compute team subtotal, if applicable
If the payroll table has a subtotal or team total row, compute the total for the full team.
☐ Add all chatter hours
☐ Add all base pay amounts
☐ Add all bonuses
☐ Add all final total pay amounts
☐ Make sure the subtotal matches the individual rows
Do not submit the payroll if the team total does not match the row-by-row computation.

11. Final payroll review
Before submitting or marking the payroll as ready, review everything one more time.
Final review checklist:
☐ Payroll period is correct
☐ All active chatters are included
☐ Removed or inactive chatters are not included unless they worked during the period
☐ Hourly rates are correct
☐ Hours match the verified Yum Hours sheet
☐ Base pay is calculated correctly
☐ Bonuses are added only when approved
☐ Dashes or blanks are treated as zero
☐ Total pay is accurate
☐ Team subtotal is accurate
☐ Any unclear item is flagged before submission

12. Submit for review
Once all payroll details are complete and checked:
☐ Update the ClickUp payroll table
☐ Mark the payroll task as ready for review, if applicable
☐ Notify the manager or payroll reviewer in Slack
☐ Mention any flagged items that need confirmation
Sample update:
Payroll computation is complete and ready for review. I also flagged the rows that need confirmation before final approval.

⚠️ Important Notes / Tips / Warnings
☐ Always use checked or verified hours only.
☐ Do not use scheduled hours unless they are confirmed.
☐ Do not guess missing hours, bonuses, or rates.
☐ Do not edit hourly rates unless there is an approved update.
☐ Only include overtime if it is clearly approved.
☐ Only include bonuses that are confirmed in the trackers.
☐ Always check the correct payroll period before computing.
☐ Review all totals before submitting.
☐ If anything is unclear, flag it first instead of assuming.
☐ Payroll errors can affect payout accuracy, so double-check every row carefully.

title: Update Yum GPT — Weekly and As Needed
description:
Task: Update Yum GPT — Weekly and As Needed
Description:
 MJ is responsible for keeping the Yum GPT up to date so it always reflects the most current information, scripts, tone guidelines, and pricing rules the chatter team relies on. The GPT should be treated as a living document — updated every week and immediately whenever something important changes.
When to Update:
Every week as part of your regular routine
Immediately when any of the following change: 
Fan engagement tone or messaging guidelines
Pricing rules, tiers, or SOP
Content types and how they are priced
Emily's custom info, schedule, or pickup lines
Chatter training materials
Any instructions from management
Step-by-Step: How to Update the Yum GPT
Step 1 — Log in to ChatGPT
Go to chat.openai.com
Log in using the Yum Productions shared account credentials
Step 2 — Open the Yum GPT
Look for "YUM Productions GPT" in the Pinned section on the left sidebar
Click the dropdown arrow next to the name
Select "Edit GPT" from the dropdown menu
Step 3 — Click Configure
Once the GPT Builder opens, click on the "Configure" tab at the top
This is where all the instructions, knowledge files, and settings live
Do not click "Create" — always go to "Configure" when updating
Step 4 — Identify What Needs to Be Updated
There are two areas you may need to update:
A. Instructions (text inside the GPT)
 This includes:
Fan engagement tone and formatting rules
Engagement guidelines (e.g. how to handle priority fans/HVMs)
Pricing guidance logic and rules
Missing info responses and unlisted content type responses
Any general behavior or response rules
To update: scroll to the Instructions box and edit the text directly. Be careful not to delete existing rules unless confirmed outdated.
B. Knowledge Files (uploaded documents)
 These are the files currently uploaded:
Model's Info Sheet — Emily's Custom & Live Schedule + Pickup Lines (PDF) — 3 versions uploaded
Copy of Chatters Training (PDF)
YUM GPT Master Reference (Document)
YUM Pricing Guide and 6-6 Rules (Document)
To update a knowledge file:
Click the X on the outdated file to remove it
Click "Upload files" to upload the new version
Always remove the old version first before uploading the new one to avoid confusion
Step 5 — Test Before Saving
Use the preview panel on the right side to test the update
Test fan engagement: paste a sample fan message and check the GPT responds in Emily's voice with the 3 tone variations correctly
Test pricing: ask the GPT to price a custom without giving full info — it should ask for missing details, not guess
If anything is off, go back and fix before saving
Step 6 — Save the Changes
Once satisfied, click "Update" to save
Changes go live immediately for all chatters using the GPT
Step 7 — Log the Update in ClickUp
Log what was updated, the date, and the reason
Tag Yvonne Legazpi, Divine and RA so they are aware of the changes
Completion Standard:
The Yum GPT is updated every week without needing to be reminded. Any important change is reflected in the GPT by the end of that same week. All updates are logged in ClickUp and Yvonne is notified.

title: Audit Report
description:
OBJECTIVE
To accurately generate weekly audit reports for OnlyFans accounts, ensuring all data is updated, and necessary details and screenshots are included.
PREREQUISITES
Access Requirements:
FansMetric (FM) account login credentials.
Access to info@divineorigines.com.
Access to the Reports folder in Google Drive: Google Drive Reports Folder.
Timing:
Run the report after 12:00 AM (Monday, EST).
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Log in to FansMetric (FM)
Open the FansMetric platform.
Use the credentials for divine.origines@gmail.com to log in.
STEP 2: Access the Latest Report
Open the Google Drive Reports Folder.
Locate the most recent report file.
Make a copy of the file to avoid overwriting the original.
STEP 3: Update Dates
Open the copied report in Google Slides.
Update the date range in the report title and on the first page. Use the reporting period of the past week (Monday to Sunday).
STEP 4: Populate Key Data
Total Followers:
Extract the Paid Account and Free Account follower count data from FansMetric.
Include the weekly change (e.g., +218 or -202).
Follow the same steps for both accounts.

Weekly Sales (Paid and Free Accounts):
Navigate to the Sales Metrics section in FansMetric.

Scroll down and include Chatter Performance Report screenshots. 
Total Sales:
Add Net Sales and Gross Sales data.
Match the font color if there's a decrease or increase from last week's sales. 

Popular Content:
Identify the top-performing posts and PPV (Pay-Per-View) messages based on metrics such as purchases, views, and likes.
MOST POPULAR WALL POST: Engagement > Posts > Views
MOST SOLD PPV: Engagement > Messages > Purchase 
TOP FANS: Fans > Top Fans
STATEMENTS (FREE ONLY): Statements
STEP 5: Add Screenshots
Take screenshots directly from FansMetric for the following sections:
Follower counts (Paid and Free accounts).
Weekly Sales data.
Total Sales charts.
Popular posts and PPV messages (including engagement metrics).
Ensure screenshots are clear and relevant. Position them neatly within the report slides.
STEP 6: Verify and Save
Double-check the report for accuracy and completeness.
Ensure all updated dates, screenshots, and data match the weekly reporting period.
Save the file with a naming convention like:
Audit_Report_[DateRange]
STEP 7: Submit the Report
Save the updated report in the designated Google Drive folder.
Notify the team via project management tool (e.g., ClickUp and Slack).
BEST PRACTICES
Always use the previous report as a reference to maintain consistency in layout and data presentation.
Ensure data integrity by cross-checking all figures with FansMetric.
Submit the report no later than Monday 5 PM (PHT).

Confirm if there’s new content uploaded
If no new content, navigate to the Used Wall (PAID) or Used Wall (FREE) and reuse old photos by downloading them and then uploading into the NEW folders
Content can be reused for wall posts after at least 2 weeks since it was last posted

STEP 2: FILL OUT THE CAPTION TRACKER
2.1. Open the OF Caption Tracker via the YUM Production bookmarks.
2.2. Under the appropriate monthly tab, input:
Date and Time
Category (e.g. Daily Post, Drop - Photo, Drop - Video)
Account (Free or VIP)
Caption: Captions can be copy-pasted from other OF models from Emily's feed (short, one-liner captions). Alternatively, you can use ChatGPT to generate short, one-liner captions that are bubbly/playful/flirty and fits the content being posted. 
Note: for fake drops (2x a week), we need to add an additional line of caption such as "New video drops tonight!" or "Shot some fresh nudes, dropping tonight!". Alternate between video and nude set for fake drops. No specific days of the week, only 2 days per week. 
Additional Note: Confirm weekly with Divine if fake drops are continuing or if the model plans on dropping new content
Asset Link (Drive link to content)

STEP 3: GET APPROVAL
3.1. Notify Jerold once the tracker is complete.
3.2. Wait for the review and approval before scheduling.

STEP 4: SCHEDULING IN FANSMETRIC
4.1. After access is granted, go to Fansmetric > Queue > Add Post

 4.2. Upload the asset, paste the caption, and choose publish time.
Be mindful that FM time is based on your computer time and post must be scheduled in EST (adjust if needed). Schedule at 10:00 PM PHT daily (10 AM EST)

Scheduled (after posting in Fansmetric)
Published (after confirming it went live properly)
4.4. Move the content to Used (Wall Post) folder in Google Drive

6.1. Use Fansmetric > Statistics > Posts to:
 - Identify best post times
 - Review top-performing captions for style inspiration

Avoid robotic captions — always match caption tone with the content vibe
Strictly avoid banned words per OnlyFans policy (e.g., "young", "teen", "child")
Free account: Used for soft teasing, directing fans to VIP
VIP account: Full access + PPV drops
PPV drops require extra payment, even for VIP subscribers
Live Show Promotion: Promote lives via wall posts if there are scheduled lives, always confirm with Divine.

title: Vault Maintenance
description:
Vault Maintenance SOP
Recurring Frequency
 Weekly or as needed when new content is uploaded
Deadline
 No fixed deadline unless assigned as part of a time-sensitive content update
🎯 Overview
This task ensures the OF vault is properly maintained so all content is organized, searchable, correctly priced, and placed in the right folders. Vault maintenance includes sorting new content, updating old content, checking price folders, applying descriptive categories, and cleaning up unnecessary or duplicate folders. New content uploaded into OF first lands in All Media and must then be sorted into the correct folder system. 
When there is no new content, vault maintenance still continues as a review and cleanup process by checking whether all existing content has the correct pricing, descriptive categories, and quarterly folder placement. 
✅ Task
Maintain Emily’s OF vault by:
 sorting newly uploaded content into the proper folders 
 assigning the correct price folder 
 applying descriptive category tags 
 moving content based on age 
 checking old content for missing or incorrect folder placement 
 cleaning up unnecessary or duplicate folders to keep the vault organized   
🛠 Tools Required
 OnlyFans Vault 
 All Media section in OF 
 Model Info Sheet 
 ClickUp 
 Slack vault maintenance thread 
 Google Drive, if new content is first stored there before being uploaded to OF  
📋 Step-by-Step Process
1️⃣ Open the Vault and Check All Media
Go to Emily’s OF Vault and open All Media.
All newly uploaded or newly dropped content appears in All Media first. This is the starting point for vault maintenance. Any new content found here must be sorted into the proper folders. 
2️⃣ Sort New Content Into the Correct Folder Set
If the content is newly uploaded for the week, it must be added to all applicable folders:
New Content
 the correct Quarterly Folder
 the correct descriptive category folder
Use the circle selector on the media item, then click the folder icon to assign the content to the proper categories. New weekly content should always be placed in all required folders, not left only in All Media. 
3️⃣ Create the Correct Quarterly Folder if Missing
Check whether the correct quarterly folder already exists.
If a new quarter has started and the folder does not yet exist, create a new quarterly folder using the proper naming structure. Example: if the current quarter is April to June 2026, create the corresponding quarterly folder before sorting content into it. 
4️⃣ Apply the Correct Price Folder
After sorting the content into New Content and the correct Quarterly Folder, assign the proper price folder.
Current process requires that even newly uploaded content must already be assigned to a price folder. Pricing must not be guessed. Always cross-check against the Model Info Sheet first before applying the correct vault price. 
5️⃣ Check the Model Info Sheet for Original Pricing
Open the Model Info Sheet and identify:
 content type 
 content duration, if video 
 applicable base/original price 
Use the Model Info Sheet as the source of truth for original pricing. Vault pricing is then applied based on the current pricing rule, content type, and age of the content. 
6️⃣ Price Videos Based on Type, Duration, and Age
For videos, determine:
 the content type 
 the content duration 
 the original price from the Model Info Sheet 
Vault pricing is based on the generic lowest applicable tier. If the content is already 6 months old, apply the 6–6 rule and reduce the original price by 50%. Example: if the original low-tier price is $50, the updated vault price becomes $25 once the content is 6 months old. 
For older video content, the price shown in the vault should reflect the updated discounted folder, not the original full price. 
7️⃣ Price Photos Using the Standard Folder Guide
For older photo content, use the following standard folder guide:
 boob only or butt only = $5
 boob and butt visible = $10
 pussy visible only = $10
 full nude with pussy visible = $15
Also assess image quality:
 If the content is very old or pixelated, lower the price when appropriate. 
 If the content quality is especially strong, the folder price may be justified at a higher tier within the existing rule set.  
8️⃣ Apply Descriptive Category Tags
Add the content to the proper descriptive category folders based on what appears in the content.
A single piece of content may have multiple descriptive tags if applicable. For example, if a video includes more than one content element, it may be tagged in more than one descriptive category. However, it must only have one final price folder and remain properly sorted by date. 
9️⃣ Move Content Based on Age
Content must be moved through the temporary folders based on age:
Week 1: place in New Content
After 1 week: move to Last Week New Content
After 2 weeks: remove from Last Week New Content
 after that, keep it in its proper Quarterly Folder only  
This keeps the “new” folders accurate and prevents old content from staying in short-term folders too long.
🔟 Maintain the Vault Even When There Is No New Content
If there is no new content uploaded, continue vault maintenance by auditing older content.
Check that all existing content has:
 a price folder 
 descriptive category tags 
 correct quarterly placement  
This applies especially to older videos, since videos usually require closer review to confirm category and pricing. 
1️⃣1️⃣ Clean Up Unnecessary or Incorrect Categories
Part of vault maintenance is cleanup.
If a category is unnecessary, one-off, duplicated, or no longer useful:
 rename it if needed 
 move content into the proper permanent folder 
 delete the extra category if no longer needed 
This prevents the vault from becoming too cluttered and makes it easier for chatters to find content.

If no new content has been uploaded, the task becomes a maintenance audit of existing content rather than a new-content sorting task.

Too many unnecessary folders make content harder to manage and sell. Regular cleanup is part of the task.

TASK
Verify and update each chatter’s weekly working hours and meeting attendance by cross-checking individual logs with Slack activity and compiling results in the YUM Hours sheet. Final submission is due every Thursday by 7:00 AM PST.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Individual Chatter Timesheets 
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Chatters - Yum Hours - Google Sheets

Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Yum Hours - Google Sheets

 Adjust hours first

TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)
FansMetric (FM) – For verifying chatter conversations and fan movement
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Open the Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).
The fan's name was updated and matched in VIP. 
The fan has been "Already in PAID/VIP"
If any of the above criteria is missed, mark as Invalid. 

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

Resub Cases
 Fan explicitly resubscribed 
 Previous VIP → stopped → re-engaged via message/MM 
 Check Billing info to verify if the fan actually resubscribed 
MM Checking
 Use MM Tracker to identify sender 
 Since MM has no chatter name, always cross-check 
Interaction Rule
 Any chatter can interact 
 Credit goes to: 
 Last MM sender 
 Source of resub/transfer 
Invalid Cases
 Username not found / inactive 
 No interaction (buried or no reply) 
 No clear MM or chat basis 
STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 5: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

title: AOM set-up
description:
OVERVIEW
Automated Online Messages (AOMs) are short, engaging one-liners sent to fans when they log in. These messages are designed to reflect Emily’s personality and encourage chat engagement across both VIP (Paid) and Free OnlyFans accounts.
TASK
Create one-liner AOMs per day to be used across:
VIP (Paid) Account (2 AOMs daily)
Free Account (2 AOMs daily)
These AOMs should drive engagement and feel natural, even if a fan receives all on the same day.
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Create the AOMs
Use ChatGPT to help write the AOMs.
Tone must match Emily’s brand: bubbly, sexy/flirty, and playful.
Keep messages short, natural, one-liner, and conversational
Avoid endearments (e.g., babe, hun, baby).
STEP 2: Schedule the AOMs in Fansmetric
VIP (Paid) Account
Schedule the 2 AOMs 
Starts 10:00 PM PHT (current day) Ends 10:00 PM PHT (next day)
Starts 11:50 PM PHT (current day) Ends 10:00 PM PHT (next day)
To: Fans
Exclude: Muted, Whales, Boyfriend VIP, Exclude from PPV/MM
Add 3 Preview Photos weekly to any AOM in the Paid Account by navigating to: Chatting Client > Automations > Auto Online Messages (select AOM, edit message, add media)
Free Account
Schedule 2 AOMs
Starts 10:00 PM PHT (current day) Ends 10:00 PM PHT (next day)
Starts 11:50 PM PHT (current day) Ends 10:00 PM PHT (next day)
To: Fans
Exclude: Muted, Already in Paid, Exclude from PPV/MM
 
NOTES
Always prioritize the VIP account first before scheduling for the Free account.
Watch out for weekly manager meeting updates, as AOM strategies may be reviewed or changed.

title: Payroll Computation
description:
✅ Overview
This SOP explains the step-by-step process for computing payroll for YUM chatters. The goal is to make sure each chatter’s pay is calculated accurately based on verified hours, approved hourly rate, and qualified bonuses.
Payroll must always be based on checked and confirmed data from the official trackers. Do not guess or manually estimate any hours, rates, or bonuses.

✅ Task
Compute each chatter’s payroll by checking their verified working hours, calculating base pay, adding approved bonuses, and confirming the final total pay before submission or review.

✅ Tools Required
☐ ClickUp
☐ Chatters - Yum Hours Google Sheet
☐ VIP Top Chatters / Bonus Tracker
☐ Model’s Info Sheet
☐ Resub / Transfer Tracker
☐ KPI / Bonus Structure Tracker
☐ Calculator, if needed
☐ Slack, for confirmation or reporting

✅ Payroll Computation Checklist
1. Confirm the payroll period
Before starting the computation, make sure you are working on the correct payroll date or pay period.
☐ Check the payroll coverage date
☐ Confirm the correct week or cutoff period
☐ Make sure the ClickUp payroll table matches the same payroll period
☐ Do not start computation if the date or week is unclear

2. Open the payroll table in ClickUp
Go to ClickUp and open the correct payroll task, page, or table.
Check that the table includes the following columns:
☐ Name
☐ Rate
☐ Hours
☐ Base Pay
☐ Top Chatter Bonus
☐ Resub / Transfer Bonus
☐ KPI Bonus
☐ Total Pay
Make sure all active chatters for the payroll period are included in the table.

3. Check each chatter’s hourly rate
Review the Rate column for each chatter.
☐ Confirm that the hourly rate is already listed
☐ Do not change the rate unless there is an approved update
☐ If the rate is missing, ask for confirmation before computing
☐ If the rate looks incorrect, flag it before proceeding
Important: Never update a chatter’s rate based on memory. Always wait for confirmation from the manager or approved tracker.

4. Get verified working hours
Open the Chatters - Yum Hours Google Sheet.
Go to the correct weekly hours tab or checked hours section.
For each chatter:
☐ Locate the chatter’s name
☐ Check the correct payroll week
☐ Use the checked or verified total hours only
☐ Include approved overtime only if clearly noted
☐ Do not include unapproved or unclear hours
Copy the verified total hours into the Hours column in ClickUp.
Important: Use verified hours only. Do not use scheduled hours if they are not confirmed.

5. Calculate base pay
Compute each chatter’s base pay using this formula:
Base Pay = Hourly Rate x Verified Hours
Example:
Rate: $5.00
Verified Hours: 41
Base Pay: $205.00
Enter the result in the Base Pay column.
Checklist:
☐ Rate is correct
☐ Hours are verified
☐ Base pay calculation is accurate
☐ Amount is entered in the correct row

6. Check Top Chatter Bonus
Open the VIP Top Chatters or Bonus Tracker.
Go to the correct payweek or bonus section.
Check if the chatter qualified for a top chatter bonus.
Current bonus structure:
☐ Top 1 = $75
☐ Top 2 = $50
Enter the correct amount in the Top Chatter Bonus column.
If the chatter did not qualify, enter a dash or leave it blank based on the current payroll format.
Important: Only add this bonus if the chatter is clearly listed as qualified in the tracker.

7. Check Resub / Transfer Bonus
Open the Model’s Info Sheet or Resub / Transfer Tracker.
Review the entries within the payroll period.
For each chatter:
☐ Check if they have valid resub or transfer entries
☐ Confirm that the entries are within the correct date range
☐ Include only approved or validated entries
☐ Exclude pending, duplicate, unclear, or unapproved entries
Enter the approved amount in the Resub / Transfer Bonus column.
If there is no qualified bonus, enter a dash.

8. Check KPI Bonus
Open the KPI or Bonus Structure Tracker.
Check if each chatter qualified for a KPI bonus during the payroll period.
☐ Confirm the chatter’s KPI result
☐ Check if the bonus is approved
☐ Enter the correct KPI bonus amount
☐ Enter a dash if they did not qualify
Important: Do not add a KPI bonus unless it is confirmed in the tracker or approved by management.

9. Calculate total pay
Compute the final total pay using this formula:
Total Pay = Base Pay + Top Chatter Bonus + Resub / Transfer Bonus + KPI Bonus
Treat blank cells or dashes as zero.
Example:
Base Pay: $205.00
Top Chatter Bonus: $75.00
Resub / Transfer Bonus: $40.00
KPI Bonus: $0.00
Total Pay: $320.00
Enter the final amount in the Total Pay column.
Checklist:
☐ Base pay is added
☐ Top chatter bonus is added, if applicable
☐ Resub / transfer bonus is added, if applicable
☐ KPI bonus is added, if applicable
☐ Final total is correct

10. Compute team subtotal, if applicable
If the payroll table has a subtotal or team total row, compute the total for the full team.
☐ Add all chatter hours
☐ Add all base pay amounts
☐ Add all bonuses
☐ Add all final total pay amounts
☐ Make sure the subtotal matches the individual rows
Do not submit the payroll if the team total does not match the row-by-row computation.

11. Final payroll review
Before submitting or marking the payroll as ready, review everything one more time.
Final review checklist:
☐ Payroll period is correct
☐ All active chatters are included
☐ Removed or inactive chatters are not included unless they worked during the period
☐ Hourly rates are correct
☐ Hours match the verified Yum Hours sheet
☐ Base pay is calculated correctly
☐ Bonuses are added only when approved
☐ Dashes or blanks are treated as zero
☐ Total pay is accurate
☐ Team subtotal is accurate
☐ Any unclear item is flagged before submission

12. Submit for review
Once all payroll details are complete and checked:
☐ Update the ClickUp payroll table
☐ Mark the payroll task as ready for review, if applicable
☐ Notify the manager or payroll reviewer in Slack
☐ Mention any flagged items that need confirmation
Sample update:
Payroll computation is complete and ready for review. I also flagged the rows that need confirmation before final approval.

⚠️ Important Notes / Tips / Warnings
☐ Always use checked or verified hours only.
☐ Do not use scheduled hours unless they are confirmed.
☐ Do not guess missing hours, bonuses, or rates.
☐ Do not edit hourly rates unless there is an approved update.
☐ Only include overtime if it is clearly approved.
☐ Only include bonuses that are confirmed in the trackers.
☐ Always check the correct payroll period before computing.
☐ Review all totals before submitting.
☐ If anything is unclear, flag it first instead of assuming.
☐ Payroll errors can affect payout accuracy, so double-check every row carefully.

Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)
FansMetric (FM) – For verifying chatter conversations and fan movement
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Open the Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).
The fan's name was updated and matched in VIP. 
The fan has been "Already in PAID/VIP"
If any of the above criteria is missed, mark as Invalid. 

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7)

 Fan explicitly resubscribed 
 Previous VIP → stopped → re-engaged via message/MM

 Any chatter can interact

 Username not found / inactive
