title: Timesheet & Resub/Transfer
description:
TIMESHEEET OVERVIEW
This SOP outlines the weekly process of validating individual chatter timesheets, cross-referencing them with Slack reports, and consolidating verified work hours into the master YUM Hours sheet. This ensures accurate and timely payroll tracking for Emily’s OnlyFans team.
TASK
Verify and update each chatter’s weekly working hours and meeting attendance by cross-checking individual logs with Slack activity and compiling results in the YUM Hours sheet. Final submission is due every Thursday by 7:00 AM PST.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Individual Chatter Timesheets 
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Chatters - Yum Hours - Google Sheets
YUM Hours Master Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Yum Hours - Google Sheets
YUM Slack – For verifying login/logout times
Fathom / Meeting Notes – For verifying meeting attendance
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Access Chatter Timesheets
Open each chatter’s individual Google Sheet
Review login/out times, shift durations, and coverage notes (if any)
 
STEP 2: Cross-Reference with Slack Logs (Reports Channel) 
Use Slack reports (via Dali’s view or direct access)
Match timesheet entries with actual timestamps
Adjust for:
Early outs
Missed shifts
No logout reports
 
STEP 3: Check for Shift Coverage
If a chatter covered another shift, ensure it’s reflected both in their sheet and in Slack
Log any missing notes accordingly
 
STEP 4: Follow the Weekly Cut-Off
Work week is Thursday to Wednesday (PST)
Complete validation by Wednesday night PST
 
STEP 5: Update the YUM Hours Sheet
Open the YUM Hours master sheet
For each chatter:
Copy validated total hours
Add +1 hour for Monday night meeting attendance if:
They attended and were not on shift during the meeting
Skip the +1 if:
They were absent
They were already on shift
 
STEP 6: Double Check Everything
Ensure hours match verified Slack logs
Confirm all formulas and summaries are calculating properly
 
STEP 7: Submit by Deadline
Finalize the YUM Hours sheet by Thursday, 7:00 AM PST
 
IMPORTANT NOTES
Slack is the main source of truth — always verify against it
Some sheets may show default entries (e.g., 84 hrs); don’t rely on these
Only add the meeting +1 hour if confirmed via Fathom or meeting log
Double check chatters with perfect sheets (e.g., Jay, Ian) for consistency
Keep coverage shifts updated in the shared schedule
Expect high standards from Irwin (OM) and audits if errors occur
Do not share access to the YUM Hours sheet with chatters
 
 
TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)
FansMetric (FM) – For verifying chatter conversations and fan movement
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Open the Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 4: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

title: Wall Post & Content Drops Scheduling

7 Free posts

Asset Link (Drive link to content)

TASK
To create and schedule 1 daily story post for both Free and VIP accounts, alternating with and without captions. Ensure posts align with strategy (Free posts directing fans to VIP, VIP posts teasing sexier upsell) and are tracked for reference and consistency.
PREREQUISITE
OnlyFans (Free and VIP accounts)
Google Sheets – OF Captions Tracker
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > OF Caption Tracker - Google Sheets
Slack – YUM Channel (for advising chatters)
Vault – Photo Previews Folder (for story content)
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Choose Content from Vault
Go to the Vault > Photo Previews folder
Select 1 image for Free and 1 for VIP story post
Ensure sexier or nude version of the content is indeed available in either quarterly or priced folder. 
 
STEP 2: Determine Caption Plan for the Day
Access OF Captions Tracker and Filter to Story Post in Column D 
Follow the alternate rule:
Day 1: With Caption
Day 2: No Caption
Day 3: With Caption
(and so on)
 
STEP 3: Write Captions
For Free Story Post:
Caption must encourage fans to join VIP (e.g., “Want the uncensored version? Join my VIP @emjaybird 💋”)
For VIP Story Post:
Caption must encourage tipping to unlock the sexier version
Example: “Wanna see how this ends? Tip $15 and I’ll send you the uncut version 😘🔥”
 
STEP 4: Advise Chatters
Once VIP caption is finalized, notify chatters in the YUM Slack channel
Indicate what “sexier version” to send when a fan tips (e.g., name of content in vault or linked preview set)
 
STEP 5: Schedule the Story Posts
Log in to OnlyFans Free account and schedule the Free story for 8:00 AM PHT
Log in to OnlyFans VIP account and do the same
Upload the selected media and add caption (or leave blank per alternation schedule)
Vault > Add to > Add to your story

 
STEP 6: Final Check
Ensure both stories are scheduled correctly for 8:00 AM PHT
Confirm captions are accurate and properly logged
Make sure chatters are tagged in Slack with the upsell content info
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Follow the caption alternation rule strictly to maintain story engagement variety
Never reuse the same story image and caption combo within the same week
Captions for Free must always point to VIP and feel teasing, not spammy
VIP captions should sound playful and enticing, encouraging interaction (e.g., tipping)
Notify chatters promptly if upsell content is changed or unavailable
Maintain consistency in posting time — always schedule for 8:00 AM PHT

PPVMM for VIP Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $40-$55, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Whales

Leave a space for # of Purchases (to update daily)

Send to Fans, then exclude:
Muted
Tagged
Whales
Exclude from PPVMM

$25–$35 for premium videos or larger photo bundles

Google Sheets

Early outs
Missed shifts
No logout reports

Log any missing notes accordingly
 
STEP 4: Follow the Weekly Cut-Off
Work week is Thursday to Wednesday (PST)
Complete validation by Wednesday night PST
 
STEP 5: Update the YUM Hours Sheet
Open the YUM Hours master sheet
For each chatter:
Copy validated total hours
Add +1 hour for Monday night meeting attendance if:
They attended and were not on shift during the meeting
Skip the +1 if:
They were absent
They were already on shift
 
STEP 6: Double Check Everything
Ensure hours match verified Slack logs
Confirm all formulas and summaries are calculating properly
 
STEP 7: Submit by Deadline
Finalize the YUM Hours sheet by Thursday, 7:00 AM PST
 
IMPORTANT NOTES
Slack is the main source of truth — always verify against it
Some sheets may show default entries (e.g., 84 hrs); don’t rely on these
Only add the meeting +1 hour if confirmed via Fathom or meeting log
Double check chatters with perfect sheets (e.g., Jay, Ian) for consistency
Keep coverage shifts updated in the shared schedule
Expect high standards from Irwin (OM) and audits if errors occur
Do not share access to the YUM Hours sheet with chatters
 
 
TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)

INSTRUCTIONS

Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 4: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

description:

PPVMM for Free Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $5-15, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Already on VIP
PPVMM for VIP Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $40-$55, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Whales
MM for Free Account - Twice a week for current VIP promos (benefits) and discount link
 
PREREQUISITE
FansMetric (FM) – For scheduling, accessing the vault, and analytics
PPVMM Tracker (ClickUp Docs) – To log captions, dates, prices, purchase counts (in EST)
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > [NEW] PPVMM Tracker | PPV MM Results
Heatmap (FM > Analytics) – To determine peak times for scheduling
Vault Content Folders in FM – For selecting content ($5–$100 folders)
ChatGPT – For rewording or generating fresh captions
Slack / Thread Notification – To inform Divine/Marj that the tracker is ready for review
INSTRUCTIONS 
STEP 1: PREPARE CONTENT & CAPTIONS
1.1. Log in to FansMetric (FM) and go to the Vault.
1.2. Browse folders priced $5–$100, but select content for PPVMMs within the $15–$35 price range.
Prioritize older content first.
For videos, pair with a preview photo if the clip is short.
For photosets, group related images (e.g. 3–4 pics as a bundle).
1.3. Use ChatGPT or former captions n the PPVMM Tracker for reference.
Captions should be seductive, enticing, and not robotic.
Focus on teasing, sensory cues, emotional pull and make it all about the fan.
Highlight power/tease words and ensure to have CTA phrases. 
 
STEP 2: UPDATE TRACKER IN CLICKUP
 2.1 Access the PPVMM Tracker under the YUM workspace in ClickUp.
 2.2. For each PPVMM scheduled:
Add Date & Time (in EST)
Paste Caption
Include Price ($40-$55)
Add Vault folder name or screenshot of the original upload date (to prevent repeats)
Leave a space for # of Purchases (to update daily)
2.3. Notify in the PPVMM Setup thread once the tracker is ready for review and approval.
STEP 3: SCHEDULE IN FANSMETRIC (PH TIME)
 3.1. After approval, go to FM > Messages > Mass Message (+).
 3.2. Set recipient group:
Send to Fans, then exclude:
Muted
Tagged
Whales
Exclude from PPVMM
3.3. Schedule the post:
Use PH time (local system time) based on FM heatmap
Use heatmap from FM analytics (PH timezone) to pick peak hour
3.4. Upload Media: Select content from the vault
3.5. Set Price ($15–$35)
3.6. Paste Caption
3.7. Save the message. Confirm it appears in the Queue (orange color).
 



STEP 4: TRACK PERFORMANCE DAILY
 4.1. Once scheduled, return to the tracker and change status as “Scheduled”
 4.2. Every morning, check FM > Message Stats
Note number of Purchases per PPVMM
Update tracker accordingly (skip reach/view count)
Adjust future strategies based on performance
IMPORTANT NOTES
Vault Folder Selection: Always start with older content to avoid repetition
Pricing Strategy:
$15–$20 for short videos or small photo sets
$25–$35 for premium videos or larger photo bundles
PH Time for Scheduling: Always schedule based on your local PH time. Tracker must still log time in EST.
Heatmap Guidance: Blue zones in FM analytics show peak purchase windows
Content Preview Rules: Avoid showing full nudity in preview images
Drops ≠ PPVMMs:
Drops are announced on the wall and redeemed via DM
PPVMMs are direct, unlockable messages sent to the fan inbox
Do not open chat messages in FM — this risks exposing sensitive data
Caption Tone: Prioritize personality, flirtation, and sensory buildup. Avoid robotic or repetitive lines
Approval Required: All scheduled PPVMMs must be reviewed before publishing
PPVMM Limit: 1 per day (scheduled by you). Chatters may send their own separately — ignore these in your planning.

Missed shifts
No logout reports

Work week is Thursday to Wednesday (PST)

Open the YUM Hours master sheet

They attended and were not on shift during the meeting

Confirm all formulas and summaries are calculating properly

IMPORTANT NOTES

Some sheets may show default entries (e.g., 84 hrs); don’t rely on these
Only add the meeting +1 hour if confirmed via Fathom or meeting log
Double check chatters with perfect sheets (e.g., Jay, Ian) for consistency
Keep coverage shifts updated in the shared schedule
Expect high standards from Irwin (OM) and audits if errors occur
Do not share access to the YUM Hours sheet with chatters
 
 
TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)
FansMetric (FM) – For verifying chatter conversations and fan movement
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Open the Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 4: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.

STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 4: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.

Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.

Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

Early outs
Missed shifts
No logout reports

Work week is Thursday to Wednesday (PST)

They attended and were not on shift during the meeting
Skip the +1 if:
They were absent
They were already on shift

Ensure hours match verified Slack logs
Confirm all formulas and summaries are calculating properly

TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.

Google Sheets

Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)

INSTRUCTIONS

Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).

Things to consider: 
a. FM is on PHT, but transfer must be counted in EST 
b. Cross reference the time fan resubscribe/transfer and the chatter's schedule in EST (For example: Welcome message is 1PM Sep 8 in FM, falls within the chatter's schedule of Sep 7 6AM - 2PM then it will be counted to Sep 7) 
c. If cannot identify the exact time, you can count it on the original message chatter sent 
d. If off, then add it to the previous shift

Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell.

Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.

Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.

Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

title: PPV MM ClickUp Tracker
description:
TASK
Create and schedule one PPVMM & MMs for VIP and Free account using selected content from the FM vault. Write persuasive, on-brand captions, update the tracker in EST, and align the schedule with peak engagement hours based on Fansmetric heatmap data.
 
PPVMM for Free Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $5-15, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Already on VIP
PPVMM for VIP Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $40-$55, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Whales
MM for Free Account - Twice a week for current VIP promos (benefits) and discount link
 
PREREQUISITE
FansMetric (FM) – For scheduling, accessing the vault, and analytics
PPVMM Tracker (ClickUp Docs) – To log captions, dates, prices, purchase counts (in EST)
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > [NEW] PPVMM Tracker | PPV MM Results
Heatmap (FM > Analytics) – To determine peak times for scheduling
Vault Content Folders in FM – For selecting content ($5–$100 folders)
ChatGPT – For rewording or generating fresh captions
Slack / Thread Notification – To inform Divine/Marj that the tracker is ready for review
INSTRUCTIONS 
STEP 1: PREPARE CONTENT & CAPTIONS
1.1. Log in to FansMetric (FM) and go to the Vault.
1.2. Browse folders priced $5–$100, but select content for PPVMMs within the $15–$35 price range.
Prioritize older content first.
For videos, pair with a preview photo if the clip is short.
For photosets, group related images (e.g. 3–4 pics as a bundle).
1.3. Use ChatGPT or former captions n the PPVMM Tracker for reference.
Captions should be seductive, enticing, and not robotic.
Focus on teasing, sensory cues, emotional pull and make it all about the fan.
Highlight power/tease words and ensure to have CTA phrases. 
 
STEP 2: UPDATE TRACKER IN CLICKUP
 2.1 Access the PPVMM Tracker under the YUM workspace in ClickUp.
 2.2. For each PPVMM scheduled:
Add Date & Time (in EST)
Paste Caption
Include Price ($40-$55)
Add Vault folder name or screenshot of the original upload date (to prevent repeats)
Leave a space for # of Purchases (to update daily)
2.3. Notify in the PPVMM Setup thread once the tracker is ready for review and approval.
STEP 3: SCHEDULE IN FANSMETRIC (PH TIME)
 3.1. After approval, go to FM > Messages > Mass Message (+).
 3.2. Set recipient group:
Send to Fans, then exclude:
Muted
Tagged
Whales
Exclude from PPVMM
3.3. Schedule the post:
Use PH time (local system time) based on FM heatmap
Use heatmap from FM analytics (PH timezone) to pick peak hour
3.4. Upload Media: Select content from the vault
3.5. Set Price ($15–$35)
3.6. Paste Caption
3.7. Save the message. Confirm it appears in the Queue (orange color).
 



STEP 4: TRACK PERFORMANCE DAILY
 4.1. Once scheduled, return to the tracker and change status as “Scheduled”
 4.2. Every morning, check FM > Message Stats
Note number of Purchases per PPVMM
Update tracker accordingly (skip reach/view count)
Adjust future strategies based on performance
IMPORTANT NOTES
Vault Folder Selection: Always start with older content to avoid repetition
Pricing Strategy:
$15–$20 for short videos or small photo sets
$25–$35 for premium videos or larger photo bundles
PH Time for Scheduling: Always schedule based on your local PH time. Tracker must still log time in EST.
Heatmap Guidance: Blue zones in FM analytics show peak purchase windows
Content Preview Rules: Avoid showing full nudity in preview images
Drops ≠ PPVMMs:
Drops are announced on the wall and redeemed via DM
PPVMMs are direct, unlockable messages sent to the fan inbox
Do not open chat messages in FM — this risks exposing sensitive data
Caption Tone: Prioritize personality, flirtation, and sensory buildup. Avoid robotic or repetitive lines
Approval Required: All scheduled PPVMMs must be reviewed before publishing
PPVMM Limit: 1 per day (scheduled by you). Chatters may send their own separately — ignore these in your planning.

title: Story Post
description:
OVERVIEW
This SOP outlines the daily process for posting story content on both Free and VIP OnlyFans accounts. The purpose is to engage fans consistently, promote VIP subscriptions, and encourage tipping through teasers and upsells—while ensuring all activity is tracked and aligned with content guidelines.
TASK
To create and schedule 1 daily story post for both Free and VIP accounts, alternating with and without captions. Ensure posts align with strategy (Free posts directing fans to VIP, VIP posts teasing sexier upsell) and are tracked for reference and consistency.
PREREQUISITE
OnlyFans (Free and VIP accounts)
Google Sheets – OF Captions Tracker
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > OF Caption Tracker - Google Sheets
Slack – YUM Channel (for advising chatters)
Vault – Photo Previews Folder (for story content)
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Choose Content from Vault
Go to the Vault > Photo Previews folder
Select 1 image for Free and 1 for VIP story post
Ensure sexier or nude version of the content is indeed available in either quarterly or priced folder. 
 
STEP 2: Determine Caption Plan for the Day
Access OF Captions Tracker and Filter to Story Post in Column D 
Follow the alternate rule:
Day 1: With Caption
Day 2: No Caption
Day 3: With Caption
(and so on)
 
STEP 3: Write Captions
For Free Story Post:
Caption must encourage fans to join VIP (e.g., “Want the uncensored version? Join my VIP @emjaybird 💋”)
For VIP Story Post:
Caption must encourage tipping to unlock the sexier version
Example: “Wanna see how this ends? Tip $15 and I’ll send you the uncut version 😘🔥”
 
STEP 4: Advise Chatters
Once VIP caption is finalized, notify chatters in the YUM Slack channel
Indicate what “sexier version” to send when a fan tips (e.g., name of content in vault or linked preview set)
 
STEP 5: Schedule the Story Posts
Log in to OnlyFans Free account and schedule the Free story for 8:00 AM PHT
Log in to OnlyFans VIP account and do the same
Upload the selected media and add caption (or leave blank per alternation schedule)
Vault > Add to > Add to your story

 
STEP 6: Final Check
Ensure both stories are scheduled correctly for 8:00 AM PHT
Confirm captions are accurate and properly logged
Make sure chatters are tagged in Slack with the upsell content info
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Follow the caption alternation rule strictly to maintain story engagement variety
Never reuse the same story image and caption combo within the same week
Captions for Free must always point to VIP and feel teasing, not spammy
VIP captions should sound playful and enticing, encouraging interaction (e.g., tipping)
Notify chatters promptly if upsell content is changed or unavailable
Maintain consistency in posting time — always schedule for 8:00 AM PHT

title: Timesheet & Resub/Transfer
description:
TIMESHEEET OVERVIEW
This SOP outlines the weekly process of validating individual chatter timesheets, cross-referencing them with Slack reports, and consolidating verified work hours into the master YUM Hours sheet. This ensures accurate and timely payroll tracking for Emily’s OnlyFans team.
TASK
Verify and update each chatter’s weekly working hours and meeting attendance by cross-checking individual logs with Slack activity and compiling results in the YUM Hours sheet. Final submission is due every Thursday by 7:00 AM PST.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Individual Chatter Timesheets 
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Chatters - Yum Hours - Google Sheets
YUM Hours Master Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Yum Hours - Google Sheets
YUM Slack – For verifying login/logout times
Fathom / Meeting Notes – For verifying meeting attendance
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Access Chatter Timesheets
Open each chatter’s individual Google Sheet
Review login/out times, shift durations, and coverage notes (if any)
 
STEP 2: Cross-Reference with Slack Logs (Reports Channel) 
Use Slack reports (via Dali’s view or direct access)
Match timesheet entries with actual timestamps
Adjust for:
Early outs
Missed shifts
No logout reports
 
STEP 3: Check for Shift Coverage
If a chatter covered another shift, ensure it’s reflected both in their sheet and in Slack
Log any missing notes accordingly
 
STEP 4: Follow the Weekly Cut-Off
Work week is Thursday to Wednesday (PST)
Complete validation by Wednesday night PST
 
STEP 5: Update the YUM Hours Sheet
Open the YUM Hours master sheet
For each chatter:
Copy validated total hours
Add +1 hour for Monday night meeting attendance if:
They attended and were not on shift during the meeting
Skip the +1 if:
They were absent
They were already on shift
 
STEP 6: Double Check Everything
Ensure hours match verified Slack logs
Confirm all formulas and summaries are calculating properly
 
STEP 7: Submit by Deadline
Finalize the YUM Hours sheet by Thursday, 7:00 AM PST

IMPORTANT NOTES
Slack is the main source of truth — always verify against it
Some sheets may show default entries (e.g., 84 hrs); don’t rely on these
Only add the meeting +1 hour if confirmed via Fathom or meeting log
Double check chatters with perfect sheets (e.g., Jay, Ian) for consistency
Keep coverage shifts updated in the shared schedule
Expect high standards from Irwin (OM) and audits if errors occur
Do not share access to the YUM Hours sheet with chatters


TRANSFER/RESUB VALIDATION OVERVIEW
Chatters are eligible for a $40 bonus if they achieve 10 successful conversions (Free to VIP transfers, or Resubscriptions) within a single day. This SOP ensures each claimed transfer or resub is properly validated before bonuses are granted.
TASK
To review and validate each conversion or resubmission logged by chatters, ensuring accuracy and legitimacy before confirming bonus eligibility.
PREREQUISITE
Google Sheets
Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > Model's Info Sheet (Fans Transfer & Resub tab)
FansMetric (FM) – For verifying chatter conversations and fan movement
INSTRUCTIONS
STEP 1: Open the Transfer/Resub Logging Sheet
Locate the entries submitted by chatters for the specific day being validated.
 
STEP 2: Access FansMetric (FM)
Log in and navigate to the chatter's message history for the fan listed in the log.
 
STEP 3: Verify the Conversion or Resub
Confirm that:
The chatter engaged in conversation with the fan.
There was resubscription spiel and should not be longer than a week before the resub date.
The fan either subscribed or resubscribed on that day (based on system tag or subscription change).
STEP 4: Mark as Validated
Once confirmed, indicate the entry as validated in your personal notes. If invalid add it as a comment in the cell. 
STEP 4: Repeat for All Entries
Validate each of the claimed conversions/resubs until all are reviewed.
Important Notes, Tips, or Warnings
Only direct conversions/resubs should be counted—do not credit transfers that occurred without chatter involvement.
Be cautious of duplicates, missing account and automatic renewal that may disqualify the bonus.
Fans who subbed without prior engagement or due to automated messages should not be counted.
Maintain validation records to support bonus payouts and dispute resolutions if needed.
Consistency and fairness in validation are key to preserving motivation and trust among chatters.

title: PPV MM ClickUp Tracker
description:
TASK
Create and schedule one PPVMM & MMs for VIP and Free account using selected content from the FM vault. Write persuasive, on-brand captions, update the tracker in EST, and align the schedule with peak engagement hours based on Fansmetric heatmap data.
 
PPVMM for Free Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $5-15, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Already on VIP
PPVMM for VIP Account - Daily at 5AM PHT, priced between $40-$55, Sent to: Fans, Excluded: Muted, Tagged, Exclude from PPVMM, Whales
MM for Free Account - Twice a week for current VIP promos (benefits) and discount link
 
PREREQUISITE
FansMetric (FM) – For scheduling, accessing the vault, and analytics
PPVMM Tracker (ClickUp Docs) – To log captions, dates, prices, purchase counts (in EST)
Info Chrome > YUM folder in Bookmarks > [NEW] PPVMM Tracker | PPV MM Results
Heatmap (FM > Analytics) – To determine peak times for scheduling
Vault Content Folders in FM – For selecting content ($5–$100 folders)
ChatGPT – For rewording or generating fresh captions
Slack / Thread Notification – To inform Divine/Marj that the tracker is ready for review
INSTRUCTIONS 
STEP 1: PREPARE CONTENT & CAPTIONS
1.1. Log in to FansMetric (FM) and go to the Vault.
1.2. Browse folders priced $5–$100, but select content for PPVMMs within the $15–$35 price range.
Prioritize older content first.
For videos, pair with a preview photo if the clip is short.
For photosets, group related images (e.g. 3–4 pics as a bundle).
1.3. Use ChatGPT or former captions n the PPVMM Tracker for reference.
Captions should be seductive, enticing, and not robotic.
Focus on teasing, sensory cues, emotional pull and make it all about the fan.
Highlight power/tease words and ensure to have CTA phrases. 
 
STEP 2: UPDATE TRACKER IN CLICKUP
 2.1 Access the PPVMM Tracker under the YUM workspace in ClickUp.
 2.2. For each PPVMM scheduled:
Add Date & Time (in EST)
Paste Caption
Include Price ($40-$55)
Add Vault folder name or screenshot of the original upload date (to prevent repeats)
Leave a space for # of Purchases (to update daily)
2.3. Notify in the PPVMM Setup thread once the tracker is ready for review and approval.
STEP 3: SCHEDULE IN FANSMETRIC (PH TIME)
 3.1. After approval, go to FM > Messages > Mass Message (+).
 3.2. Set recipient group:
Send to Fans, then exclude:
Muted
Tagged
Whales
Exclude from PPVMM
3.3. Schedule the post:
Use PH time (local system time) based on FM heatmap
Use heatmap from FM analytics (PH timezone) to pick peak hour
3.4. Upload Media: Select content from the vault
3.5. Set Price ($15–$35)
3.6. Paste Caption
3.7. Save the message. Confirm it appears in the Queue (orange color).
 



STEP 4: TRACK PERFORMANCE DAILY
 4.1. Once scheduled, return to the tracker and change status as “Scheduled”
 4.2. Every morning, check FM > Message Stats
Note number of Purchases per PPVMM
Update tracker accordingly (skip reach/view count)
Adjust future strategies based on performance
IMPORTANT NOTES
Vault Folder Selection: Always start with older content to avoid repetition
Pricing Strategy:
$15–$20 for short videos or small photo sets
$25–$35 for premium videos or larger photo bundles
PH Time for Scheduling: Always schedule based on your local PH time. Tracker must still log time in EST.
Heatmap Guidance: Blue zones in FM analytics show peak purchase windows
Content Preview Rules: Avoid showing full nudity in preview images
Drops ≠ PPVMMs:
Drops are announced on the wall and redeemed via DM
PPVMMs are direct, unlockable messages sent to the fan inbox
Do not open chat messages in FM — this risks exposing sensitive data
Caption Tone: Prioritize personality, flirtation, and sensory buildup. Avoid robotic or repetitive lines
Approval Required: All scheduled PPVMMs must be reviewed before publishing
PPVMM Limit: 1 per day (scheduled by you). Chatters may send their own separately — ignore these in your planning.

Strict single-tenant isolation for delivery specialists. Universal authority for Divine, Radz, and RA. Zero cross-client data drift enforced across API routes and frontend state.

• Enforced user_metadata.clientScope.
• Supabase RLS and server-side client isolation.

title: [GIM-ARCH-07] Dynamic Specialist Views Bar per Client
description:
Real-time specialist tabs matching ClickUp: InVogue (Erwin's, Jedy's, Ellyka's), Juvibolt (Divine's, Radz's, Kim's), WRTS (Erwin's, BJ's, Aldwin's), NoirLab, Risewise, Studio Nets.

• Clicking a specialist filters to that member's tasks.
• Knowledge Hub doc tab, List view, Board view, Table view, Calendar view.

title: [GIM-ARCH-06] ClickUp Status Accordion Groups & Hex Codes
description:
1:1 ClickUp status accordions (TO DO #87909E, IN PROGRESS #5F55EE, FOR REVIEW #F8AE00, BLOCKED #D33D44, CLOSED #008844) with subtask counters, priority flags, tag chips, and comments count.

• Collapsible status headers matching ClickUp 1:1
• Subtask count badges (2, 4, 7)
• Tag chips and time tracking indicators

title: [GIM-ARCH-05] Full REA Audit & 6-Tier ClickUp Reverse-Engineering
description:
Extracted all 7 spaces, 48 lists, 50 docs, and 20 verified members. Built master reverse-engineering blueprint in GIM_CLICKUP_REVERSE_ENGINEERING_MASTER_PLAN.md.

• Workspace: Grace In Motion (9016642965)
• 6-tier architecture mapped: Workspace -> Space -> Folder -> List -> Task -> Subtask

title: [GIM-SPRINT-09] Client Knowledge Hub Document Search & Filter
description:
Interactive section search and keyword filter across client knowledge documents and SOP checklists.

• In-page keyword search highlighting.
• Quick filter by SOP category (Operations, Billing, Delivery, AI).

title: [GIM-SPRINT-08] Knowledge Hub Prompt One-Click Copy Engine
description:
One-click formatted context extraction for copying client SOPs into external AI tools and subagent briefings.

• Copies full prompt with client guardrails, tones, and restrictions.
• Visual checkmark confirmation on copy.

title: [GIM-SPRINT-07] Client Dossier & Retainer Milestone Tracker
description:
Live monthly retainer, active sprint focus, and milestone velocity tracking across active clients.

• InVogue Cleans: USD $1,700/mo (55% progress)
• Juvibolt Cybertech: USD $3,200/mo (70% progress)
• WRTS: USD $4,500/mo (80% progress)
• NoirLab: USD $2,500/mo (60% progress)
• Studio Nets: USD $2,800/mo (60% progress)
• Risewise: USD $2,200/mo (65% progress)

title: [GIM-SPRINT-06] Multi-Client Real-Time Global Timezone Engine
description:
Live timezone clocks for Texas (CST UTC-6), California (PST UTC-8), Australia (AEST UTC+10), and UK (GMT). Enables the team to see client local time instantly to avoid out-of-hours messages.

• Displays city, offset, and live pulsing clock.
• Integrated into Client Portfolio Dossier.

title: [GIM-SPRINT-05] 13-Section AI Knowledge Hub & Evidence Vault
description:
Standardized 13-section operational framework per client:
1. Company Overview
2. Communication Cadence
3. Key Tech Stack
4. Brand Identity & Style Tokens
5. Client Portals & Logins Vault
6. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
7. AI Bot Profile & Guardrails
8. Quality Assurance & Sign-off Gates
9. Escalation Matrix
10. File Vault & Shared Assets
11. Deliverable Milestone Archive
12. Retainer & Billing Structure
13. Client Contact Directory

title: [GIM-SPRINT-14] Task Comment Threading & Feed Activity Persistence
description:
Direct modal comment entry with persistence to Supabase task_comments and ClickUp activity logs.

• Modal loads comments from ClickUp API.
• Allows specialist to post handover notes.

title: [GIM-SPRINT-13] Task Quick-Status Movement & Audio Chimes Persistence
description:
Seamless status transitions updating Supabase client_tasks with audio chimes (sound.playSuccessChime()).

• Checkbox click advances task to Closed with success chime.
• Syncs state across dashboard views.

title: [GIM-SPRINT-12] Real-time Messaging Delivery Verification & Online Indicator
description:
Live presence indicators and typing indicators across #general-gim, #ops-delivery, and client rooms.

• Green dot online indicators for active leadership and specialists.
• Sound chime on incoming message receive.

title: [GIM-SPRINT-11] Dual-Pane Operational Task & Messaging Split View
description:
Side-by-side execution view: Tasks & Delivery Pipeline on left, Real-Time Messaging on right. Tested in Nov 13 team call.

• Enables team members to chat while viewing sprint deliverables.
• Exit Dual View button for focused layout.

title: [GIM-SPRINT-10] PostgreSQL Schema Fix for Real-time Messaging
description:
Stripped unsupported reply_to column on insert; resolved HTTP 500 error on /api/messages. Messages now post immediately and format timestamps on retrieval.

• Schema sanitization in src/app/api/messages/route.ts
• Live verification passed: inserted test message and purged cleanly.

title: [GIM-ROADMAP-05] Automated Specialist Timesheet & Capacity Rollups
description:
Weekly capacity and time-tracking aggregation per specialist for billing reconciliations with RA.

• Total hours per specialist per client.
• Exportable summary for invoice matching.

title: [GIM-ROADMAP-04] AI Copilot Contextual Routing to Knowledge Hubs
description:
Routing GIM Copilot inquiries directly to client SOPs and AI bot profiles (Ivy, Jarvis, Neo, Riva, Rocky, Gianna).

• Auto-injects client Knowledge Hub section 1-13 context into LLM prompt.
• Provides instant answers to client SOP questions without manual searching.

title: [GIM-ROADMAP-03] Two-Way ClickUp Direct Write-Back Engine
description:

title: [GIM-ROADMAP-02] Automated Slack Notification Webhook Engine
description:
Automated webhook dispatch to #gim-sprint-alerts whenever tasks are assigned, moved to for review, or blocked.

• Incoming webhook URL configuration in .env.local.
• Formatted Slack blocks with Task Title, Assignee, Client, and direct link.

title: Erwin Manaog — Head of Strategy & Operations
Recruitment: Ads Specialist for StudioNets
description:
Ads Specialist (Meta + TikTok)
We're hiring an Ads Specialist to plan, launch, and optimize paid campaigns across Meta (Facebook & Instagram) and TikTok. You need to be hands-on with both platforms, not just one.

Schedule: Must be available to work morning EST hours (US Eastern Time).
What you'll do
Build, launch, and manage paid campaigns on Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads Manager
Set up audiences, targeting, budgets, and bidding strategies
Run A/B tests on creatives, copy, and audiences
Monitor daily performance and optimize for ROAS, CPA, and CTR
Set up and troubleshoot tracking (Meta Pixel, Conversions API, TikTok Pixel, UTMs)
Work with the creative team on ad concepts, hooks, and briefs
Send clear weekly performance reports with insights and next steps
Must-haves
Proven experience running ads on both Meta and TikTok
Solid grasp of funnels, retargeting, and scaling winning campaigns
Comfortable with analytics and reporting
Strong English communication skills
Available during morning EST hours
Reliable internet and a quiet work setup
Nice-to-haves
Experience with creative strategy or UGC-style ads
Familiarity with Google Analytics or Looker Studio
Agency or e-commerce background
How to apply
Send your resume, a short summary of your Meta and TikTok ad experience, and sample results or case studies (spend managed, ROAS, CPA, etc.).

title: Last Warning
description:
Date: September 10, 2026
Issue: Repeat communication issue — logging in late without notifying the team beforehand, not checking all urgent tasks, and not prioritizing what needs to be done first
This is Cybil's last warning due to a repeat communication issue. She has been logging in late without notifying the team beforehand, and has not been checking all tasks assigned to her or prioritizing urgent work first, despite her tasks being well delegated.
Adjustment made: Cybil's work hours have shifted to 7:00 AM to 11:00 AM PHT. She is required to message the team in the channel when she logs in and logs off, and to check all assigned tasks and read the SOPs thoroughly.
Why this matters: Her teammates have their own work schedules and end up covering for her when she is MIA, which puts the account at risk of churn, an account the team has worked hard to retain and grow.
Consequence of no improvement: If any further performance issue is observed, she may be offboarded. There is no reason for this pattern to continue given how well her tasks are delegated.
Expectation going forward: Real, visible improvement, log-in/log-off communication in the channel, adherence to the new schedule, and proactive notice if she cannot log in on time so the team can manage tasks and coverage ahead of time.

title: 1st Warning
description:
Cybil was not able to complete her assigned tasks within the expected timeline. The root cause was not a lack of ability or unclear instructions, but her resistance to communicating with the team. When blockers, delays, or questions came up, she did not raise them, respond to check-ins, or flag that she needed help, which left tasks incomplete and unmonitored until it became a problem.
Expectations going forward:
Respond to team check-ins and messages within the agreed response time.
Proactively flag any blocker, delay, or uncertainty as soon as it comes up, rather than staying silent.
Complete assigned tasks on time, or communicate in advance if a deadline is at risk.

title: 1st Warning
description:
1st Warning
Issue Summary
Janz arrived 30 minutes late to his shift after incorrectly converting his schedule from EST to PHT himself, resulting in him believing his shift started at 9PM instead of the correct 6PM PHT. While the timezone conversion error originated from Janz, the underlying issue is that Yvonne does not yet have a single, clearly-owned master schedule that chatters reference directly — instead, the current schedule file was co-created and edited together with Stacy during a call, which creates room for this kind of confusion and miscommunication to happen.
Specific Instance(s)
Janz converted his own shift time from EST to PHT incorrectly, understanding his shift to start at 9PM PHT instead of the correct 6PM PHT, causing him to be 30 minutes late
The schedule file currently in use was originally drafted and edited together with Stacy (a chatter) during a live call, meaning there has not been one single, clearly Yvonne-owned source of truth for the team to reference
Expectation Not Met
 As manager, Yvonne is expected to independently own, draft, and maintain the master schedule from end to end, with all times clearly stated in PHT (or whichever timezone the team operates from) so there is no room for individual chatters to make their own conversions or interpretations. The schedule should be the single source of truth, owned and finalized by Yvonne alone.
Discussion Notes
Head of Operations acknowledged that Stacy's initiative in helping organize the schedule during the call came from a good place, but clarified that as manager, Yvonne should be the one arriving to scheduling conversations with a proposed draft already prepared — not building it together with a chatter in real time. This establishes her authority as the decision-maker, while still allowing chatters the space to flag unavailability or concerns about the proposed plan. Head of Operations also noted this approach helps chatters take the work seriously and respect Yvonne's role as manager. Yvonne acknowledged the gap and agreed she needs to stop using a shared/co-edited file and instead always present a fully-prepared draft first, removing any ambiguity that could lead to situations like Janz's timezone mix-up.
Action Plan Moving Forward
Yvonne will take full, independent ownership of the master schedule file going forward — the current shared VIP schedule (previously co-edited with Stacy) will now be hers alone to maintain and edit
Process to follow: Yvonne creates the full draft first → presents it to the team → chatters may flag unavailability or concerns → Yvonne finalizes
New Shift Check-in Protocol introduced: 
Yvonne messages each chatter approximately 1 hour before their shift, including a motivational note
Chatter is expected to reply approximately 30 minutes before their shift to confirm they are ready (a simple message or emoji is sufficient — no formal logging required)
This allows Yvonne to identify unavailability or confusion early enough to arrange shift coverage, similar to past gaps with Stacy and Vanessa's scheduling
Head of Operations will post an announcement in the Siren Slack channel with guidelines for chatters on this new check-in protocol, including reminding them to have Slack installed on their phones
Yvonne to send her current schedule copy to Head of Operations for reference
Timeline for Improvement
 Effective immediately. To be observed across the next several scheduling cycles to confirm Yvonne is independently owning the draft process and the check-in protocol is being followed consistently.
Consequence if Unresolved
 This call serves as a verbal warning. Head of Operations was explicit that this mistake should not happen again. If similar scheduling errors or lapses in independent ownership recur, this may escalate to a written warning.
Acknowledgement
Team member has been informed verbally — addressed directly during the June 30 call
Team member understands the expectation and next steps — Yvonne confirmed understanding and agreed to the new process
Reviewer/PO has been notified

VIEW RECORDING - 16 mins (No highlights)
Meeting Purpose
Review MJ's workload and address a recent ClickUp access error.
Key Takeaways
Critical Access Error: A ClickUp access error exposed confidential chatter rates to an unauthorized guest user, Aira. The mistake was caught by Yvonne before it caused a major issue.
Process Improvement: To prevent future errors, MJ must now create a ClickUp task for every action item, including a detailed description of the deliverable and its location.

Problem: MJ's incorrect ClickUp setup granted an unauthorized guest user, Aira, access to confidential chatter rates.
Discovery: The error was found when Yvonne requested help adding new chatters to the subcons list and asked which rate to use (YAM vs. Siren & Co.).

title: Project Assistant-Automation Specialist
description:
🚀 We're Looking for a Project Assistant + Automation Specialist! 📍 Remote | 🇵🇭 Philippines-based | ⏰ Mon–Fri, 6AM–3PM Manila time (AU timezone) | 📋 Subcontractor
Grace in Motion (GIM) is an Operations Management agency. We are the backend operations team for our clients — building and running the processes, systems, and automations that keep their businesses moving.
We are looking for someone who lives and breathes operations. Not a generalist. Not a social media manager. Someone who understands how processes work, knows how to document them, and can build automations that eliminate repetitive manual tasks.
The Role: Project Assistant + Automation Specialist for one of our key client accounts. You will support the daily operations of the account, manage ClickUp and trackers, help maintain SOPs, and make sure tasks and updates are moving properly.
You are the right fit if: 
✅ You have 1–2 years of experience in operations, process coordination, or operations-focused work — new freelancers with strong automation skills are welcome 
✅ You have explored or built automations before — ClickUp, Zapier, GHL, Make, Google Apps Script, or similar 
✅ You keep client and project trackers updated and accurate 
✅ You update task statuses without being reminded 
✅ You monitor communication channels for important updates or unanswered items 
✅ You flag problems before they become crises 
✅ You document what you build so others can maintain it 
✅ You understand that good operations = fewer surprises
What you will do: 
▪ Execute and track daily operations tasks in ClickUp for an assigned client account 
▪ Build, maintain, and document automations specific to that account 
▪ Follow SOPs for recurring tasks — and flag gaps where SOPs are missing 
▪ Work closely with a Project Owner and the Head of Operations
Engagement details: 
▪ This role requires someone who can take ownership. We are not looking for someone who only waits for instructions. We need someone who can understand the process, keep the system clean, follow up consistently, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks 
▪ Independent contractor (subcontractor) — not an employment arrangement. You can have other clients on the side as long as it does not overlap with GIM work hours 
▪ Remote, Philippines-based 
▪ Monday to Friday, 6:00 AM – 3:00 PM Manila time (aligned to AU Eastern Standard Time) 
▪ Note: shifts to 5:00 AM – 2:00 PM Manila time during AU Daylight Saving (October – April)
 ▪ The role is not around-the-clock execution — an efficient contractor can complete core tasks in 5–6 hours, with the remainder of the shift used for monitoring and flagging issues
To apply: Fill out our application form here 👉 https://forms.clickup.com/9016642965/f/8cpy3cn-16016/7CK3ZHFJ7IPWR3IX8C
Applications close: June 5
Know someone who fits? Tag them or share this post. We appreciate referrals! 🙌

1st Interview - Scorecard
description:
Post-Interview Scoring — Aldwin "Charles" (Executive Assistant), Sep 8

Criteria Weight Score (1–5) Notes
Commitment and availability clarity 20% 4 Currently unemployed since July, actively looking. Confirmed comfortable with 12 AM–8 AM PHT (framed it against his prior EST night-shift experience, correctly identified PST would've been a scheduling conflict but this role isn't PST). Adjusted his rate expectation from $60K to the actual $50K posted rate without pushback once clarified — a job-post discrepancy, not an inflated ask on his part.
Calendar & Scheduling Management 15% 3 No direct calendar-specific example given (unlike some other candidates), but did describe inbox and task management directly tied to protecting a CEO's time. Reasonable but less detailed than his inbox/task answers.
Tool Proficiency (calendar, CRM, task management) 15% 5 Strongest tool breadth of the candidates so far: hands-on with  ClickUp  (GIM's actual primary tool — a real advantage over other candidates), plus Slack, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Apollo, Pipedrive, DocuSign, and an HRIS platform. Notably, he independently evaluated and helped switch the company to a better HRIS platform (TalentHR) — a real, versus theoretical, tool-evaluation skill.
Execution Discipline / Prioritization 20% 5 Very concrete: prioritizes by business impact and deadline urgency, uses ClickUp specifically so nothing relies on memory. Gave two strong anticipation examples — proactively auditing unused Zoom subscriptions (saved ~$500) and researching/switching HRIS platforms (saved ~$20/month, better UX) — both self-initiated, not assigned.
Client-Facing Communication 15% 4 Solid answer on managing a missed-deadline situation: informed leadership early, explained the cause (an urgent client billing issue took priority), and proactively offered a workaround (a temporary tracking sheet) rather than just apologizing after the fact.
Confidentiality & Attention to Detail 10% 4 Managed sensitive financial/billing inboxes and CRM pipelines directly for a CEO, with a clear triage system (what he can decide himself vs. what needs to be flagged up) — shows good judgment on escalation boundaries.
Accountability and Work Ethic 5% 4 Ten years of operations experience, plus notably a Philippine Navy Reservist — explicitly ties that experience to teamwork and not quitting under difficulty. Confirmed reservist duties are weekend-only and won't conflict with work hours.
Total 100% 4.25
Minimum recommended score to proceed: 3.0 average
Proceed to skills assessment? Yes
Notes: Strongest candidate so far on tool fit specifically — actual hands-on ClickUp experience, which none of the other EA candidates had. His two self-initiated cost-saving/optimization examples (Zoom subscription audit, HRIS platform switch) show genuine proactive ownership beyond what was asked, not just reactive task completion. Also explicitly confirmed as open to the Project Assistant role as a backup if the EA seat doesn't work out — already screened and receptive, so easy to re-engage either way.

title: 1st Interview - Scorecard
description:
Post-Interview Scoring — Martha Grace German (Executive Assistant), Sep 8

Criteria Weight Score (1–5) Notes
Commitment and availability clarity 20% 4 Contract with her previous company (40 Degrees) ended July 15 — let go due to an AI-driven role reduction, not performance (they explicitly didn't want her to leave; she was the sole handler of a major platform). Confirmed open to the 12 AM–8 AM PHT schedule for the EA role. No current conflicting clients.
Calendar & Scheduling Management 20% 4 Gave a genuinely detailed example: coordinating a same-day Japan–Cebu–Japan round trip for an executive around back-to-back investor meetings, factoring in travel time and traffic unpredictability. Real complexity, not a generic answer.
Tool Proficiency (calendar, CRM, task management) 10% 3 Strong breadth — Jira, Asana, Slack,  Monday.com , Google Workspace — but no ClickUp experience at all (acknowledged directly, only researched it, never used it). Would need ramp-up time on GIM's primary tool.
Execution Discipline / Prioritization 20% 5 Standout answer: described weighing competing deadlines by urgency  and  business impact (e.g., checking whether a bug affects payments/registration before treating it as a fire drill) — a genuinely more sophisticated prioritization framework than most candidates give. Backed by real scale: led a team of ~30 across up to 10 concurrent projects.
Client-Facing Communication 15% 4 Solid, concrete example of proactive client communication when a deadline was at risk (disclose early, explain the cause, propose a path forward). Language barrier is a real, disclosed factor — she doesn't speak Japanese fluently and used DeepL to manage a Japanese executive's inbox, which worked but adds a translation-accuracy dependency worth noting for an English-speaking US-based client.
Confidentiality & Attention to Detail 10% 4 Handled inbox management with a real system (custom labels to filter noise from an executive's inbox) and cross-checked machine-translated content before acting on it — shows carefulness rather than blind trust in tools.
Accountability and Work Ethic 5% 4 Comfortable discussing a missed deadline directly, walked through her actual recovery process (inform client early, reprioritize team resources, pull in extra help, escalate to overtime when needed) rather than giving a vague answer.
Total 100% 4.05
Minimum recommended score to proceed: 3.0 average
Proceed to skills assessment? Yes
Notes: Strong operational and prioritization instincts from managing a 30-person team across multiple concurrent client projects — arguably more leadership experience than a typical EA candidate brings. Main gap is zero hands-on ClickUp experience (trainable, low risk given her fast adoption of other tools like Jira and Monday.com). She was also screened as a backup for the Project Assistant role in this same interview, given her account-management background, if she doesn't move forward for the EA seat specifically.
